records.arabic: بن عبيد بن يزيد بن قيس بن ضبيعة بن الأصرم بن جحجى بن كلفة بن عوف بن عمرو بن عوف بن مالك بن الأوس الأنصاري الأوسي ذكره البخاري في الصحابة وقال قال لي يحيى بن موسى عن يعقوب بن محمد أنبأنا إدريس بن محمد بن يونس بن محمد بن أنس الظفري حدثني جدي عن أبيه قال قدم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة وأنا بن أسبوعين فأتى بي إليه فمسح برأسي وحج بي حجة الوداع وأنا بن عشر سنين وقال دعا لي بالبركة وقال سموه باسمي ولا تكنوه بكنيتي قال يونس ولقد عمر أبي حتى شاب كل شيء منه ومات وما شاب موضع يد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من رأسه وكذا أخرجه مطين عن أبي أمية الطرطوسي وعن يعقوب بن محمد هو الزهري به واختصره بن أبي حاتم فقال محمد بن أنس بن فضالة قال قدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة وأنا بن أسبوعين وأخرجه أبو علي بن السكن مطولا من وجه آخر عن يعقوب بن محمد بهذا السند لكن قال محمد بن فضالة فنسب محمد إلى جده قال بن شاهين سمعت عبد الله بن سليمان بن الأشعث يقول محمد بن أنس بن فضالة هو الذي كان تصدق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بماله الذي كان في بني ظفر فأشار بذلك إلى ما أخرجه بن أبي داود وابن منده من طريق سفيان بن حمزة عن عمرو بن أبي فروة عن مشيخة أهل بيته قال قتل أنس بن فضالة يوم أحد فأتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بمحمد بن أنس بن فضالة فتصدق عليه بعذق لا يباع ولا يوهب الحديث قال بن منده لا يروي إلا بهذا الإسناد وقال البخاري أيضا قال أبو كامل عن فضيل بن سليمان عن يونس بن محمد عن فضالة عن أبيه وكان أبوه ممن صحب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم هو وجده إن النبي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أتاهم في بني ظفر ووصله البغوي عن أبي كامل وهو فضيل بن حسين والصلت بن مسعود كلاهما عن فضيل بن سليمان بهذا وزاد فجلس على صخرة ومعه بن مسعود ومعاذ فأمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قارئا فقرأ حتى إذا بلغ فكيف إذا جئنا من كل أمة بشهيد وجئنا بك على هؤلاء شهيدا الآية بكى حتى اضطرب لحياه وقال رب على هؤلاء شهدت فكيف بمن لم أره وهكذا أخرجه بن شاهين عن البغوي وقال قال البغوي لا أعلم روى محمد بن فضالة غير هذا الحديث وفرق البغوي وابن شاهين وابن قانع وغيرهم بين محمد بن أنس بن فضالة وبين محمد بن فضالة والراجح أنهما واحد لكن قال بن شاهين سمعت عبد الله بن سليمان يعني بن أبي داود ويقول شهد محمد بن أنس بن فضالة فتح مكة والمشاهد بعدها والله أعلم
records.english: ibn ʿUbayd ibn Yazīd ibn Qays ibn Ḍubayʿah ibn al-Aṣram ibn Jaḥjā ibn Kulfah ibn ʿAwf ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf ibn Mālik ibn al-Aws, al-Anṣārī al-Awsī and Awsī. Al-Bukhārī mentioned him among the Companions and said: Yaḥyā ibn Mūsā told me, from Yaʿqūb ibn Muḥammad: Idrīs ibn Muḥammad ibn Yūnus ibn Muḥammad ibn Anas al-Ẓafarī informed us: My grandfather related to me from his father, who said, ‘The Prophet ﷺ arrived in Medina when I was two weeks old. I was brought to him, and he stroked my head. I performed the Farewell Pilgrimage when I was ten years old.’ He said, ‘He prayed that I be blessed and said, “Name him after my name, but do not give him my kunya.”’ Yūnus said, ‘My father lived to an advanced age, until everything on him turned white, and he died, yet the place on his head touched by the Prophet’s ﷺ hand did not turn white.’ Muṭayyan likewise transmitted it from Abū Umayyah al-Ṭarṭūsī, from Yaʿqūb ibn Muḥammad—he being al-Zuhrī—with this chain. Ibn Abī Ḥātim abridged it, saying: Muḥammad ibn Anas ibn Faḍālah said, ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ arrived in Medina when I was two weeks old.’ Abū ʿAlī ibn al-Sakan transmitted it at length by another route from Yaʿqūb ibn Muḥammad with this chain, but he said ‘Muḥammad ibn Faḍālah,’ thus tracing Muḥammad’s lineage to his grandfather. Ibn Shāhīn said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sulaymān ibn al-Ashʿath say, ‘Muḥammad ibn Anas ibn Faḍālah is the one upon whom the Prophet ﷺ bestowed his property that was among Banū Ẓafar.’ By this he alluded to what Ibn Abī Dāwūd and Ibn Mandah transmitted by way of Sufyān ibn Ḥamzah, from ʿAmr ibn Abī Farwah, from the elders of his household, who said: ‘Anas ibn Faḍālah was killed on the day of Uḥud. Muḥammad ibn Anas ibn Faḍālah was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, and he bestowed upon him a date cluster that was neither to be sold nor given away’—the report. Ibn Mandah said, ‘It is narrated only with this chain.’ Al-Bukhārī also said: Abū Kāmil related from Fuḍayl ibn Sulaymān, from Yūnus ibn Muḥammad, from Faḍālah, from his father—and his father, as well as his grandfather, was among those who accompanied the Prophet ﷺ—that the Prophet, the Prophet ﷺ, came to them among Banū Ẓafar. Al-Baghawī connected it from Abū Kāmil—namely Fuḍayl ibn Ḥusayn—and from al-Ṣalt ibn Masʿūd, both from Fuḍayl ibn Sulaymān with this account, adding: ‘He sat on a rock, with Ibn Masʿūd and Muʿādh beside him. The Messenger of God ﷺ instructed a reciter, who recited until he reached the verse, “How will it be when We bring a witness from every nation and bring you as a witness against these?” He wept until his jaws trembled, and said, “My Lord, I testified concerning these; but what of those whom I did not see?”’ Ibn Shāhīn likewise transmitted it from al-Baghawī and said: Al-Baghawī said, ‘I do not know of Muḥammad ibn Faḍālah narrating anything other than this report.’ Al-Baghawī, Ibn Shāhīn, Ibn Qāniʿ, and others distinguished Muḥammad ibn Anas ibn Faḍālah from Muḥammad ibn Faḍālah. The weightier view is that they are one person. Ibn Shāhīn, however, said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sulaymān—meaning Ibn Abī Dāwūd—say, ‘Muḥammad ibn Anas ibn Faḍālah witnessed the conquest of Mecca and the expeditions thereafter.’ والله أعلم

records.arabic: بن ورقاء الخزاعي تقدم نسبه في ترجمة والده وأخرج الحديث في مقدمة تاريخه من طريق الأجلح بن عبد الله سمعت زيد بن علي وعبد الله بن حسن وجعفر بن محمد يذكر كل واحد منهم عن آبائه وعمن أدرك من أهله وغيرهم أنهم سموا له من شهد مع علي من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى أن قال وعبد الله بن بديل بن ورقاء ومحمد بن بديل بن ورقاء الخزاعيان قتلا بصفين وهما رسولا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى أهل اليمن قلت والراوي عن الأجلح غياث بن إبراهيم وهو ساقط نسب إلى وضع الحديث
records.english: ibn Warqāʾ al-Khuzāʿī. His lineage was given earlier in the notice on his father. An unnamed author transmitted the report in the introduction to his History by way of al-Ajlaḥ ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: I heard Zayd ibn ʿAlī, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥasan, and Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, each relating from his forefathers and from others among his family whom he had met, that they named for him those Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ who were present with ʿAlī. He continued until saying, ‘ʿAbd Allāh ibn Budayl ibn Warqāʾ and Muḥammad ibn Budayl ibn Warqāʾ, the two Khuzāʿīs, were killed at Ṣiffīn, and they were the two envoys of the Messenger of God ﷺ to the people of Yemen.’ I say: The transmitter from al-Ajlaḥ is Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm, who is discredited and was accused of fabricating reports.

records.english: al-Anṣārī the bāʾ vowelled i and the dotted letter quiescent—will be treated in the following notice.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بوزن عظيم الأنصاري ذكره البخاري في الصحابة وأخرج من طريق زخر بفتح الزاي وسكون المعجمة بن حصن حدثني جدي حميد بن منهب حدثني خريم بن حارثة بن لام الطائي قال اقتتلنا يوم الحرة فكان أول من تلقاني الشيماء بنت بقيلة الأزدية فتعلقت بها فقلت هذه وهبها لي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهي كما قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فدعاني خالد عليها بالبينة فأتيته بها وهي محمد بن سلمة ومحمد بن بشير الأنصاري فسلمها إلي وأخرجه بن منده بطوله من هذا الوجه وقال لا يعرف إلا بهذا الإسناد تفرد به زكريا بن يحيى عن زخر قلت وقد تقدم بطوله في ترجمة خريم بن أوس وأخرج البغوي وابن شاهين وابن يونس وابن منده من طريق سلمة بن شريح عن يحيى بن محمد بن بشير الأنصاري عن أبيه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إذا أراد الله بعبد هوانا أنفق ماله في البنيان فقال قال ولا أعلم روى محمد بن بشير غيره وأخرجه بن حبان من هذا الوجه وقال هذا مرسل وشك في صحبته بن يونس فقال يقال له صحبة وقد ذكر في أهل مصر وليس هو بالمعروف فيهم وله بمصر حديث فذكر الحديث وذكره محمد بن الربيعة الجيزي في الصحابة الذين دخلوا مصر ولم يذكر له حديثا وذكره بن عبد البر فقال محمد بن بشير الأنصاري روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم روى عنه ابنه يحيى زعم بعضهم أن حديثه مرسل كذا ذكره محمد بن بشر بكسر الموحده وسكون المعجمة وتبع في ذلك بن أبي حاتم فإنه ذكره فيمن اسم أبيه بشر مع محمد بن بشر العبدي ولكن ذكره بوزن عظيم جميع من تقدم
records.english: on the morphological pattern of ʿaẓīm Anṣārī. Al-Bukhārī mentioned him among the Companions and transmitted by way of Zakhr—with the zāy vowelled a and the dotted letter quiescent—ibn Ḥiṣn: My grandfather Ḥumayd ibn Manhab related to me: Khuraym ibn Ḥārithah ibn Lām al-Ṭāʾī related to me, saying: ‘We fought on the day of al-Ḥarrah. The first person I encountered was al-Shaymāʾ bint Buqaylah al-Azdiyyah, so I seized her and said, “This is the woman whom the Messenger of God ﷺ granted to me, and she is as the Messenger of God ﷺ said.” Khālid called upon me to produce evidence concerning her, so I brought him my two witnesses, Muḥammad ibn Salamah and Muḥammad ibn Bashīr al-Anṣārī, and he delivered her to me.’ Ibn Mandah transmitted it in full by this route and said, ‘It is known only through this chain. Zakariyyā ibn Yaḥyā alone transmitted it from Zakhr.’ I say: It was given in full earlier in the notice on Khuraym ibn Aws. Al-Baghawī, Ibn Shāhīn, Ibn Yūnus, and Ibn Mandah transmitted by way of Salamah ibn Shurayḥ, from Yaḥyā ibn Muḥammad ibn Bashīr al-Anṣārī, from his father, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said, ‘When God intends humiliation for a servant, He causes his wealth to be spent on building.’ He said, ‘I know of no other report narrated by Muḥammad ibn Bashīr.’ Ibn Ḥibbān transmitted it by this route and said, ‘This is disconnected,’ and Ibn Yūnus expressed doubt about his companionship, saying, ‘He is said to have had companionship. He was listed among the people of Egypt, but he is not well known among them. He has one report in Egypt,’ and he then cited the report. Muḥammad ibn al-Rabīʿah al-Jīzī listed him among the Companions who entered Egypt but cited no report for him. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr mentioned him, saying, ‘Muḥammad ibn Bashīr al-Anṣārī narrated from the Prophet ﷺ, and his son Yaḥyā narrated from him. Some maintain that his report is disconnected.’ Thus he recorded him as Muḥammad ibn Bishr, with the bāʾ vowelled i and the dotted letter quiescent, following Ibn Abī Ḥātim, who listed him among those whose father was named Bishr, alongside Muḥammad ibn Bishr al-ʿAbdī. Yet all those mentioned previously recorded his name on the pattern of ʿaẓīm.

records.arabic: بن عراب بن عوف بن ذؤالة بن شبوة بن ثوبان بن عبس بن غالب العكي وفد على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وشهد فتح مصر ذكروه في كتبهم ذكره بن يونس وأورده بن منده عنه مختصرا
records.english: ibn ʿIrāb ibn ʿAwf ibn Dhuʾālah ibn Shabwah ibn Thawbān ibn ʿAbs ibn Ghālib, al-ʿAkkī. He came as a delegation to the Messenger of God ﷺ and witnessed the conquest of Egypt. They mention him in their books. Ibn Yūnus recorded him, and Ibn Mandah included an abridged notice from him.

records.arabic: الأنصاري ذكره بن القداح وقال سماه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم محمدا وشهد معه فتح مكة حكاه بن أبي داود عنه وأخرجه بن شاهين واستدركه أبو موسى وذكر محمد بن حبيب في كتابه المحبر أنه أول من سمى محمدا في الإسلام من الأنصار وفي الإكليل للحاكم إن معاذ بن جبل كان من بني سعد بن علي بن أسد بن ساردة إنما صار في بني سلمة لأن فلان بن محمد بن الجد بن قيس وهو من بني سلمة كان أخاه من أمه انتهى وهذا يدل على قدم زمان محمد بن الجد بن قيس فيؤيد ما قاله القداح
records.english: al-Anṣārī. Ibn al-Qaddāḥ mentioned him and said that the Prophet ﷺ named him Muḥammad and that he witnessed the conquest of Mecca with him. Ibn Abī Dāwūd related this from him, Ibn Shāhīn transmitted it, and Abū Mūsā added him as an omission. Muḥammad ibn Ḥabīb stated in his book al-Muḥabbar that he was the first person among the Anṣār to be named Muḥammad in Islam. In al-Ḥākim’s al-Iklīl it is stated that Muʿādh ibn Jabal belonged to Banū Saʿd ibn ʿAlī ibn Asad ibn Sāridah and came to be among Banū Salimah only because so-and-so ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Jadd ibn Qays, who was of Banū Salimah, was his maternal brother. End of the passage. This indicates the early date of Muḥammad ibn al-Jadd ibn Qays and thus supports what Ibn al-Qaddāḥ said.

records.english: Ibn Ḥibbān mentioned him among the Companions and said, ‘It is said that he had companionship.’

records.arabic: بن عبد المطلب بن هاشم الهاشمي أخو عبد الله وعون ذكره بن حبان والبغوي وابن شاهين وابن حبان وغيرهم في الصحابة وقال محمد بن حبيب في المحبر هو أول من سمي محمد في الإسلام من المهاجرين وقال الدارقطني ولد بأرض الحبشة وقال بن منده وابن عبد البر ولد علي عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم آله وسلم وذكر أبو عمر عن الواقدي أنه كان يكنى أبا القاسم وأنه تزوج أم كلثوم بنت علي بعد عمر قال واستشهد بتستر وقيل إنه عاش إلى أن شهد صفين مع علي قال الدارقطني في كتاب الإخوة يقال إنه قتل بصفين اعترك هو وعبيد الله بن عمر بن الخطاب فقتل كل منهما الآخر وذكر المرزباني في معجم الشعراء أنه كان مع أخيه محمد بن أبي بكر بمصر فلما قتل اختفى محمد بن جعفر فدل عليه رجل من عك ثم من غافق فهرب إلى فلسطين وجاء إلى رجل من أخواله من خثعم فمنعه من معاوية فقال في ذلك شعرا وهذا محقق يرد قول الواقدي إنه استشهد بتستر
records.english: ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ibn Hāshim, al-Hāshimī Hāshimī, brother of ʿAbd Allāh and ʿAwn. Ibn Ḥibbān, al-Baghawī, Ibn Shāhīn, Ibn Ḥibbān again in the source list, and others mentioned him among the Companions. Muḥammad ibn Ḥabīb said in al-Muḥabbar that he was the first of the Emigrants to be named Muḥammad in Islam. Al-Dāraquṭnī said that he was born in Abyssinia. Ibn Mandah and Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said that he was born during the lifetime of the Prophet ﵌. Abū ʿUmar related from al-Wāqidī that his kunya was Abū al-Qāsim, that he married Umm Kulthūm bint ʿAlī after ʿUmar, and that he was martyred at Tustar. It is also said that he lived until he witnessed Ṣiffīn with ʿAlī. Al-Dāraquṭnī said in the Book of Brothers, ‘It is said that he was killed at Ṣiffīn. He and ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb engaged one another, and each killed the other.’ Al-Marzubānī mentioned in the Dictionary of Poets that he was in Egypt with his brother Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr. When the latter was killed, Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar went into hiding, but a man of ʿAkk, then of Ghāfiq, informed on him. He fled to Palestine and went to a maternal kinsman of his from Khathʿam, who protected him from Muʿāwiyah. He composed poetry about that. This is verified and refutes al-Wāqidī’s statement that he was martyred at Tustar.

title.english: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib

records.arabic: بن الحارث بن معمر بن حبيب بن وهب بن حذافة بن جمح أبو القاسم القرشي الجمحي وقيل أبو إبراهيم وقيل أبو وهب أمه أم جميل بنت المجلل العامرية يقال إنه ولد بأرض الحبشة وهاجر أبواه ومات أبوه بها فقدمت به أمه إلى المدينة مع أهل السفينين فروى عبد الله بن الحارث بن محمد بن حاطب عن أبيه عن جده قال لما قدمنا من أرض الحبشة خرجت بي أمي يعني إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالت يا رسول الله هذا بن أخيك وقد أصابه هذا الحرق من النار فادع الله له الحديث ورواه أيضا عبد الرحمن بن عثمان بن محمد الحاطبي عن أبيه عن جده أخرجه أحمد وابن أبي خيثمة والبغوي وفيه أن أمه قالت يا رسول الله هذا محمد بن حاطب وهو أول من سمع بك قالت فمسح على رأسك وتفل في فيك ودعا لك بالبركة وأخرج بن أبي خيثمة عن محمد بن سلام الجمحي قال وحدثني بعض أصحابنا قال هو أول من سمي في الإسلام محمدا ولد بأرض الحبشة وأرضعته أسماء بنت عميس مع ابنها عبد الله بن جعفر وأرضعت أم محمد عبد الله بن جعفر فكانا يتواصلان على ذلك حتى ماتا وقال بن شاهين سمعت البغوي يقول هو أول من سمي في الإسلام محمدا قال وكان يكنى أبا القاسم وجزم بن سعد بأن كنيته أبو إبراهيم وقال الهيثم مات في ولاية بشر على العراق وقال غيره سنة أربع وسبعين وأخرج من طريق أبي مالك الأشجعي قال قال لي بن حاطب خرج حاطب وجعفر إلى النجاشي فولدت أنا في تلك السفينة قلت والذي اشتهر أنه ولد بأرض الحبشة محمول على المجاز لأنه ولد قبل أن يصلوا إليها وقد روى محمد بن حاطب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعن أمه وعن علي روى عنه أولاده إبراهيم وعمر والحارث وأبو بلج وأبو مالك الأشجعي وهو بن محمد وسماك بن حرب وغيرهم وقيل مات سنة ست وثمانين
records.english: ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Muʿammar ibn Ḥabīb ibn Wahb ibn Ḥudhāfah ibn Jumaḥ, Abū al-Qāsim, al-Qurashī al-Jumaḥī and Jumaḥī. It is also said that he was Abū Ibrāhīm or Abū Wahb. His mother was Umm Jamīl bint al-Mujallal al-ʿĀmiriyyah. It is said that he was born in Abyssinia, that his parents emigrated there, and that his father died there. His mother brought him to Medina with the people of the two ships. ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥāṭib narrated from his father, from his grandfather, who said: ‘When we arrived from Abyssinia, my mother took me out’—meaning to the Messenger of God ﷺ—‘and said, “O Messenger of God, this is your brother’s son, and he has suffered this burn from fire, so pray to God for him”’—the report. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿUthmān ibn Muḥammad al-Ḥāṭibī also narrated it from his father, from his grandfather; Aḥmad, Ibn Abī Khaythamah, and al-Baghawī transmitted it. It states that his mother said, ‘O Messenger of God, this is Muḥammad ibn Ḥāṭib, and he was the first to hear of you.’ She said, ‘He stroked your head, spat into your mouth, and prayed that you be blessed.’ Ibn Abī Khaythamah transmitted from Muḥammad ibn Sallām al-Jumaḥī, who said: One of our companions related to me that he was the first person in Islam to be named Muḥammad. He was born in Abyssinia. Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays nursed him alongside her son ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, while Muḥammad’s mother nursed ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar; the two continued to maintain relations on that account until they died. Ibn Shāhīn said: I heard al-Baghawī say, ‘He was the first person in Islam to be named Muḥammad.’ He said that his kunya was Abū al-Qāsim. Ibn Saʿd stated definitively that his kunya was Abū Ibrāhīm. Al-Haytham said that he died while Bishr was governor of Iraq; someone else said in the year 74. He transmitted by way of Abū Mālik al-Ashjaʿī, who said: Ibn Ḥāṭib said to me, ‘Ḥāṭib and Jaʿfar set out for the Negus, and I was born on that ship.’ I say: The well-known statement that he was born in Abyssinia is to be understood figuratively, for he was born before they reached it. Muḥammad ibn Ḥāṭib narrated from the Prophet ﷺ, from his mother, and from ʿAlī. His children Ibrāhīm, ʿUmar, and al-Ḥārith, as well as Abū Balj, Abū Mālik al-Ashjaʿī—who is Ibn Muḥammad—Simāk ibn Ḥarb, and others narrated from him. It is also said that he died in the year 86.

records.arabic: النضري بالنون ويقال المصري بكسر الميم وهو الأشهر ووقع عند أبي عمر بضم الميم وفتح الضاد المعجمة وقد قال بن منده لا يعرف في الشاميين ولا في المصريين ذكره في الصحابة وأخرج البغوي وغيره من طريق الوليد بن سليمان عن بسر بن عبيد الله عن بن محيريز عن عبد الله بن السعدي عن محمد بن حبيب قال أتينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقلنا يا رسول الله إن رجالا يقولون قد انقطعت الهجرة فقال لا تنقطع الهجرة ما قوتل الكفار وقال البغوي رواه غير واحد عن بن محيريز عن عبد الله بن السعدي أن النسائي أخرجه من طريق أبي إدريس عن عبد الله بن السعدي ليس فيه محمد بن حبيب
records.english: al-Naḍrī nūn. He is also called al-Miṣrī, with the mīm vowelled i, and this is the better-known form. In Abū ʿUmar’s text it occurs with the mīm vowelled u and the dotted ḍād vowelled a: al-Muḍarī. Ibn Mandah said, ‘He is known neither among the Syrians nor among the Egyptians.’ He mentioned him among the Companions. Al-Baghawī and others transmitted by way of al-Walīd ibn Sulaymān, from Busr ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from Ibn Muḥayrīz, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Saʿdī, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥabīb, who said: ‘We went to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said, “O Messenger of God, some men say that emigration has ceased.” He replied, “Emigration does not cease so long as the unbelievers are fought.”’ Al-Baghawī said: More than one transmitter narrated it from Ibn Muḥayrīz, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Saʿdī. Al-Nasāʾī transmitted it by way of Abū Idrīs, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Saʿdī, without Muḥammad ibn Ḥabīb in the chain.

records.arabic: بن عتبة بن ربيعة بن عبد شمس بن عبد مناف العبشمي أبو القاسم ولد بأرض الحبشة وكان أبوه من السابقين الأولين وهو مشهور بكنيته واختلف في اسمه كما سيأتي في الكنى وأمه سهلة بنت سهيل بن عمرو العامرية قال بن لهيعة عن أبي الأسود عن عروة ولد محمد بن أبي حذيفة بأرض الحبشة وكذا قال بن إسحاق والواقدي وابن سعد وذكره الواقدي فيمن كان يكنى أبا القاسم واسمه محمد من الصحابة واستشهد أبوه أبو حذيفة باليمامة فضم عثمان محمدا هذا إليه ورباه فلما كبر واستخلف عثمان استأذنه في التوجه إلى مصر فأذن له فكان من أشد الناس تأليبا عليه ذكر أبو عمر الكندي في أمراء مصر أن عبد الله بن سعد أمير مصر لعثمان كان توجه إلى عثمان لما قام الناس عليه فطلب أمراء الأمصار فتوجه إليه وذلك في رجب سنة خمس وثلاثين واستناب عقبة بن عامر وفي نسخة بن مالك فوثب محمد بن أبي حذيفة على عقبة فأخرجه من مصر وذلك في شوال منها ودعا إلى خلع عثمان وأسعر البلاد وحرض الناس على عثمان وأخرج من طريق الليث عن عبد الكريم بن الحارث الحضرمي أن بن أبي حذيفة كان يكتب الكتب على ألسنة أزواج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في الطعن على عثمان كان يأخذ الرواحل فيحصرها ثم يأخذ الرجال الذين يريد أن يبعث بذلك معهم فيجعلهم على ظهور بيت في الحر فيستقبلون بوجوههم الشمس ليلوحهم تلويح المسافر ثم يأمرهم أن يخرجوا إلى طريق المدينة ثم يرسلوا رسلا يخبروا بقدومهم فيأمر بتلقيهم فإذا أتوا الناس قالوا لهم ليس عندنا خبر الخبر في الكتب فيتلقاهم بن أبي حذيفة ومعه الناس فيقول لهم الرسل عليكم بالمسجد فيقرأ عليهم الكتب من أمهات المؤمنين إنا نشكو إليكم بأهل الإسلام كذا وكذا من الطعن على عثمان فيضج أهل المسجد بالبكاء والدعاء ثم روى من طريق بن لهيعة عن يزيد بن أبي حبيب قال بايع أهل مصر محمد بن أبي حذيفة بالإمارة إلا عصابة منهم معاوية بن حديج وبسر بن أرطاة فقدم عبد الله بن سعد حتى إذا بلغ القلزم وجد هناك خيلا لابن أبي حذيفة فمنعوه أن يدخل فانصرف إلى عسقلان ثم جهز بن أبي حذيفة الذين ثاروا على عثمان وحاصروه إلى أن كان من قتله ما كان فلما علم بذلك من امتنع من مبايعة بن أبي حذيفة اجتمعوا وتبايعوا على الطب بدمه فسار بهم معاوية بن حديج إلى الصعيد فأرسل إليهم بن أبي حذيفة جيشا آخر فالتقوا فقتل قائد الجيش ثم كان من مسير معاوية بن أبي سفيان إلى مصر لما أراد المسير إلى صفين فرأى ألا يترك أهل مصر مع بن أبي حذيفة خلفه فسار إليهم في عسكر كثيف فخرج إليهم بن أبي حذيفة في أهل مصر فمنعوه من دخول الفسطاط فأرسل إليهم إنا لا نريد قتال أحد وإنما نطلب قتلة عثمان فدار الكلام بينهم في الموادعة واستخلف بن أبي حذيفة على مصر الحكم بن الصلت بن مخرمة بن المطلب بن عبد مناف وخرج مع جماعة منهم عبد الرحمن بن عديس وكنانة بن بشر وأبو شمر بن أبرهة بن الصباح فلما بلغوا به غدر بهم عسكر معاوية وسجنوهم إلى أن قتلوا بعد ذلك وذكر أبو أحمد الحاكم أن محمدا بن أبي حذيفة لما ضبط مصر وأراد معاوية الخروج إلى صفين بدأ بمصر أولا فقاتله محمد بن أبي حذيفة بالعريش إلى أن تصالحا وطلب منه معاوية ناسا يكونون تحت يده رهنا ليأمن جانبهم إذا خرج إلى صفين فأخرج محمد رهنا عدتهم ثلاثون نفسا فأحيط بهم وهو فيهم فسجنوا وقال أبو أحمد الحاكم خدع معاوية محمد بن أبي حذيفة حتى خرج إلى العريش في ثلاثين نفسا فحاصره ونصب عليه المنجنيق حتى نزل على صلح فحبس ثم قتل وأخرج بن عائذ من طريق بن لهيعة عن يزيد بن حبيب قال فرقهم معاوية بصفين فسجن بن أبي حذيفة ومن معه في سجن دمشق وسجن بن عديس والباقين في سجن بعلبك وأخرج يعقوب بن سفيان في تاريخه من طريق بن المبارك عن حرملة بن عمران عن عبد العزيز بن عبد الملك السليحي حدثني أبي قال كنت مع عقبة بن عامر قريبا من المنبر فخرج بن أبي حذيفة فحطب الناس ثم قرأ عليهم سورة وكان قارئا فقال عقبة صدق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ليقرأن القرآن ناس لا يجاوز تراقيهم فسمعه بن أبي حذيفة فقال إن كنت صادقا إنك لمتهم وأخرج البغوي من طريق الليث عن يزيد بن أبي حبيب قال كان رجال من الصحابة يحدثون أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال يقتل بجبل الخليل والقطران من أصحابي أو من أمتي ناس فكان أولئك النفر الذين قتلوا مع محمد بن أبي حذيفة هناك ورواه أبو عمر الكندي من وجه آخر عن الليث قال قال محمد بن أبي حذيفة هذه الليلة التي قتل فيها عثمان فإن يكن القصاص بعثمان فسيقتل في غد فقتل في الغد وذكر خليفة بن خياط في تاريخه أن عليا لما ولي الخلافة أقر محمد بن أبي حذيفة على إمرة مصر ثم ولاها محمد بن أبي بكر واختلف في وفاته فقال بن قتيبة قتله رشدين مولى معاوية وقال بن الكلبي قتله مالك بن هبيرة السكوني
records.english: ibn ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah ibn ʿAbd Shams ibn ʿAbd Manāf, al-ʿAbshamī, Abū al-Qāsim. He was born in Abyssinia. His father was among the foremost early converts. He is well known by his kunya, and there is disagreement about his name, as will come in the section on kunyahs. His mother was Sahlah bint Suhayl ibn ʿAmr al-ʿĀmiriyyah. Ibn Lahīʿah related from Abū al-Aswad, from ʿUrwah, that Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥudhayfah was born in Abyssinia. Ibn Isḥāq, al-Wāqidī, and Ibn Saʿd said the same. Al-Wāqidī listed him among the Companions whose kunya was Abū al-Qāsim and whose name was Muḥammad. His father Abū Ḥudhayfah was martyred at al-Yamāmah, so ʿUthmān took this Muḥammad into his household and raised him. When he grew up and ʿUthmān became caliph, he asked ʿUthmān’s permission to go to Egypt, and he permitted him. He then became one of the most vehement agitators against him. Abū ʿUmar al-Kindī stated in The Governors of Egypt that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿd, ʿUthmān’s governor of Egypt, went to ʿUthmān when the people rose against him and he summoned the provincial governors. That was in Rajab of the year 35. He appointed ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir as his deputy—or, in one copy, Ibn Mālik. Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥudhayfah rose against ʿUqbah and expelled him from Egypt in Shawwāl of that year. He called for ʿUthmān’s removal, inflamed the country, and incited the people against him. He transmitted by way of al-Layth, from ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn al-Ḥārith al-Ḥaḍramī, that Ibn Abī Ḥudhayfah used to compose letters in the names of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ attacking ʿUthmān. He would take riding camels and pen them up, then take the men with whom he intended to send the letters, place them on a rooftop in the heat, and turn their faces toward the sun so that they became weathered like travelers. He would then order them to go out to the Medina road and send messengers announcing their arrival, whereupon he ordered that they be met. When they came to the people, the people asked them, and they replied, ‘We have no report; the report is in the letters.’ Ibn Abī Ḥudhayfah and the people would meet them; the messengers would then address them, saying, ‘Go to the mosque.’ The letters purportedly from the Mothers of the Believers would then be read to them: ‘We complain to you, people of Islam, of such-and-such accusations against ʿUthmān.’ The people of the mosque would erupt in weeping and supplication. He then narrated by way of Ibn Lahīʿah, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, who said: The people of Egypt pledged allegiance to Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥudhayfah as governor, except for a group including Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥudayj and Busr ibn Arṭāh. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿd returned, but when he reached al-Qulzum he found cavalry belonging to Ibn Abī Ḥudhayfah there; they prevented him from entering, so he withdrew to ʿAsqalān. Ibn Abī Ḥudhayfah then equipped those who rose against ʿUthmān and besieged him until his killing occurred as it did. When those who had refused to pledge allegiance to Ibn Abī Ḥudhayfah learned of this, they gathered and pledged over the damaged phrase ‘al-ṭibb bi-damihi’; its intended sense remains unresolved. Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥudayj led them to Upper Egypt. Ibn Abī Ḥudhayfah sent another army against them; the two sides met and the army’s commander was killed. Then Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān marched toward Egypt when he intended to proceed to Ṣiffīn, judging that he should not leave the people of Egypt under Ibn Abī Ḥudhayfah behind him. He marched against them with a large force. Ibn Abī Ḥudhayfah came out against them with the people of Egypt and barred them from entering al-Fusṭāṭ. Muʿāwiyah sent word, ‘We do not wish to fight anyone; we seek only ʿUthmān’s killers.’ Negotiations for a truce passed between them. Ibn Abī Ḥudhayfah appointed al-Ḥakam ibn al-Ṣalt ibn Makhramah ibn al-Muṭṭalib ibn ʿAbd Manāf as his deputy over Egypt and went out with a group including ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿUdays, Kinānah ibn Bishr, and Abū Shimr ibn Abrahah ibn al-Ṣabāḥ. When they reached Muʿāwiyah’s army, it betrayed them and imprisoned them until they were later killed. Abū Aḥmad al-Ḥākim mentioned that when Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥudhayfah took control of Egypt and Muʿāwiyah wished to go to Ṣiffīn, he began with Egypt. Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥudhayfah fought him at al-ʿArīsh until they made peace. Muʿāwiyah requested people whom he could hold as hostages so that he would be safe from their quarter when he went to Ṣiffīn. Muḥammad sent out thirty hostages, and they were surrounded while he was among them and were imprisoned. Abū Aḥmad al-Ḥākim said: Muʿāwiyah deceived Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥudhayfah until he came out to al-ʿArīsh with thirty men. He besieged him and set up a mangonel against him until he surrendered under an agreement; then he imprisoned and killed him. Ibn ʿĀʾidh transmitted by way of Ibn Lahīʿah, from Yazīd ibn Ḥabīb, who said: Muʿāwiyah separated them at Ṣiffīn. He imprisoned Ibn Abī Ḥudhayfah and those with him in the prison of Damascus, and imprisoned Ibn ʿUdays and the others in the prison of Baalbek. Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān transmitted in his History by way of Ibn al-Mubārak, from Ḥarmalah ibn ʿImrān, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿAbd al-Malik al-Sulayḥī: My father related to me, saying: I was with ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir near the pulpit when Ibn Abī Ḥudhayfah came out, addressed the people, and then recited a sura to them, for he was a reciter. ʿUqbah said, ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ spoke truly: people will recite the Qurʾan, yet it will not pass beyond their throats.’ Ibn Abī Ḥudhayfah heard him and said, ‘If you speak the truth, then you are surely one of them.’ Al-Baghawī transmitted by way of al-Layth, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, who said: Men among the Companions used to relate that the Prophet ﷺ said, ‘At Mount al-Khalīl and al-Qaṭrān, men from among my Companions—or from my community—will be killed.’ They were those men who were killed there with Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥudhayfah. Abū ʿUmar al-Kindī narrated it by another route from al-Layth and said: Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥudhayfah said on the night in which ʿUthmān was killed, ‘If retribution is exacted for ʿUthmān, I shall be killed tomorrow.’ He was killed the next day. Khalīfah ibn Khayyāṭ stated in his History that when ʿAlī assumed the caliphate, he retained Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥudhayfah as governor of Egypt, then appointed Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr over it. There is disagreement about his death: Ibn Qutaybah said that Rushdīn, Muʿāwiyah’s client, killed him, while Ibn al-Kalbī said that Mālik ibn Hubayrah al-Sakūnī killed him.

records.arabic: الأنصاري ذكره البغوي وقال ذكره البخاري فيمن روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا يعرف وكذا قال بن شاهين لم يزد وقال أبو نعيم ذكره أبو العباس الهروي في المحمدين في الصحابة وذكر روايته عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ليكمل أمتي يوم القيامة سبعين أمة نحن آخرها وخيرها وقال بن منده محمد بن حزم تابعي روى عنه قتادة ولا يعرف وقال بن الأثير الذي لا يعرف محمد بن عمرو بن حزم الآتي فلعله نسب إلى جده
records.english: al-Anṣārī. Al-Baghawī mentioned him and said, ‘Al-Bukhārī listed him among those who narrated from the Prophet ﷺ, but he is not known.’ Ibn Shāhīn likewise said this and added nothing. Abū Nuʿaym said: Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Harawī mentioned him among the men named Muḥammad who were Companions and cited his narration from the Prophet ﷺ: ‘On the Day of Resurrection, my community will complete seventy communities; we are the last and the best of them.’ Ibn Mandah said, ‘Muḥammad ibn Ḥazm is a Successor. Qatādah narrated from him, and he is not known.’ Ibn al-Athīr said, ‘The one who is not known is Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm, who will appear later; perhaps he was traced to his grandfather.’

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن الحارث بن معمر الجمحي بن عم محمد بن حاطب تقدم نسبه قريبا قال بن عبد البر ولد أيضا بأرض الحبشة وقيل قبل الهجرة إلى أرض الحبشة فهو أسن من محمد بن حاطب كذا قال وقد تقدم أن محمد بن حاطب أول من سمي محمدا في الإسلام من المهاجرين فيكون أسن وأخرج أحمد من طريق عثمان بن محمد عن أم محمد بن حاطب أنها لما أحضرت إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ابنها قالت هذا محمد بن حاطب وهو أول من سمي باسمك وقد تقدم في ترجمة محمد بن حاطب وأخرج أبو الفرج الأصبهاني من وجهين عن عبد الملك بن عمير قال أتى عمر بن الخطاب بحلل فقال علي بالمحمدين فأتى بمحمد بن أبي بكر ومحمد بن جعفر ومحمد بن طلحة ومحمد بن عمرو بن حزم ومحمد بن حاطب وابن عمه محمد بن حطاب وكلهم سماه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم محمدا فذكر قصته فإن كان محفوظا حمل على المجاز أي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أقرهم على ذلك
records.english: ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Muʿammar, al-Jumaḥī, cousin of Muḥammad ibn Ḥāṭib. His lineage was given shortly before. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said that he too was born in Abyssinia. It is also said that he was born before the emigration to Abyssinia, in which case he was older than Muḥammad ibn Ḥāṭib. That is what he said. Yet it was stated above that Muḥammad ibn Ḥāṭib was the first of the Emigrants to be named Muḥammad in Islam, so he would be the older. Aḥmad transmitted by way of ʿUthmān ibn Muḥammad, from the mother of Muḥammad ibn Ḥāṭib, that when she brought her son to the Prophet ﷺ she said, ‘This is Muḥammad ibn Ḥāṭib, and he is the first to be named after you.’ This was given earlier in the notice on Muḥammad ibn Ḥāṭib. Abū al-Faraj al-Iṣbahānī transmitted by two routes from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, who said: Garments were brought to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and he said, ‘Bring me the men named Muḥammad.’ Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr, Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar, Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥah, Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm, Muḥammad ibn Ḥāṭib, and his cousin Muḥammad ibn Ḥaṭṭāb were brought. The Prophet ﷺ had named all of them Muḥammad; then he related the story. If this is preserved correctly, the statement is to be understood figuratively: that the Prophet ﷺ approved of their being so named.

records.arabic: بن عامر قال بن القداح شهد الفتح وكان اسمه عبد مناة فسماه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم محمدا أخرجه بن شاهين عن بن أبي داود عنه
records.english: ibn ʿĀmir. Ibn al-Qaddāḥ said that he witnessed the Conquest. His name had been ʿAbd Manāh, but the Prophet ﷺ named him Muḥammad. Ibn Shāhīn transmitted it from Ibn Abī Dāwūd, from him.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الأنصاري قال بن القداح صحب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وشهد فتح مكة ذكره بن شاهين أيضا عن أبي داود عنه
records.english: al-Anṣārī. Ibn al-Qaddāḥ said that he accompanied the Prophet ﷺ and witnessed the conquest of Mecca. Ibn Shāhīn also mentioned it from Abū Dāwūd, from him.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن عبد يزيد المطلبي القرشي يأتي في القسم الأخير إن شاء الله تعالى
records.english: ibn ʿAbd Yazīd, al-Muṭṭalibī al-Qurashī and Qurashī. He will appear in the final section, إن شاء الله تعالى.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: قال بن منده أخرجه أبو حاتم الرازي في الوحدان وهو وهم ثم أخرج من طريقه بسند له إلى محمد بن عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى عن عطاء عن محمد بن زيد قال أهدي لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لحم صيد فأبى أن يأكله قال وهذا رواه قيس بن سعد عن عطاء عن بن عباس قلت أخرجه أبو داود والنسائي من طريق حماد بن سلمة عن قيس بن سعد عن عطاء عن بن عباس عن زيد بن أرقم وأكثر الطبراني من تخريج طرقه وقال بن أبي حاتم عن أبيه روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فذكر هذا الحديث روى عن عطاء بن أبي رباح وكذا قال بن عبد البر وهو على الاحتمال لجواز التعدد مع بعده بقرينة كثرة خطأ محمد بن عبد الرحمن
records.english: Ibn Mandah said: Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī included him among those with a single transmitter, but this is an error.’ He then transmitted by Abū Ḥātim’s route, with a chain reaching Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Zayd, who said: ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ was given game meat as a gift, but he declined to eat it.’ He said, ‘Qays ibn Saʿd narrated this from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās.’ I say: Abū Dāwūd and al-Nasāʾī transmitted it by way of Ḥammād ibn Salamah, from Qays ibn Saʿd, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from Zayd ibn Arqam. Al-Ṭabarānī collected many of its routes. Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from his father: ‘He narrated from the Prophet ﷺ’—and cited this report—‘and ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ narrated from him.’ Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said the same. This interpretation also remains possible, since there could have been two people, although that is remote in view of Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān’s many errors.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: له ذكر في كتاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم للداريين ذكره بن منده من رواية سعيد بن زياد عن آبائه عن أبي هند الداري في قصة إسلامه وأمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يكتب له الكتاب الذي طلبه وذكر فيه شهادة أبي بكر وعمر وعثمان وعلي ومحمد بن أبي سفيان وقد تعقبه أبو نعيم بأن الصواب في هذا معاوية بن أبي سفيان لا محمد قلت هو على الاحتمال أيضا
records.english: He is mentioned in the Prophet’s ﷺ document for the Dārīs. Ibn Mandah recorded him from the narration of Saʿīd ibn Ziyād, from his forefathers, from Abū Hind al-Dārī, in the account of his acceptance of Islam and the Prophet’s ﷺ instruction that the document he requested be written for him. It mentions the testimony of Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, and Muḥammad ibn Abī Sufyān. Abū Nuʿaym objected that the correct name here is Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān, not Muḥammad. I say: This too remains possible.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن عبد الأسد المخزومي قال بن حبان له صحبة وقال البغوي ذكره بعض من ألف في الصحابة وأنكر عليه حكاه بن شاهين عن البغوي
records.english: ibn ʿAbd al-Asad, al-Makhzūmī. Ibn Ḥibbān said that he had companionship. Al-Baghawī said, ‘One of those who wrote works on the Companions mentioned him, and he was criticized for doing so.’ Ibn Shāhīn related this from al-Baghawī.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن رفاعة بن خليفة بن أبي كعب قال بن القداح شهد أحدا وحضر فتح العراق وقتل يوم صفين ذكره بن شاهين عن بن أبي داود عن بن القداح
records.english: ibn Rifāʿah ibn Khalīfah ibn Abī Kaʿb. Ibn al-Qaddāḥ said that he witnessed Uḥud, was present at the conquest of Iraq, and was killed on the day of Ṣiffīn. Ibn Shāhīn mentioned him from Ibn Abī Dāwūd, from Ibn al-Qaddāḥ.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الأنصاري من بني مالك بن الأوس ذكر ذلك العسكري وقيل فيه صفوان بن محمد والأول أصوب وأخرج أحمد وأصحاب السنن وابن حبان والحاكم في صحيحيهما من طريق داود بن أبي هند عن الشعبي عنه أنه أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بأرنبين ذبحهما بمروة على الشك وأخرجه علي بن عبد العزيز في مسنده من رواية حماد بن سلمة عن داود فقال عن محمد بن صفوان بالجزم وكذا أخرجه البغوي من طريق شعبة ومن طريق عبدة بن سليمان وحكى بن شاهين عن البغوي أنه الراجح وقال لا أعلم لمحمد بن صفوان غيره
records.english: al-Anṣārī, of Banū Mālik ibn al-Aws. Al-ʿAskarī mentioned this. He is also called Ṣafwān ibn Muḥammad, but the first form is more correct. Aḥmad, the compilers of the Sunan, Ibn Ḥibbān, and al-Ḥākim transmitted in their two Ṣaḥīḥ works by way of Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind, from al-Shaʿbī, from him, that he brought the Prophet ﷺ two hares which he had slaughtered with a flint—this wording being uncertain. ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz transmitted it in his Musnad from the narration of Ḥammād ibn Salamah, from Dāwūd, stating Muḥammad ibn Ṣafwān without uncertainty. Al-Baghawī likewise transmitted it by way of Shuʿbah and by way of ʿAbdah ibn Sulaymān. Ibn Shāhīn related from al-Baghawī that this is the weightier version, and he said, ‘I know of no other report belonging to Muḥammad ibn Ṣafwān.’

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن عابد بن عبد الله بن عمر بن مخزوم قال بن القداح له صحبة ذكره بن شاهين عن أبي داود وقال أبو عمر لا رؤية له وفي صحبته نظر وهو سبط خديحة بنت خويلد أمه هند بنت عتيق بن عامر بن عبد الله بن عمر بن مخزوم وأمها خديجة وعابد بالموحدة والدال المهملة قلت ذكر الزبير بن بكار ما يقوي قول بن القداح فإنه لما ذكر أباه قال كان له رفاعة وبه كان يكنى وصيفي بن أمية قتل يوم بدر انتهى ومن يقتل أبوه ببدر وهي في السنة الثانية من الهجرة يكون أدرك من العهد النبوي ثمان سنين فأكثر فلا يسمى محمدا إلا وقد أسلم أبوه وأمه فلعله ولد بعد قتل أبيه وأسلمت أمه فسمته محمدا أو بعض أهله إن كانت أمه ماتت قبل تسميته
records.english: ibn ʿĀbid ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn Makhzūm. Ibn al-Qaddāḥ said that he had companionship. Ibn Shāhīn mentioned him from Abū Dāwūd. Abū ʿUmar said, ‘He had no direct sighting, and his companionship is questionable.’ He was a grandson of Khadīḥah bint Khuwaylid—the first spelling is damaged, and the same unit later gives Khadījah. His mother was Hind bint ʿAtīq ibn ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn Makhzūm, whose mother was Khadījah. ʿĀbid is spelled with the letter bāʾ and an undotted dāl. I say: Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār mentioned something that strengthens Ibn al-Qaddāḥ’s position, for when he mentioned Muḥammad’s father, he said, ‘He had a son named Rifāʿah, after whom he received his kunya, and Ṣayfī ibn Umayyah was killed on the day of Badr.’ End of the passage. One whose father was killed at Badr, in the second year of the Hijra, would have lived through eight years or more of the prophetic period. He would not have been named Muḥammad unless his father and mother had embraced Islam. Perhaps, then, he was born after his father was killed and his mother embraced Islam and named him Muḥammad—or some member of his family did so, if his mother died before he was named.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن الحارث الخطبي الأنصاري نسبه هشيم في روايته عن حصين عن الشعبي عنه حديثا مرفوعا في صوم يوم عاشوراء ويقال إنه نزل الكوفة وأخرج له أحمد والنسائي وابن ماجة وابن خزيمة والحاكم في صحيحها من طريق حصين عن الشعبي عن محمد بن صيفي في صوم يوم عاشوراء وسنده صحيح وأخرج البغوي من طريق الأعمش وغيره عن الشعبي عن محمد بن صيفي قال أتيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بأرنبين الحديث وقال البغوي هذا وهم والصواب محمد بن صفوان يعني كما تقدم في الذي قبله
records.english: ibn al-Ḥārith, al-Khaṭbī al-Anṣārī. Hushaym gave this lineage in his narration from Ḥuṣayn, from al-Shaʿbī, from him, of a report raised to the Prophet concerning fasting on the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ. It is said that he settled in Kufa. Aḥmad, al-Nasāʾī, Ibn Mājah, Ibn Khuzaymah, and al-Ḥākim transmitted for him in their two Ṣaḥīḥ works by way of Ḥuṣayn, from al-Shaʿbī, from Muḥammad ibn Ṣayfī, concerning fasting on the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ, and its chain is sound. Al-Baghawī transmitted by way of al-Aʿmash and others, from al-Shaʿbī, from Muḥammad ibn Ṣayfī, who said, ‘I brought the Messenger of God ﷺ two hares’—the report. Al-Baghawī said, ‘This is an error; the correct person is Muḥammad ibn Ṣafwān,’ meaning as stated in the preceding notice.

records.arabic: بن الأسود بن عباد بن غنم بن سواد ذكر بن القداح أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سماه محمدا وشهد فتح مكة أخرجه بن شاهين عن أبي داود عنه
records.english: ibn al-Aswad ibn ʿAbbād ibn Ghanm ibn Sawād. Ibn al-Qaddāḥ mentioned that the Prophet ﷺ named him Muḥammad and that he witnessed the conquest of Mecca. Ibn Shāhīn transmitted it from Abū Dāwūd, from him.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic:
بن عبيد الله القرشي التيمي تقدم نسبه في ترجمة أبيه أحد العشرة ذكره البخاري في الصحابة وقالوا ولد في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأخرج البخاري والبغوي والطبراني وغيرهم من طريق هلال الوزان عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى قال نظر عمر إلى عبد الحميد يعني بن زيد بن الخطاب وكان اسمه محمدا ورجل يقول له فعل الله يا محمد وفعل فقال له عمر لا أرى محمدا يسب بك والله لا يدعى محمدا أبدا ما دمت حيا فسماه عبد الرحمن وأرسل إلى بني طلحة وهم سبعة وسيدهم وكبيرهم محمد لتغيير أسمائهم فقال له محمد أذكرك الله يا أمير المؤمنين فوالله لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم سماني محمدا فقال عمر قوموا فلا سبيل إلى تغيير شيء سماه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأخرج بن منده من طريق يوسف بن إبراهيم الطلحي عن أبيه إبراهيم بن محمد أن طلحة قال سمى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ابني محمدا وكناه أبا القاسم وأخرج الزبير بن بكار من طريق راشد بن حفص الزهري قال أدرك أربعة من أبناء الصحابة كل منهم يسمى محمدا ويكنى أبا القاسم بن أبي بكر وابن علي وابن سعد وابن طلحة وأخرج بن قانع وابن السكن وابن شاهين من طريق محمد بن عبد الرحمن مولى آل طلحة عن إبراهيم بن محمد بن طلحة عن ظئر محمد بن طلحة قال أتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بمحمد بن طلحة حين ولد ليحنكه ويدعو له وكان يفعل ذلك بالصبيان فقال لعائشة من هذا قالت محمد بن طلحة فقال هذا سميي هذا أبو القاسم ومن طريق محمد بن زيد بن المهاجر عن إبراهيم بن محمد بن طلحة قال لما ولدت حمنة بنت جحش محمد بن طلحة جاءت به إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فسماه محمدا وكناه أبا سليمان وأخرجه بن منده من وجه آخر عن إبراهيم بن محمد عن طلحة عن أبيه أنه ذهب به إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حين ولد فسماه محمدا وقال هو أبو سليمان لا أجمع له بني اسمي وكنيتي وقال بن منده المشهور الأول وكان محمد كثير العبادة وكان يقال له السجاد وأخرج البغوي من طريق حصين بن عبد الرحمن عن أبي جميلة الطهوي قال لما كان يوم الجمل قال محمد بن طلحة لعائشة يا أم المؤمنين قالت كن كخير ابني آدم قال فأغمد سيفه وكان قد سله ثم قام حتى قتل قال البغوي قال غيره قتله شريع بن أوفى فمر به علي فقال هذا السجاد قتله بره بأبيه وكان ذلك في سنة ست وثلاثين واختلف في اسم قاتله وذكر البخاري في تفسير غافر تعليقا ما يقوى ما قال البغوي أن اسم قاتله شريح بن أبي أوفى
يذكرني حم والرمح شاجر
فهلا تلا حم قبل التقدم وهي أبيات أولها وأشعث قوام بآيات ربه قليل الأذى فيما ترى العين مسلم قال بن عبد البر وقيل اسم قاتله كعب بن مدلج وقيل شداد بن معاوية وقيل عصام بن مقشعر وقيل الأشتر وقيل عبد الله بن مكعبر وقيل غير ذلك وقد ذكرتها منسوبة لقائلها في فتح الباري
records.english:
ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, al-Qurashī al-Taymī and Taymī. His lineage was given earlier in the notice on his father, one of the Ten. Al-Bukhārī mentioned him among the Companions, and they said that he was born during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ. Al-Bukhārī, al-Baghawī, al-Ṭabarānī, and others transmitted by way of Hilāl al-Wazzān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, who said: ʿUmar looked at ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd—meaning the son of Zayd ibn al-Khaṭṭāb—whose name had been Muḥammad, while a man was saying to him, ‘May God do such-and-such to you, Muḥammad!’ ʿUmar said to him, ‘I will not allow Muḥammad to be insulted through you. By God, you shall never be called Muḥammad so long as I live,’ and named him ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. He sent for the sons of Ṭalḥah, who were seven, their chief and eldest being Muḥammad, intending to change their names. Muḥammad said to him, ‘I remind you of God, O Commander of the Believers. By God, Muḥammad ﷺ named me Muḥammad.’ ʿUmar said, ‘Rise, then; there is no way to change something that the Messenger of God ﷺ named.’ Ibn Mandah transmitted by way of Yūsuf ibn Ibrāhīm al-Ṭalḥī, from his father Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad, that Ṭalḥah said, ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ named my son Muḥammad and gave him the kunya Abū al-Qāsim.’ Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār transmitted by way of Rāshid ibn Ḥafṣ al-Zuhrī, who said: I encountered four sons of Companions, each named Muḥammad and bearing the kunya Abū al-Qāsim: the son of Abū Bakr, the son of ʿAlī, the son of Saʿd, and the son of Ṭalḥah. Ibn Qāniʿ, Ibn al-Sakan, and Ibn Shāhīn transmitted by way of Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, client of the family of Ṭalḥah, from Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥah, from Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥah’s wet nurse, who said: ‘I brought Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥah to the Prophet ﷺ when he was born so that he might rub his palate and pray for him, as he used to do for children. He said to ʿĀʾishah, “Who is this?” She said, “Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥah.” He replied, “This is my namesake; this is Abū al-Qāsim.”’ By way of Muḥammad ibn Zayd ibn al-Muhājir, from Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥah, it is narrated: ‘When Ḥamnah bint Jaḥsh gave birth to Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥah, she brought him to the Messenger of God ﷺ, who named him Muḥammad and gave him the kunya Abū Sulaymān.’ Ibn Mandah transmitted by another route from Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad, from Ṭalḥah, from his father, that he took him to the Messenger of God ﷺ when he was born. He named him Muḥammad and said, ‘He is Abū Sulaymān. I will not combine for him my name and my kunya.’ Ibn Mandah said, ‘The first version is the well-known one.’ Muḥammad was devoted to worship and was called al-Sajjād. Al-Baghawī transmitted by way of Ḥuṣayn ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Jamīlah al-Ṭahawī, who said: On the day of the Camel, Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥah said to ʿĀʾishah, ‘O Mother of the Believers.’ She replied, ‘Be like the better of Adam’s two sons.’ He sheathed his sword after having drawn it, then stood until he was killed. Al-Baghawī said: Someone else said that Shurayḥ ibn Awfā killed him. ʿAlī passed by him and said, ‘This is al-Sajjād; his dutifulness toward his father killed him.’ That was in the year 36. There is disagreement over his killer’s name. In his commentary on Sūrat Ghāfir, al-Bukhārī cited without a full chain material that supports al-Baghawī’s statement that his killer was Shurayḥ ibn Abī Awfā:
‘Ḥā Mīm reminds me while the spear is entangled;
why did he not recite Ḥā Mīm before advancing?’
These are verses whose opening is:
‘And a dishevelled man, steadfast through the signs of his Lord,
causing little harm, as the eye can see, a Muslim.’
Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: It is also said that his killer was Kaʿb ibn Mudlij; or Shaddād ibn Muʿāwiyah; or ʿIṣām ibn Muqashʿir; or al-Ashtar; or ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mukaʿbar; and still other names have been given. I have recorded the verses with their attribution to their author in Fatḥ al-Bārī.

records.arabic: بن ثابت بن أبي الأقلح الأنصاري قال بن منده له ذكر في حديث وأبوه صحابي شهير استشهد ببئر معونة وذكر بن القداح أنه شهد بيعة الرضوان وما بعدها وأورد بن منده بسند له أن بن عمر شهد جنازته فكان بين عمودي سريره وذكره بن شاهين عن بن أبي داود فيمن شهد بيعة الرضوان قلت وذلك قبل موت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بنحو ست سنين فكأنه لم يقف على كلام بن أبي داود فإن بيعة الرضوان كانت سنة الهجرة فأقل ما يكون سن من شهدها يزيد على خمس عشرة فهو صحابي لا محالة وإن لم يثبت شهود بيعة الرضوان يكون من أجل تاريخ موت والده أدرك من الحياة النبوية ست سنين أو يزيد وقال بن منده أيضا له ذكر في حديث ثم أورد من طريق عثمان بن عتبة بن عويم بن ساعدة قال كان عبد الله بن عمر شهد محمد بن عاصم بن ثابت بن أبي الأفلح بين عمودي سريره كأني أنظر إلى صفرة لحيته قلت قال بن الأثير استدركه أبو موسى وقد ذكره بن منده ولا وجه لاستدراكه قلت إنما ذكره مضموما إلى خمسة كل منهم اسمه محمد ذكرهم بن شاهين فحكى أبو موسى كلامه لكنه لم ينبه على أن بن عاصم غير داخل في استدراكه
records.english: ibn Thābit ibn Abī al-Aqlaḥ, al-Anṣārī. Ibn Mandah said that he is mentioned in a report. His father was a famous Companion who was martyred at Biʾr Maʿūnah. Ibn al-Qaddāḥ mentioned that Muḥammad witnessed the Pledge of al-Riḍwān and the events thereafter. Ibn Mandah cited with his chain that Ibn ʿUmar attended his funeral and walked between the two side poles of his bier. Ibn Shāhīn mentioned him, from Ibn Abī Dāwūd, among those who witnessed the Pledge of al-Riḍwān. I say: That was about six years before the death of the Prophet ﷺ. It is as though Ibn Mandah did not encounter Ibn Abī Dāwūd’s statement, for the source says the Pledge of al-Riḍwān took place ‘in the year of the Hijra,’ a date that conflicts with its own preceding six-year interval; the youngest age of anyone who witnessed it would exceed fifteen; he would therefore unquestionably be a Companion. Even if his presence at the Pledge of al-Riḍwān is not established, the date of his father’s death means that he lived through six years or more of the prophetic period. Ibn Mandah also said, ‘He is mentioned in a report,’ then cited by way of ʿUthmān ibn ʿUtbah ibn ʿUwaym ibn Sāʿidah, who said: ‘ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar attended the funeral of Muḥammad ibn ʿĀṣim ibn Thābit ibn Abī al-Aflaḥ, walking between the two side poles of his bier. It is as though I can see the yellowness of his beard.’ I say: Ibn al-Athīr said, ‘Abū Mūsā added him as an omission, although Ibn Mandah had already mentioned him, so there is no basis for adding him.’ I say: Ibn Shāhīn mentioned him together with five men, each named Muḥammad. Abū Mūsā reproduced his statement, but did not make clear that Ibn ʿĀṣim was not included among those he was adding.

records.arabic: بن نضلة تقدم نسبه في ترجمة أبيه قال بن القداح سماه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم محمدا وشهد فتح مكة أخرجه بن شاهين عن بن أبي داود عنه
records.english: ibn Naḍlah. His lineage was given earlier in the notice on his father. Ibn al-Qaddāḥ said that the Prophet ﷺ named him Muḥammad and that he witnessed the conquest of Mecca. Ibn Shāhīn transmitted it from Ibn Abī Dāwūd, from him.

records.arabic: الأنصاري الخزرجي ولد رئيس الخزرج المشهور بالنفاق تقدم نسبه في ترجمة أخيه عبد الله بن عبد الله ذكره بن منده في الصحابة وأخرج من طريق راشد الحماني عن ثابت البناني عن محمد بن عبد الله بن أبي بن سلول قال أتانا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال يا معشر الأنصار إن الله عز وجل قد أحسن عليكم الثناء في الطهور فكيف تصنعون قلنا يا رسول الله كان فينا أهل الكتاب فكان أحدهم إذا جاء من الغائط غسل بالماء طرفيه فغسلنا فقال وإن الله أحسن عليكم الثناء الحديث قال بن منده غريب لا يعرف إلا من حديث جعفر بن عبد الله السالمي عن الربيع بن بدر عن جعفر وأن الثلاثة ضعفاء قال وروى من حديث عبد الله بن سلام ومن حديث محمد بن عبد الله بن سلام ورجح أبو نعيم هذه الرواية فقال وهم فيه جعفر والصواب محمد بن عبد الله بن سلام قلت وهو على الاحتمال في تعدد القصة
records.english: al-Anṣārī al-Khazrajī and Khazrajī, son of the leader of the Khazraj who was well known for hypocrisy. His lineage was given earlier in the notice on his brother ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh. Ibn Mandah mentioned him among the Companions and transmitted by way of Rāshid al-Ḥimmānī, from Thābit al-Bunānī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl, who said: ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ came to us and said, “O company of the Anṣār, God ﷿ has praised you highly regarding purification. What do you do?” We said, “O Messenger of God, there were People of the Book among us. Whenever one of them returned from relieving himself, he washed his private parts with water, so we washed likewise.” He said, “Indeed, God has praised you highly”’—the report. Ibn Mandah said, ‘It is rare and known only from the report of Jaʿfar ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Sālimī, from al-Rabīʿ ibn Badr, from Jaʿfar; all three are weak.’ He said: It is also narrated as a report of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and as a report of Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām. Abū Nuʿaym preferred this latter version, saying, ‘Jaʿfar erred in it; the correct person is Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām.’ I say: It remains possible that the incident occurred more than once.

names.arabic: محمد بن عبد الله بن أبي
names.english: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy

title.arabic: محمد بن عبد الله بن أبي
title.english: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy

records.arabic: الأسدي تقدم نسبه في ترجمة أبيه وهو بن أخي زينب أم المؤمنين ولأمه فاطمة بنت أبي حبيش صحبة وذكر الواقدي أنه ولد قبل الهجرة بخمس سنين وحكاه الطبري فقال فيما قيل قال البخاري له صحبة وقال بن حبان سمع من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأخرج الزبير بن بكار من طريق محمد بن أبي يحيى حدثني أبو كثير مولى محمد بن عبد الله بن جحش وكانت له صحبة فذكر الحديث في التشديد في الدين وفي فضل الجماع وأخرجه أحمد وابن أبي خيثمة والبغوي وغيرهم وفي رواية بعضهم كنا جلوسا في موضع الجنائز مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وصرح بعضهم بقوله سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ومداره على العلاء بن عبد الرحمن عن أبي كثير مولى محمد بن عبد الله بن جحش عنه وأخرج حديثه في ستر العورة أحمد والنسائي وابن ماجة وعلقه البخاري وصححه الحاكم وقال بن سعد يكنى أبا عبد الله قتل أبوه بأحد فأوصى به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فاشترى له مالا بخيبر وأقطعه دارا بالمدينة وأخرج البغوي من طريق علي بن زيد عن أنس عن سعيد بن المسيب أن عمر كتب أبناء المهاجرين ممن شهد بدرا في أربعة آلاف منهم محمد بن عبد الله بن جحش
records.english: al-Asadī. His lineage was given earlier in the notice on his father. He was the nephew of Zaynab, Mother of the Believers. His mother, Fāṭimah bint Abī Ḥubaysh, had companionship. Al-Wāqidī mentioned that he was born five years before the Hijra. Al-Ṭabarī related this with the qualification ‘according to what is said.’ Al-Bukhārī said that he had companionship, and Ibn Ḥibbān said that he heard from the Prophet ﷺ. Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār transmitted by way of Muḥammad ibn Abī Yaḥyā: Abū Kathīr, client of Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh—and he had companionship—related to me; he then cited the report concerning the stern warning about debt and the merit of intercourse. Aḥmad, Ibn Abī Khaythamah, al-Baghawī, and others transmitted it. In one version: ‘We were sitting in the place for funerals with the Messenger of God ﷺ.’ Some of them state explicitly, ‘I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ.’ It turns on al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Kathīr, client of Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh, from him. Aḥmad, al-Nasāʾī, and Ibn Mājah transmitted his report on covering the private parts; al-Bukhārī cited it without a full chain, and al-Ḥākim declared it sound. Ibn Saʿd said that his kunya was Abū ʿAbd Allāh. His father was killed at Uḥud and entrusted him to the Prophet ﷺ, who bought him property at Khaybar and allotted him a house in Medina. Al-Baghawī transmitted by way of ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Anas, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, that ʿUmar enrolled the sons of the Emigrants whose fathers had witnessed Badr at a stipend of four thousand, including Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh.

names.arabic: محمد بن عبد الله بن جحش
names.english: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh

title.english: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh

records.arabic: المذحجي ثم الحكمي ذكر الزبير بن بكار أن أمه آمنة بنت عفان أخت عثمان وأمها أروى بنت كريز أسلمتا معا وسيأتي ذكرهما ولم يذكروا عبد الله في الصحابة فكأنه مات قبل الفتح فيكون ابنه من أهل هذا القسم أو الذي بعده
records.english: al-Madhḥijī, then al-Ḥakamī. Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār mentioned that his mother was Āminah bint ʿAffān, sister of ʿUthmān, and that her mother was Arwā bint Kurayz. The two women embraced Islam together, and they will be mentioned later. They did not list ʿAbd Allāh among the Companions, so it is as though he died before the Conquest; his son would therefore belong to this section or the following one.

names.arabic: محمد بن عبد الله بن أبي سعد
names.english: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Saʿd

title.arabic: محمد بن عبد الله بن أبي سعد
title.english: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Saʿd

records.arabic: بن الحارث الإسرائيلي ذكره البخاري في الصحابة وقال بن حبان يقال له صحبة وقال بن شاهين قال بن أبي داود روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حديثا وقال بن منده رأى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وسمع منه وقال أبو عمر له رؤية ورواية محفوظة وأخرج أحمد والبخاري في تاريخه وأبو بكر بن أبي شيبة وابن قانع والبغوي والطبراني وابن منده من طريق مالك بن مغول عن سيار عن شهر بن حوشب عن محمد بن عبد الله بن سلام قال قدم علينا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال ما الذي أثنى الله عليكم فيه رجال يحبون أن يتطهروا قال نستنجي بالماء وأخرجه البغوي عن أبي هشام الرفاعي عن يحيى بن آدم عن مالك بن مغول كذلك لكن قال فيه لا أعلمه إلا عن أبيه قال أبو هشام وكتبته من أصل كتاب يحيى بن آدم ليس فيه عن أبيه وقال البغوي حدث به الفريابي عن مالك بن مغول عن سيار عن شهر عن محمد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يذكر أباه وقال بن منده رواه داود بن أبي هند عن شهر مرسلا لم يذكر محمدا ولا أباه ورواه سلمة بن رجاء عن مالك بن مغول فزاد فيه عن أبيه وقال أبو زرعة الرازي الصحيح عندنا عن محمد ليس فيه عن أبيه والله أعلم
records.english: ibn al-Ḥārith, al-Isrāʾīlī Israelite. Al-Bukhārī mentioned him among the Companions. Ibn Ḥibbān said, ‘He is said to have had companionship.’ Ibn Shāhīn said: Ibn Abī Dāwūd said, ‘He narrated a report from the Prophet ﷺ.’ Ibn Mandah said that he saw the Prophet ﷺ and heard from him. Abū ʿUmar said that he had a sighting and a preserved narration. Aḥmad, al-Bukhārī in his History, Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn Qāniʿ, al-Baghawī, al-Ṭabarānī, and Ibn Mandah transmitted by way of Mālik ibn Mighwal, from Sayyār, from Shahr ibn Ḥawshab, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, who said: ‘The Prophet ﷺ came to us and said, “What is the practice for which God praised you in the words, ‘men who love to purify themselves’?” They replied: “We cleanse ourselves with water.”’ Al-Baghawī transmitted it from Abū Hishām al-Rifāʿī, from Yaḥyā ibn Ādam, from Mālik ibn Mighwal in the same way, but he said in it, ‘I know it only as being from his father.’ Abū Hishām said, ‘I copied it from the original book of Yaḥyā ibn Ādam, and it does not contain “from his father.”’ Al-Baghawī said: Al-Firyābī related it from Mālik ibn Mighwal, from Sayyār, from Shahr, from Muḥammad, from the Prophet ﷺ, without mentioning his father. Ibn Mandah said: Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind narrated it from Shahr in disconnected form, mentioning neither Muḥammad nor his father. Salamah ibn Rajāʾ narrated it from Mālik ibn Mighwal and added ‘from his father.’ Abū Zurʿah al-Rāzī said, ‘The sound version according to us is from Muḥammad, without “from his father.”’ والله أعلم

names.arabic: محمد بن عبد الله بن سلام
names.english: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām

title.arabic: محمد بن عبد الله بن سلام
title.english: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām

records.arabic: غير منسوب ذكره الباوردي وأورد له من طريق حماد بن سلمة عن إسحاق بن عبد الله بن أبي طلحة عن محمد بن عبد الله أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رأى امرأة تأكل بشمالها فقال لا تأكلي بها ولا تشربي بها وهذا يحتمل أن يكون ولد بن سلام
records.english: with no lineage given. Al-Bāwardī mentioned him and cited for him by way of Ḥammād ibn Salamah, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Ṭalḥah, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh, that the Messenger of God ﷺ saw a woman eating with her left hand and said, ‘Do not eat with it or drink with it.’ This may be the son of Ibn Salām.

records.arabic: الأنصاري ذكر بن القداح أنه شهد بيعة الرضوان والمشاهد بعدها وكان في الحرس يوم بني قريظة وأورده بن شاهين عن بن أبي داود عنه
records.english: al-Anṣārī. Ibn al-Qaddāḥ mentioned that he witnessed the Pledge of al-Riḍwān and the expeditions thereafter, and that he was among the guard on the day of Banū Qurayẓah. Ibn Shāhīn included him from Ibn Abī Dāwūd, from Ibn al-Qaddāḥ.

names.arabic: محمد بن عبد الله بن مجدعة
names.english: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Majdaʿah

title.arabic: محمد بن عبد الله بن مجدعة
title.english: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Majdaʿah

records.arabic: بن جبر الأنصاري أبوه مشهور في الصحابة وأما هو فذكره بن منده فقال ذكره بن منيع والحديث عن أبيه كذا اختصره وأشار إلى ما أخرجه البغوي من طريق محمد بن طلحة التيمي عن محمد بن أبي عبس بن جبر عن أبيه عن جده قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من لي بابن الأشرف فقال محمد بن سلمة أنا الحديث في قصة قتل كعب بن الأشرف وأشار بن منده إلى أن الضمير في قوله عن جده لأبي عبس بن محمد فيكون الحديث لأبي عبس بن جبر لا لولده محمد ولكن قد ذكره بن شاهين عن بن أبي داود عن بن القداح أن محمدا شهد بيعة الرضوان والمشاهد بعدها
records.english: ibn Jabr, al-Anṣārī. His father is well known among the Companions. As for him, Ibn Mandah mentioned him, saying, ‘Ibn Manīʿ mentioned him, but the report belongs to his father.’ This is how he abridged it, alluding to what al-Baghawī transmitted by way of Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥah al-Taymī, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿAbs ibn Jabr, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said, ‘Who will deal with Ibn al-Ashraf?’ Muḥammad ibn Salamah replied, ‘I will’—the report concerning the killing of Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf. Ibn Mandah indicated that the pronoun in ‘from his grandfather’ belongs to Abū ʿAbs ibn Muḥammad. The report would thus belong to Abū ʿAbs ibn Jabr, not to his son Muḥammad. Yet Ibn Shāhīn mentioned him from Ibn Abī Dāwūd, from Ibn al-Qaddāḥ, stating that Muḥammad witnessed the Pledge of al-Riḍwān and the expeditions thereafter.

records.arabic: بن الحارث بن المطلب بن عبد مناف القرشي المطلبي كان أبوه من السابقين وقد تقدم وهو أحد الثلاثة الذين بارزوا يوم بدر ومات من الضربة التي ضربها يومئذ فأما محمد فذكره البلاذري وغيره في أولاد عبيدة
records.english: ibn al-Ḥārith ibn al-Muṭṭalib ibn ʿAbd Manāf, al-Qurashī al-Muṭṭalibī and Muṭṭalibī. His father, who was among the foremost early converts, was treated earlier. He was one of the three men who engaged in single combat on the day of Badr and died from the blow he received that day. As for Muḥammad, al-Balādhurī and others mentioned him among ʿUbaydah’s children.

records.arabic: بن بشر بن عبيد بن دهمان بن يسار بن مالك بن حطيط الثقفي ذكر الزبير بن بكار أن أمه ريحانة بنت أبي العاص بن أمية بن أخت الحكم والد مروان ولم أر لوالده ذكرا في الصحابة وكأنه مات قبل الفتح وأسلمت أمه فلذلك سمي محمدا وقد تقدم محمد بن عبد الله بن أبي سعد المذحجي وقصته تشبه هذه القصة وأم هذا خالة أم ذاك
records.english: ibn Bishr ibn ʿUbayd ibn Dahmān ibn Yasār ibn Mālik ibn Ḥuṭayṭ, al-Thaqafī. Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār mentioned that his mother was Rayḥānah bint Abī al-ʿĀṣ ibn Umayyah, niece of al-Ḥakam, Marwān’s father. I have not seen his father mentioned among the Companions. It is as though he died before the Conquest and Muḥammad’s mother embraced Islam, for which reason he was named Muḥammad. Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Saʿd al-Madhḥijī and his similar story were given above. This man’s mother was the maternal aunt of that man’s mother.

records.arabic: بن ربيعة بن سواءة بن جشم بن سعد المنقري ذكره بن سعد والبغوي والباوردي وابن السكن وغيرهم في الصحابة وقال بن سعد عداده في أهل الكوفة وقال بن شاهين له صحبة وأورد من طريق العلاء بن ال فضل بن أبي سوية المنقري حدثني أبي الفضل بن عبد الملك عن أبيه عبد الملك بن أبي سوية عن أبيه أبي سوية عن أبيه خليفة بن عبدة المنقري قال سألت محمد بن عدي بن ربيعة كيف سماك أبوك في الجاهلة محمدا قال أما إني سألت أبي عما سألتني عنه فقال خرجت رابع أربعة من بني تميم أنا أحدهم وسفيان بن مجاشع ويزيد بن عمرو بن ربيعة بن حرقوص بن مازن وأسامة بن مالك بن جندب بن العنبر نريد بن جفنة الغساني بالشام فلما وردنا بالشام ونزلنا على غدير وعليه سمرات وقربه قائم الديراني فقلنا لو اغتسلنا من هذا الماء وادهنا ولبسنا ثيابنا ثم أتينا صاحبنا ففعلنا فأشرف علينا الديراني فقال إن هذه للغة قوم ما هي بلغة أهل هذا البلد فقلنا نحن قوم من مضر قال من أي المضائر قال قلنا من خندف فقال أما إنه سيبعث منكم وشيكا نبي فسارعوا إليه وخذوا حظكم منه ترشدوا فإنه خاتم النبيين فقلنا ما اسمه قال محمد فلما انصرفنا من عند بن جفنة ولد لكل واحد منا غلام فسماه محمدا لذلك وأخرجه أبو نعيم من طريق أبي بكر بن خزيمة حدثني صالح بن مسمار إملاء حدثنا العلاء بن الفضل قال أبو نعيم وحدثناه عاليا الطبراني حدثنا العلاء قلت هو في المعجم الأوسط ولم يذكره في المعجم الكبير وقد أنكر بن الأثير على بن منده إخراج محمد بن عدي في الصحابة ولا إنكار عليه لأن سياقه يقتضي أن لمحمد بن عدي صحبة بخلاف محمد بن سفيان بن مجاشع فقد أنكر أبو موسى على أبي نعيم ذكره وألزمه بذكر محمد بن أسامة ومحمد بن يزيد بن ربيعة فإنه ليس في حديث أحد منهم أنه بقي إلى العهد النبوي
records.english: ibn Rabīʿah ibn Sawāʾah ibn Jusham ibn Saʿd, al-Minqarī. Ibn Saʿd, al-Baghawī, al-Bāwardī, Ibn al-Sakan, and others mentioned him among the Companions. Ibn Saʿd said that he was counted among the people of Kufa. Ibn Shāhīn said that he had companionship and cited by way of al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Faḍl ibn Abī Suwayyah al-Minqarī: My father al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbd al-Malik related to me, from his father ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī Suwayyah, from his father Abū Suwayyah, from his father Khalīfah ibn ʿAbdah al-Minqarī, who said: I asked Muḥammad ibn ʿAdī ibn Rabīʿah, ‘How did your father name you Muḥammad in the pre-Islamic period?’ He replied, ‘I asked my father the same question you have asked me, and he said: “I set out as one of four men of Banū Tamīm: myself; Sufyān ibn Mujāshiʿ; Yazīd ibn ʿAmr ibn Rabīʿah ibn Ḥurqūṣ ibn Māzin; and Usāmah ibn Mālik ibn Jundab ibn al-ʿAnbar. We intended to visit Ibn Jafnah the Ghassānid in Syria. When we arrived in Syria, we stopped at a pool surrounded by acacia trees, near which a resident monk was standing. We said, ‘If only we were to bathe in this water, apply oil, put on our clothes, and then go to our host.’ We did so. The monk looked down upon us and said, ‘This is surely the speech of a people other than the people of this land.’ We replied, ‘We are a people of Muḍar.’ He asked, ‘From which branch of Muḍar?’ We said, ‘From Khindif.’ He said, ‘A prophet will soon be sent from among you. Hasten to him and take your share from him, and you will be rightly guided, for he is the Seal of the Prophets.’ We asked, ‘What is his name?’ He replied, ‘Muḥammad.’ When we returned from Ibn Jafnah, a boy was born to each of us, and each named his son Muḥammad for that reason.”’ Abū Nuʿaym transmitted it by way of Abū Bakr ibn Khuzaymah: Ṣāliḥ ibn Mismār dictated to me: al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Faḍl related to us. Abū Nuʿaym said, ‘Al-Ṭabarānī also related it to us through a shorter chain: al-ʿAlāʾ related to us.’ I say: It is in al-Muʿjam al-Awsaṭ, though he did not include it in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr. Ibn al-Athīr criticized Ibn Mandah for including Muḥammad ibn ʿAdī among the Companions, but there is no basis for criticizing him, because the form of his account implies that Muḥammad ibn ʿAdī had companionship. This differs from Muḥammad ibn Sufyān ibn Mujāshiʿ: Abū Mūsā criticized Abū Nuʿaym for mentioning him and required him also to mention Muḥammad ibn Usāmah and Muḥammad ibn Yazīd ibn Rabīʿah, since nothing in the report about any of them states that he remained alive into the prophetic period.

records.arabic: بن أحيحة الأنصاري ذكر ذلك البلاذري فيمن سمي محمدا في الجاهلية وقد ذكر أبو موسى عن بعض الحفاظ أنه عده فيمن سمي محمدا قبل البعثة وقد تقدم ذكر محمد بن أحيحة فما أدري هو هذا أو عمه ثم رأيت في رجال الموطأ لأبي عبد الله محمد بن يحيى الحذاء عقب ما نقلته عنه في ترجمة أحيحة بن الجلاح قال ولأحيحة بن يسمى عقبة ولعقبة بن يسمى محمدا ولمحمد بنت هي والدة فضالة بن عبيد الصحابي المشهور ولمحمد بن يسمى المنذر استشهد يوم بئر معونة فالظاهر أن محمد بن عقبة مات قبل الإسلام فالله أعلم
records.english: ibn Uḥayḥah, al-Anṣārī. Al-Balādhurī mentioned him among those named Muḥammad in the pre-Islamic period. Abū Mūsā related from one of the hadith masters that he counted him among those named Muḥammad before the prophetic mission. Muḥammad ibn Uḥayḥah was mentioned earlier, and I do not know whether he is this man or his uncle. Then I saw in Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-Ḥadhdhāʾ’s work on the transmitters of al-Muwaṭṭaʾ, following what I quoted from him in the notice on Uḥayḥah ibn al-Julāḥ: ‘Uḥayḥah had a son named ʿUqbah; ʿUqbah had a son named Muḥammad; Muḥammad had a daughter who was the mother of Faḍālah ibn ʿUbayd, the famous Companion; and Muḥammad had a son named al-Mundhir, who was martyred on the day of Biʾr Maʿūnah.’ It is therefore apparent that Muḥammad ibn ʿUqbah died before Islam. فالله أعلم

records.arabic: القرشي ذكره عبد الغني بن سعيد وقال له صحبة وضبط أباه بضم المهملة وسكون اللام بعدها موحدة وتبعه بن ماكولا وأخرج بن منده من طريق عمرو بن الحارث عن يزيد بن أبي حبيب عن أسلم أبي عمران عن هبيب بموحدتين مصغرا بن مغفل بضم الميم وسكون المعجمة وفاء مكسورة وبعدها لام أنه رأى محمد بن علبة القرشي يجر إزاره فنظر إليه هبيب فقال أما سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول ويل للأعقاب من النار وهذا الحديث صحيح السند وهبيب صحابي معروف بهذا الحديث وأخرجه أحمد من هذا الوجه لكن لفظه عن هبيب أنه رأى محمدا القرشي يجر إزاره فنظر إليه وقال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الحديث كذا عنده سمعت بلفظ المثناة وله فيه قصة أخرجه بن يونس من وجه آخر عن أبي يزيد أن أبا عمران أخبره قال بعثني سلمة بن مخلد إلى صاحب الحبشة فلما حضرت بالباب وجدت هبيب بن مغفل صاحب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ومحمد بن علبة القرشي فأذن لمحمد فقام يجر إزاره فنظر إليه هبيب فقال سمعت فذكره وهكذا أخرجه النسائي من وجه آخر عن يزيد بالحديث دون القصة ولم أر عند أحد ممن أخرجه بلفظ أما سمعت بزيادة أما التي للاستفهام وسمعت بفتح التاء وجوز بعض المؤلفين في الصحابة أنها كانت أنا بنون بدل الميم واعتمد بن منده على الرواية التي وقعت له حيث ذكر محمد بن علبة في الصحابة ولعل ذلك مستند عبد الغني بن سعيد أيضا وأخرج أبو نعيم الحديث من طريق مسند أحمد وقال ظن بعض المتأخرين أن ذكر هبيب لمحمد يقتضي صحبته ولو كان يعد من يجالس صحابيا أو يخالطه الصحابي صحابيا لكثر هذا النوع وتعقبه بن الأثر فأقام عذر بن منده قلت وأبو نعيم لم يتأمل سياق بن منده الذي يؤخذ منه أن لمحمد صحبة وتكلم على السياق الذي وقع من مسند أحمد وهو لا يقتضي ذلك
records.english: al-Qurashī. ʿAbd al-Ghanī ibn Saʿīd mentioned him and said that he had companionship. He vocalized his father’s name with the undotted letter vowelled u, the lām quiescent, and then a bāʾ; Ibn Mākūlā followed him. Ibn Mandah transmitted by way of ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from Aslam Abū ʿImrān, from Hubayyib—with two bāʾs and in the diminutive—ibn Mughfil—with the mīm vowelled u, the dotted letter quiescent, a fāʾ vowelled i, and then a lām—that he saw Muḥammad ibn ʿUlbā al-Qurashī dragging his lower garment. Hubayyib looked at him and said, ‘Have you not heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say, “Woe from the Fire to the heels”?’ The chain of this report is sound, and Hubayyib is a Companion known through this report. Aḥmad transmitted it by this route, but his wording is: Hubayyib saw Muḥammad al-Qurashī dragging his lower garment, so he looked at him and said, ‘I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ’—the report. In Aḥmad’s version the word is ‘I heard,’ with the letter tāʾ, and the report contains a story. Ibn Yūnus transmitted it by another route from Abū Yazīd: Abū ʿImrān informed him, saying: ‘Salamah ibn Mukhallad sent me to the ruler of Abyssinia. When I arrived at the gate, I found Hubayyib ibn Mughfil, a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ, and Muḥammad ibn ʿUlbā al-Qurashī. Muḥammad was admitted; he rose while dragging his lower garment. Hubayyib looked at him and said, “I heard”—then he cited the report.’ Al-Nasāʾī likewise transmitted the report, without the story, by another route from Yazīd. In none of the versions of those who transmitted it have I seen the wording ‘Have you not heard,’ with the additional interrogative particle and ‘heard’ ending in an open tāʾ. Some authors on the Companions allowed that the word might have been ‘I,’ with a nūn in place of the mīm. Ibn Mandah relied upon the version that reached him when he listed Muḥammad ibn ʿUlbā among the Companions, and perhaps it was also the basis for ʿAbd al-Ghanī ibn Saʿīd. Abū Nuʿaym transmitted the report by way of Aḥmad’s Musnad and said, ‘Some later scholar supposed that Hubayyib’s mentioning Muḥammad entailed that he had companionship. If everyone who sat with a Companion or whom a Companion mixed with were counted as a Companion, this category would become enormous.’ Ibn al-Athīr answered him and established an excuse for Ibn Mandah. I say: Abū Nuʿaym did not examine Ibn Mandah’s wording, from which it can be understood that Muḥammad had companionship; he commented only on the wording found in Aḥmad’s Musnad, which does not entail that.

records.arabic:
بن وائل القرشي السهمي تقدم نسبه في ترجمة أخيه عبد الله ووالده عمرو وذكر العدوي في الأنساب أن محمدا صحب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو صغير وقال بن سعد أمه بلوية وقال بن البرقي اسمها خولة بنت حمزة بن السليل وذكر بن سعد عن الواقدي بأسانيد له أن عثمان لما عزل عمرو بن العاص عن مصر قدم المدينة فجعل يطعن على عثمان فبلغ عثمان فزجره فخرج إلى أرض له بفلسطين فأقام بها إلى أن بلغه قتل عثمان ثم بلغته بيعة علي ثم بلغته وقعة الجمل ومخالفة معاوية فأراد اللحاق به لعلمه أن عليا لا يشركه في أمره فاستشار ولديه عبد الله ومحمدا فأشار عليه عبد الله بأن يتربص حتى ينظر ما يستقر عليه الحال وقال له محمد أنت فارس أبيات العرب فلا أرى أن يجتمع هذا الأمر وليس لك فيه ذكر فقال لعبد الله أشرت علي بما هو خير لي في آخرتي وقال لمحمد أشرت علي بما هو أنبه لي في دنياي ورحل إلى معاوية والقصة طويلة وفيها دلالة على نباهة محمد في ذلك الوقت عند عمرو حتى أهله للمشورة وقال الواقدي والزبير بن بكار شهد صفين مع أبيه وقاتل فيها وأبلى بلاء عظيما وهو القائل
لو شهدت جمل مقامي ومشهدي
بصفين يوما شاب منه الذوائب الأبيات وهي مشهورة وقيل إنها لأخيه عبد الله وقد أخرجها بن عساكر بسنده إلى الزبير ثم بسنده إلى بن شهاب أن محمد بن عمرو بن العاص شهد القتال يوم صفين فذكر قصة فيها الأبيات المذكورة وأخرجها من طريق نصر بن مزاحم عن عمر بن سعيد عن محمد بن عمرو وأخرجها من وجه آخر في ترجمة عبد الله بن عمرو
records.english:
ibn Wāʾil, al-Qurashī al-Sahmī and Sahmī. His lineage was given earlier in the notices on his brother ʿAbd Allāh and his father ʿAmr. Al-ʿAdawī stated in the Genealogies that Muḥammad accompanied the Prophet ﷺ when he was young. Ibn Saʿd said that his mother was a woman of Balī. Ibn al-Barqī said her name was Khawlah bint Ḥamzah ibn al-Salīl. Ibn Saʿd mentioned from al-Wāqidī, through chains of his, that when ʿUthmān removed ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ from Egypt, ʿAmr came to Medina and began criticizing ʿUthmān. This reached ʿUthmān, who rebuked him, so ʿAmr went to an estate of his in Palestine and remained there until news reached him of ʿUthmān’s killing, then of the pledge to ʿAlī, then of the Battle of the Camel and Muʿāwiyah’s opposition. He wished to join Muʿāwiyah because he knew that ʿAlī would not give him a share in his command. He consulted his two sons, ʿAbd Allāh and Muḥammad. ʿAbd Allāh advised him to wait until he saw how matters settled. Muḥammad said to him, ‘You are the champion of the houses of the Arabs. I do not think this affair should be settled without your being mentioned in it.’ He said to ʿAbd Allāh, ‘You advised me to what is better for my hereafter,’ and to Muḥammad, ‘You advised me to what brings me greater prominence in my worldly life.’ He then travelled to Muʿāwiyah; the story is long. It indicates Muḥammad’s standing with ʿAmr at that time, such that he considered him fit for consultation. Al-Wāqidī and al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār said that he witnessed Ṣiffīn with his father, fought there, and distinguished himself greatly. He is the one who said:
‘If Jamal had witnessed my station and the scene I faced
at Ṣiffīn one day, when forelocks turned grey’—
the verses, which are well known. It is also said that they belong to his brother ʿAbd Allāh. Ibn ʿAsākir transmitted them with his chain to al-Zubayr, then with his chain to Ibn Shihāb, stating that Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ witnessed the fighting on the day of Ṣiffīn, followed by a story containing the cited verses. He also transmitted them by way of Naṣr ibn Muzāḥim, from ʿUmar ibn Saʿīd, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr, and transmitted them by another route in the notice on ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr.

records.arabic: والد هبيب الغفاري لم يذكروه وهو على شرط من ذكر محمد بن عقبة المذكور قبل بقليل
records.english: the father of Hubayb al-Ghifārī. They did not mention him, though he meets the criterion applied by whoever mentioned Muḥammad ibn ʿUqbah shortly before.
