records.arabic: والد صفية ذكره الطبراني في الصحابة ولم يخرج له شيئا
records.english: the father of Ṣafiyyah. Al-Tabarani included him among the Companions but transmitted nothing from him.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: والد عباد ذكر بن منده من طريق يعقوب القمي عن عنبسة بن سعيد الرازي عن أبي ليلى عن عباد بن مسلم عن أبيه قال مر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على أبي وقد لزم رجلا في المسجد فذكر الحديث كذا أورده مختصرا
records.english: the father of ʿAbbād. Ibn Mandah mentioned by way of Yaqub al-Qummi, from Anbasah ibn Said al-Razi, from Abu Layla, from Abbad ibn Muslim, from his father, who said: ‘The Prophet ﷺ passed my father while he was detaining a man in the mosque...’ and he related the hadith. This is how he presented it in abridged form.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: والد عوسجة قال بن حبان له صحبة وقال البغوي أحسبه كان بالكوفة حدثنا هارون بن عبد الله حدثنا مهدي بن حفص حدثنا أبو الأحوص عن سليمان بن قرم عن عوسجة عن أبيه مسلم قال سافرت مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فكان يمسح على الخفين قال البغوي لم يسنده غير مهدي وهو خطأ وأخرجه بن أبي خيثمة عن مهدي وابن السكن من طريقه قال البغوي الصواب عن عوسجة عن عبد الله بن مسعود موقوفا وقال بن السكن الصواب من فعل عبد الله وقد رواه عنه مهدي عن أبي الأحوص فقال عن سليمان عن عوسجة عن أبيه قال سافرت مع عبد الله بن مسعود قلت وقد أخرجه الطبراني عن عبد الله بن أحمد بن حنبل عن محمد بن جعفر الوركاني عن أبي الأحوص مثل ما روى مهدي مرفوعا ولفظه رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بال ثم توضأ وسمح على خفيه
records.english: the father of ʿAwsajah. Ibn Hibban said that he had companionship. Al-Baghawi said, ‘I think that he was in Kufa. Harun ibn Abd Allah related to us: Mahdi ibn Hafs related to us: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Sulayman ibn Qarm, from Awsajah, from his father Muslim, who said, “I traveled with the Messenger of God ﷺ, and he used to wipe over his leather socks.”’ Al-Baghawi said that no one but Mahdi gave it a chain to the Prophet, and that this was an error. Ibn Abi Khaythamah transmitted it from Mahdi, and Ibn al-Sakan through Mahdi's route. Al-Baghawi said that the correct version was from Awsajah, from Abd Allah ibn Masud, as a statement of Abd Allah. Ibn al-Sakan said that the correct version described Abd Allah's action. Mahdi himself related it from Abu al-Ahwas as follows: from Sulayman, from Awsajah, from his father, who said, ‘I traveled with Abd Allah ibn Masud.’ I say: al-Tabarani also transmitted it from Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal, from Muhammad ibn Jafar al-Warkani, from Abu al-Ahwas, in the same elevated form that Mahdi related. Its wording is: ‘I saw the Messenger of God ﷺ urinate, then perform ablution and wipe over his leather socks.’

records.arabic: يقال هو اسم أبي الغادية الجهني حكاه البغوي وسيأتي في الكنى ذكر من اسمه مسلمة مفتوح الأول بزيادة هاء
records.english: It is said that this was the name of Abū al-Ghādiyah al-Juhanī. Al-Baghawi related this. Under the kunyahs there will appear a person named Maslamah, with a fathah on the first letter and an added ha.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن حريش بمهملة أوله وآخره معجمة بوزن عظيم بن عدي بن مجدعة بن حارثة الأنصاري ذكره بن عبد البر وقال قتل يوم جسر أبي عبيد
records.english: ibn Ḥarīsh, whose first consonant is unpointed and last is dotted, on the pattern of ʿaẓīm, ibn ʿAdī ibn Majdaʿah ibn Ḥārithah, al-Anṣārī. Ibn Abd al-Barr mentioned him and said that he was killed on the day of the Bridge of Abu Ubayd.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الأنصاري ذكره بن منده وقال عداده في أهل المدينة وأخرج من طريق حبيب بن أبي حبيب عن إبراهيم بن الحصين عن أبيه عن جده عن مسلمة بن قيس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال استشرت جبريل في اليمين مع الشاهد
records.english: al-Anṣārī. Ibn Mandah mentioned him and said that he was counted among the people of Medina. He transmitted by way of Habib ibn Abi Habib, from Ibrahim ibn al-Husayn, from his father, from his grandfather, from Maslamah ibn Qays, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said, ‘I consulted Gabriel concerning an oath accompanied by one witness.’

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن وهب بن ثعلبة بن وائلة بن عمرو بن شيبان بن محارب بن فهر بن مالك الفهري والد حبيب بن مسلمة ذكره المستغفري في الصحابة وأخرج من طريق يحيى بن زكريا بن أبي زائدة عن بن جريج عن بن أبي مليكة أن حبيب بن مسلمة الفهري جاء إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأدركه أبوه فقال يا نبي الله إن ابني يدي ورجلي فقال ارجع معه وأخرجه البغوي في ترجمة حبيب الفهري من طريق داود العطار عن بن جريج ولم يقع في روايته حبي بن مسلمة ففرق بين حبيب بن مسلمة وحبيب الفهري كما بينت ذلك في حرف الحاء وقد أخرجه أبو نعيم من طريق أبي عاصم وحجاج بن محمد كلاهما عن بن جريج وقال فيه حبيب بن مسلمة
records.english: ibn Wahb ibn Thaʿlabah ibn Wāʾilah ibn ʿAmr ibn Shaybān ibn Muḥārib ibn Fihr ibn Mālik, al-Fihrī. The father of Habib ibn Maslamah. Al-Mustaghfiri included him among the Companions and transmitted by way of Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'idah, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, that Habib ibn Maslamah al-Fihri came to the Prophet ﷺ. His father caught up with him and said, ‘O Prophet of God, my son is my hand and my foot.’ He said, ‘Go back with him.’ Al-Baghawi transmitted it in the entry for Habib al-Fihri by way of Dawud al-Attar, from Ibn Jurayj, but ‘Habib ibn Maslamah’ does not appear in his version. He therefore distinguished Habib ibn Maslamah from Habib al-Fihri, as I explained under the letter ha. Abu Nuaym transmitted it by way of Abu Asim and Hajjaj ibn Muhammad, both from Ibn Jurayj, and it says ‘Habib ibn Maslamah.’

records.arabic: بن الصامت بن نيار بن لوذان بن عبد ود بن زيد بن ثعلبة بن الخزرج بن ساعدة الأنصاري الخزرجي ويقال زرقي يكنى أبا سعيد ذكره بن السكن وأبو نعيم وغيرهما في الصحابة قال بن السكن روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أحاديث لا يذكر في شيء منها سماعا كذا قال وقد أخرج أبو نعيم من طريق بن عون عن مكحول قال ركب عقبة بن عامر إلى مسلمة وهو أمير على مصر فقال له تذكر يوم قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من علم من أخيه سبة فسترها ستره الله بها من النار يوم القيامة قال نعم قال فلهذا آخيتك وأخرج أبو نعيم أيضا من طريق وكيع عن موسى بن علي عن أبيه عن مسلمة بن مخلد قال ولدت حين قدم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة وقبض النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأنا بن عشر سنين وكذا رواه أحمد ومع ذلك قال ليست لمسلمة صحبة فلعله أراد الصحبة الخاصة وأخرجه بن الربيع الجيزي من وجهين أحدهما قال فيه مثل هذا والآخر قال قدم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأنا بن أربع سنين ومات وأنا بن أربع عشرة سنة وزاد ولأهل مصر عنه حديثان أحدهما أغروا النساء يلزمن الحجال ولم يصرح فيه بالسماع والثاني أنه ولد سنة الهجرة قال محمد بن الربيع ولي إمرة مصر وهو أول من جمعت له مصر والمغرب وذلك في خلافة معاوية وصدر من خلافة يزيد بن معاوية وتوفي بمصر سنة اثنتين وستين وقال بن الربيع ولي إمرة مصر ليزيد بن معاوية ومات بها وهذا قول بن حبان وابن البرقي وقال الواقدي رجع إلى المدينة ومات بها وذلك سنة اثنتين وستين وقال بن السكن هو أول من جعل على أهل مصر بنيان المنار ومخلد أبو بضم الميم وفتح الخاء العجمة وتشديد اللام وأخرج محمد بن الربيع من طريق ضمام بن إسماعيل عن أبي قبيل قال بعث إلى حنظلة يعني أمير مصر فقال شيخ لو كان في جسدك للسوط موضع لضربتك فقال له أبو قبيل ولم ذاك قال صرت كاهنا تقول الآخر فالآخر شر فقال له أبو قبيل ليس أنا الذي قلت هذا إنما سمعته من مسلمة بن مخلد وقد قال وكان زاد في بعث البحر فكره الجند ذلك وهو على أعوادك هذه يقول يا أهل مصر ما نقمتم مني والله لقد زدت مددكم وعددكم وقوتكم على عدوكم اعلموا أني خير ممن بعدي والآخر فالآخر شر وفي لفظ والذي نفسي بيده لا يأتينكم زمان إلا الآخر فالآخر شر فمن استطاع منكم أن يتخذ نفقا في الأرض فليفعل
records.english: ibn al-Ṣāmit ibn Niyār ibn Lawdhān ibn ʿAbd Wudd ibn Zayd ibn Thaʿlabah ibn al-Khazraj ibn Sāʿidah, al-Anṣārī al-Khazrajī. Also called Zuraqi, had the kunyah Abu Said. Ibn al-Sakan, Abu Nuaym, and others included him among the Companions. Ibn al-Sakan said, ‘He transmitted hadiths from the Prophet ﷺ, but in none of them is hearing explicitly mentioned.’ This is what he said. Abu Nuaym transmitted by way of Ibn Awn, from Makhul, who said: ‘Uqbah ibn Amir rode to Maslamah while he was governor of Egypt and asked him, “Do you remember the day the Messenger of God ﷺ said, ‘Whoever learns of a fault in his brother and conceals it, God will by that conceal him from the Fire on the Day of Resurrection’?” He replied, “Yes.” Uqbah said, “It was for this that I took you as a brother”—the transmitted verb is textually uncertain.’ Abu Nuaym also transmitted by way of Waki, from Musa ibn Ali, from his father, from Maslamah ibn Mukhallad, who said, ‘I was born when the Prophet ﷺ arrived in Medina, and the Prophet ﷺ died when I was ten years old.’ Ahmad related it in the same form. Despite this, he said that Maslamah did not have companionship, perhaps meaning close companionship. Ibn al-Rabi al-Jizi transmitted it through two routes. One says the same, while the other says, ‘The Prophet ﷺ arrived when I was four years old and died when I was fourteen.’ He added: ‘The people of Egypt transmit two hadiths from him. One is, “Urge the women to keep to their curtained chambers,” in which he did not expressly state that he heard it. The second is that he was born in the year of the Emigration.’ Muhammad ibn al-Rabi said: ‘He governed Egypt and was the first man to have both Egypt and the Maghrib combined under his authority. That was during Muawiyah's caliphate and the beginning of Yazid ibn Muawiyah's caliphate. He died in Egypt in the year sixty-two.’ Ibn al-Rabi also said that he governed Egypt for Yazid ibn Muawiyah and died there. This is the view of Ibn Hibban and Ibn al-Barqi. Al-Waqidi said that he returned to Medina and died there in the year sixty-two. Ibn al-Sakan said that he was the first to institute minaret structures for the people of Egypt. The name Mukhlad is followed in the source by a damaged vocalization note containing an unexplained “Abu”; the note then gives a dammah on the mim, a fathah on the dotted kha, and a doubled lam. Muhammad ibn al-Rabi transmitted by way of Damam ibn Ismail, from Abu Qabil, who said: ‘Hanzalah’—meaning the governor of Egypt—‘sent for me and said, “Old man, if there were any place on your body fit for the whip, I would strike you.”’ Abu Qabil asked, ‘Why is that?’ He replied, ‘You have become a soothsayer, saying, “Each successor will be worse than the one before.”’ Abu Qabil said, ‘I am not the one who said this. I heard it from Maslamah ibn Mukhallad, who did say it.’ Maslamah had increased the levy for the naval expedition, which the troops disliked, and he stood upon those timbers and said: ‘People of Egypt, what do you blame me for? By God, I have increased your reinforcements, your numbers, and your strength against your enemy. Know that I am better than those who come after me, and each successor will be worse than the one before.’ In another wording: ‘By Him in whose hand is my soul, no time will come upon you without each successor being worse than the one before. Whoever among you is able to make a tunnel in the earth should do so.’

records.arabic: يقال إنه اسم عبد الرحمن بن المنهال واختلف في اسم ولد عبد الرحمن فقيل مسلمة وقيل غير ذلك وسيأتي بيانه في المبهمات
records.english: It is said to be the name of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Minhāl. There is disagreement over the name of Abd al-Rahman's son: some said Maslamah, while others said something else. Its explanation will appear under the unidentified persons.

records.arabic:
ويقال بن حدان الحداني ذكره الرشاطي وقال له ذكر في خبر عبد الله بن علس ووفد على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد الفتح ومدحه بشعر منه
حلفت برب الراقصات إلى منى
طوالع من بين القصيمة بالركب
بأن رسول الله فينا محمد
له الرأس والقدموس من سلفي كعب
أتانا ببرهان من الله قابس
أضاء به الرحمن من ظلمة الكرب
أعز به الأنصار لما تقارنت
صدور العوالي في الحنادس والضرب وكذا أورد له المرزباني في هذه الأبيات
records.english:
also said to be Ibn Ḥaddān al-Ḥaddānī. Al-Rushati mentioned him and said that he appeared in the report of Abd Allah ibn Ulas. He came in a delegation to the Prophet ﷺ after the Conquest and praised him in poetry, including:

‘I swore by the Lord of the she-camels journeying to Mina,
ascending among the caravan from al-Qusaymah,
that the Messenger of God among us, Muhammad,
has the chief place and primacy among the forebears of Kab.
He came to us with a luminous proof from God;
the Most Merciful lit by it the darkness of distress.
Through him He strengthened the Ansar when the tips
of the spears drew close in darkness and combat.’

Al-Marzubani likewise cited these verses for him.

records.arabic: غير منسوب شهد في أمان أهل نجران الذي كتب لهم أبو بكر الصديق عقب وفاة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وذكر ذلك سيف عن طلحة الأعلم عن عكرمة واستدركه بن فتحون
records.english: with no lineage given. He witnessed the grant of security that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq wrote for the people of Najran immediately after the death of the Prophet ﷺ. Sayf mentioned this from Talhah al-Alam, from Ikrimah. Ibn Fathun supplied this omitted entry.

records.arabic: بن نوفل بن أهيب بن زهرة بن كلاب بن مرة بن كعب بن لؤي القرشي الزهري قال مصعب الزبيري يكنى أبا عبد الرحمن وأمه عاتكة بنت عوف أخت عبد الرحمن ممن أسملت وهاجرت قال يحيى بن بكير وكان مولده بعد الهجرة بسنتين وقدم المدينة في ذي الحجة بعد الفتح سنة ثمان وهو غلام أيفع بن ست سنين قال البغوي حفظ من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أحاديث أخرجه البغوي وحديثه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في خطبة علي بنت أبي جهل في الصحيحين وغيرهما ووقع في بعض طرقه عند مسلم سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأنا محتلم وهذا يدل على أنه ولد قبل الهجرة ولكنهم أطبقوا على أنه ولد بعدها وقد تأول بعضهم أن قوله محتلم من الحلم بالكسر لا من الحلم بالضم يريد أنه كان عاقلا ضابطا لما يتحمله وقال مصعب كان يلزم عمر بن الخطاب وقال الزبير كان من أهل الفضل والدين وأخرج البغوي من طريق أم بكر بنت المسور عن أبيها قال مر بي يهودي والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يتوضأ وأنا خلفه فرفع ثوبه فإذا خاتم النبوة في ظهره فقال لي اليهودي ارفع رداءه عن ظهره فذهب أفعل فنضج في وجهي كفا من ماء ومن طريق عثمان بن حكيم عن أبي أمامة بن سهل عن المسور أقبلت بحجر أحمله ثقيل وعلي إزار خفيف فانحل فلم أستطع أن أضع الحجر حتى بلغت به موضعة فقال لي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ارجع إلى ثوبك فخذه ولا تمشوا عراة وروى المسور أيضا عن الخلفاء الأربعة وعمرو بن عوف القرشي والمغيرة وغيرهم روى عنه أيضا سعيد بن المسيب وعلي بن الحسين وعوف بن الطفيل وعروة وآخرون وكان مع خاله عبد الرحمن بن عوف ليالي الشورى وحفظ عنه أشياء ثم كان مع بن الزبير فلما كان الحصار الأول أصابه حجر من حجارة المنجنيق فمات وكذا قال يحيى بن بكير وزاد أصابه وهو يصلي فأقام خمسة أيام ومات يوم أتى نعي يزيد بن معاوية سنة أربع وستين وكذا أخرجه أبو مسهر ونقل الطبري عن بن معين أنه مات سنة ثلاث وسبعين وتعقبه بأنه غلط لأنهم اتفقوا على أنه مات في حصار بن الزبير أصابه حجر من المنجنيق والمراد به الحصار الأول من الجيش الذي أرسله يزيد بن معاوية وكان ذلك سنة أربع أو خمس وستين وأما سنة ثلاث وسبعين فكان الحصار من الحجاج وفيه قتل بن الزبير ولم يبق المسور إلى هذا الزمان
records.english: ibn Nawfal ibn Uhayb ibn Zuhrah ibn Kilāb ibn Murrah ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy, al-Qurashī al-Zuhrī. Musab al-Zubayri said that his kunyah was Abu Abd al-Rahman. His mother was Atikah bint Awf, the sister of Abd al-Rahman, one of the women who embraced Islam and emigrated. Yahya ibn Bukayr said that he was born two years after the Emigration and came to Medina in Dhu al-Hijjah after the Conquest, in the year eight, as a boy approaching puberty who was six years old. Al-Baghawi said that he memorized hadiths from the Prophet ﷺ. Al-Baghawi transmitted from him, and his report from the Prophet ﷺ concerning Ali's proposal to the daughter of Abu Jahl appears in the two Sahihs and elsewhere. In one of its routes in Muslim the wording is, ‘I heard the Prophet ﷺ while I was muhtalim.’ This indicates that he was born before the Emigration, although the authorities agree that he was born after it. Some interpreted muhtalim as deriving from hilm with a kasrah, not hulm with a dammah, meaning that he was rational and accurately retained what he received. Musab said that he remained close to Umar ibn al-Khattab. Al-Zubayr said that he was a man of merit and religion. Al-Baghawi transmitted by way of Umm Bakr bint al-Miswar, from her father, who said: ‘A Jew passed by me while the Prophet ﷺ was performing ablution and I was behind him. He lifted his garment, and the Seal of Prophethood was on his back. The Jew told me, “Lift his mantle from his back.” As I was about to do so, he splashed a handful of water in my face.’ He also transmitted by way of Uthman ibn Hakim, from Abu Umamah ibn Sahl, from al-Miswar: ‘I came carrying a heavy stone while wearing a light waist-wrapper. It came undone, but I could not put down the stone until I had carried it to its place. The Prophet ﷺ said to me, “Go back to your garment and take it; do not walk naked.”’ Al-Miswar also related from the four caliphs, Amr ibn Awf al-Qurashi, al-Mughirah, and others. Said ibn al-Musayyab, Ali ibn al-Husayn, Awf ibn al-Tufayl, Urwah, and others related from him. He was with his maternal uncle Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf during the nights of the consultative council and preserved a number of reports from him. He later sided with Ibn al-Zubayr. During the first siege, he was struck by a stone from a catapult and died. Yahya ibn Bukayr said the same and added that the stone struck him while he was praying. He remained alive for five days and died on the day news arrived of Yazid ibn Muawiyah's death, in the year sixty-four. Abu Mushir likewise transmitted this. Al-Tabari reported from Ibn Main that he died in the year seventy-three, but objected that this was an error, because the authorities agreed that he died during the siege of Ibn al-Zubayr after being struck by a catapult stone. This means the first siege, by the army sent by Yazid ibn Muawiyah, in the year sixty-four or sixty-five. The siege in the year seventy-three was conducted by al-Hajjaj, during which Ibn al-Zubayr was killed; al-Miswar did not live until that time.

records.arabic: والد عبد الله ذكره أبو نعيم وأخرج من طريق أشهب بن عبد العزيز عن بن لهيعة عن بن محيريز عن عبد الله بن المسور عن أبيه قال قال رسول صلى الله عليه وسلم وجب عليكم الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر ما لم تخافوا أن يؤتى إليكم مثل الذي نهيتم عنه فإذا خفتم ذلك فقد حل لكم الصمت قال أبو نعيم كذا قال ولا نعرف لابن لهيعة عن بن محيريز شيئا
records.english: the father of ʿAbd Allāh. Abu Nuaym mentioned him and transmitted by way of Ashhab ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Ibn Lahiah, from Ibn Muhayriz, from Abd Allah ibn al-Miswar, from his father, who said: The Messenger ﷺ said, ‘Commanding what is right and forbidding what is wrong are incumbent upon you so long as you do not fear that the very thing you forbade will be brought upon you. If you fear that, silence has become lawful for you.’ Abu Nuaym said, ‘This is how he related it, but we know of nothing transmitted by Ibn Lahiah from Ibn Muhayriz.’

records.arabic: بضم أوله وفتح السن وتشديد الواو ضبطه عبد الغني بن سعيد وابن ماكولا وأورده البخاري مع المسور بن مخرمة فاقتضى أنه مثله وهو بن يزيد الأسدي ثم المالكي قال البغوي من بني مالك روى حديثه يحيى بن كثير عنه قال شهدت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ في الصلاة فترك شيئا فقيل له لما سلم قال فهلا أذكرتنيها قال كنت أراها نسخت أخرجه أبو داود في السنن
records.english: with its first letter bearing ḍammah, an open sīn, and a geminated wāw. Abd al-Ghani ibn Said and Ibn Makula vocalized it this way. Al-Bukhari placed him with al-Miswar ibn Makhramah, implying that his name was vocalized in the same manner. He was Ibn Yazid al-Asadi, then al-Maliki. Al-Baghawi said that he was of Banu Malik. Yahya ibn Kathir related his hadith from him: ‘I was present when the Messenger of God ﷺ was reciting in prayer and omitted something. After he had concluded, someone mentioned it to him. He said, “Why did you not remind me of it?” The man replied, “I thought it had been abrogated.”’ Abu Dawud transmitted it in the Sunan.

records.arabic: بن أبي وهب بن عمرو بن عائذ بن عمران بن محزوم القرشي المخزومي والد سعيد له ولأبيه حزن صحبة وله حديث في الصحيحين من طريق طارق بن عبد الرحمن قال انطلقت حاجا فمررت بقوم يصلون قلت ما هذا المسجد قالوا هذه الشجرة حيث بايع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بيعة الرضوان فلقيت سعيد بن المسيب فأخبرني فقال سعيد حدثني أبي أنه كان ممن بايع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم تحت الشجرة فلما خرجنا من العام المقبل أتيناها فلم نقدر عليها قال سعيد إن أصحاب محمد لم يعلموها فعلمتموها أنتم فأنتم أعلم وقد تقدم ذكره في حديث والده حزن بن أبي وهب وللمسيب حديث آخر في الصحيحين وغيرهما في قصة وفاة أبي طالب وفي كل ذلك رد لقول مصعب الزبيري لا يختلف أصحابنا أن المسيب وأباه من مسلمة الفتح وقد رد كلامه بذلك أبو أحمد العسكري وقد شهد المسيب فتوح الشام ولم يتحرر لي متى مات
records.english: ibn Abī Wahb ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿĀʾidh ibn ʿImrān ibn Maḥzūm, al-Qurashī al-Makhzūmī. The father of Said. Both he and his father Hazn had companionship. He has a hadith in the two Sahihs by way of Tariq ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said: ‘I set out for the pilgrimage and passed people praying. I asked, “What is this mosque?” They replied, “This is the tree at which the Messenger of God ﷺ accepted the Pledge of al-Ridwan.” I met Said ibn al-Musayyab and informed him. Said said, “My father related to me that he was among those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God ﷺ beneath the tree. When we went out the following year, we came to it but could not identify it.” Said said, “The Companions of Muhammad did not know it, yet you know it? Then you know better!”’ He was mentioned earlier in the hadith of his father Hazn ibn Abi Wahb. Al-Musayyab has another hadith in the two Sahihs and elsewhere concerning the death of Abu Talib. All of this refutes Musab al-Zubayri's statement, ‘Our authorities do not disagree that al-Musayyab and his father were among those who embraced Islam at the Conquest.’ Abu Ahmad al-Askari refuted his statement on this basis. Al-Musayyab was present at the conquests of Syria. I have not been able to establish when he died.

records.arabic: بن عبد الله بن عابد بموحدة بن عمر بن مخزوم القرشي المخزومي أخو السائب ذكره الزبير بن بكار ونقل عن أبي معشر أنه أسلم وهاجر مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من الحديبية وكان ابنه عبد الله ممن قاتل يوم الدار
records.english: ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀbid—with a bāʾ—ibn ʿUmar ibn Makhzūm, al-Qurashī al-Makhzūmī. The brother of al-Sa'ib. Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar mentioned him and reported from Abu Mashar that he embraced Islam and emigrated with the Prophet ﷺ from al-Hudaybiyyah. His son Abd Allah was among those who fought on the Day of the House.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكره أبو موسى في الذيل وحكى عن مقاتل بن سليمان أنه ذكره في تفسير سورة والعاديات وقال إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعثه في سرية إلى حي من بني كنانة وأمره عليهم وكان أحد النقباء فغابت السرية ولم يأت خبرها فقال المنافقون قتلوا جميعا فنزلت والعاديات ضبحا
records.english: Abū Mūsā mentioned him in the Supplement. And related from Muqatil ibn Sulayman that he mentioned him in his commentary on Surat al-Adiyat. He said that the Prophet ﷺ sent him at the head of an expedition against a clan of Banu Kinanah and appointed him its commander. He was one of the chiefs. The expedition was absent and no news of it arrived, so the hypocrites said, ‘They have all been killed.’ Then the words ‘By the charging steeds, panting’ were revealed.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بكسر أوله وسكون المعجمة وفتح الراء بعدها مهملة الأشعري قال البغوي ذكره البخاري في الصحابة وأخرج بن أبي عاصم وابن السكن وغيرهما من طريق سلمة بن وهرام حدثتني ميل بنت مشرح الأشعرية أن أباها مشرحا وكان من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قص أظفاره فجمعها ثم دقتها ثم قال هكذا رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وفي سنده محمد بن سليمان بن مسمول وهو ضعيف جدا وأخرجه البيهقي في أواخر الباب الأربعين من شعب الإيمان من هذا الوجه وقال بن السكن لم يرو عنه غيره
records.english: with its first letter bearing kasrah, the dotted consonant quiescent, an open rāʾ, then an unpointed consonant; al-Ashʿarī. Al-Baghawi said that al-Bukhari listed him among the Companions. Ibn Abi Asim, Ibn al-Sakan, and others transmitted by way of Salamah ibn Wahram: Mayl bint Musharrih al-Ashariyyah related to me that her father Musharrih, one of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, clipped his nails, gathered them, and then crushed them. He said, ‘This is how I saw the Messenger of God ﷺ do it.’ The chain contains Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn Masmul, who is very weak. Al-Bayhaqi transmitted it through this route at the end of the fortieth chapter of Shuab al-Iman. Ibn al-Sakan said that no one else related from him.

records.arabic: بضم أوله وفتح الشين المعجمة وسكون الميم وكسر الراء بعدها جيم بن خالد السعدي جد علي بن جحر المحدث المشهور قال بن حبان له صحبة وأخرج بن السكن عن الحسين بن إسماعيل الفارسي عن حاتم بن عبد الله بن عبدة عن علي بن حجر بن إياس بن مقاتل بن مشمرج حدثنا أبي عن أبيه إياس عن جده المشمرج قال قدمت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في وفد عبد القيس فسألهم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم هل فيكم غيركم قالوا لا غير بن أختنا قال بن أخت القوم منهم ثم كساه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بردا وأقطعه ركى ماء بالبادية وكتب له بها كتابا
records.english: with its first letter bearing ḍammah, an open dotted shīn, a quiescent mīm, a rāʾ bearing kasrah, then jīm; ibn Khālid al-Saʿdī, the grandfather of ʿAlī ibn Ḥujr, the well-known traditionist. Ibn Hibban said that he had companionship. Ibn al-Sakan transmitted from al-Husayn ibn Ismail al-Farisi, from Hatim ibn Abd Allah ibn Abdah, from Ali ibn Hujr ibn Iyas ibn Muqatil ibn Mushamrij: my father related to us, from his father Iyas, from his grandfather Mushamrij, who said, ‘I came to the Messenger of God ﷺ with the delegation of Abd al-Qays. The Prophet ﷺ asked them, “Is there anyone among you who is not one of you?” They said, “No one except our sister's son.” He said, “A people's sister's son is one of them.” The Messenger of God ﷺ then clothed him in a mantle, granted him a watering well in the desert, and wrote him a document for it.’

records.arabic: بن عثمان الحجبي تقدم ذكره في مسلم بن شيبة
records.english: ibn ʿUthmān, al-Ḥajabī. He was mentioned earlier under Muslim ibn Shaybah.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن هاشم بن عبد مناف بن عبد الدار بن قصي بن كلاب العبدري أحد السابقين إلى الإسلام يكنى أبا عبد الله قال أبو عمر أسلم قديما والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في دار الأرقم وكتم إسلامه خوفا من أمه وقومه فعلمه عثمان بن طلحة فأعلم أهله فأوثقوه فلم يزل محبوسا إلى أن هرب مع من هاجر إلى الحبشة ثم رجع إلى مكة فهاجر إلى المدينة وشهد بدرا ثم شهد أحدا ومعه اللواء فاستشهد وذكر محمد بن إسحاق عن صالح بن كيسان عن بعض آل سعد عن بن أبي وقاص قال كان مصعب بن عمير أنعم غلام بمكة وأجوده حلة مع أبويه وأخرج الترمذي بسند فيه ضعف عن علي قال رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مصعب بن عمير فبكى للذي كان فيه من النعمة ولما صار إليه وفي الصحيح عن حبان أن مصعبا لم يترك إلا ثوبا فكان إذا غطوا رأسه خرجت رجلاه وإذا غطوا رجليه خرج رأسه فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم اجعلوا على رجله شيئا من الإذخر وقال بن إسحاق في المغازي عن يزيد بن أبي حبيب لما انصرف الناس عن القعبة بعث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم معهم مصعب بن عمير يفقههم وكان مصعب هاجر إلى الحبشة الهجرة الأولى ثم رجع إلى مكة ثم هاجر إلى المدينة وفي صحيح البخاري عن البراء أول من قدم علينا مصعب بن عمير وابن أم مكتوم الحديث وزاد أبو داود من هذا الوجه الهجرة الأولى
records.english: ibn Hāshim ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn ʿAbd al-Dār ibn Quṣayy ibn Kilāb, al-ʿAbdarī. One of the earliest to embrace Islam, had the kunyah Abu Abd Allah. Abu Umar said that he embraced Islam early, while the Prophet ﷺ was in the house of al-Arqam. He concealed his Islam for fear of his mother and his people. Uthman ibn Talhah learned of it and informed his family, who bound him. He remained imprisoned until he escaped with those who emigrated to Abyssinia. He then returned to Mecca, emigrated to Medina, was present at Badr, and was later present at Uhud carrying the banner, where he was martyred. Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned from Salih ibn Kaysan, from one of the family of Sad, from Ibn Abi Waqqas, who said that Musab ibn Umayr was the most pampered young man in Mecca and the best dressed while with his parents. Al-Tirmidhi transmitted with a weak chain from Ali, who said that the Messenger of God ﷺ saw Musab ibn Umayr and wept over the luxury he had once enjoyed and the condition to which he had come. In the Sahih, from Hibban, it is related that Musab left nothing but a cloth. When they covered his head, his feet protruded, and when they covered his feet, his head protruded. The Messenger of God ﷺ said, ‘Place some idhkhir grass over his feet.’ Ibn Ishaq said in al-Maghazi, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib: ‘When the people departed from a place whose damaged name is transmitted as al-Qaʿbah, with the intended location remaining uncertain, the Prophet ﷺ sent Musab ibn Umayr with them to instruct them in religion.’ Musab had emigrated to Abyssinia in the first emigration, then returned to Mecca and emigrated to Medina. In Sahih al-Bukhari, from al-Bara: ‘The first to come to us were Musab ibn Umayr and Ibn Umm Maktum,’ to the end of the hadith. Abu Dawud added through this route, ‘the first emigration.’

records.arabic: بن امرأة الجلاس تقدم في عمير بن سعد
records.english: the son of the wife of al-Jallās. He appeared earlier under Umayr ibn Sad.

records.arabic: ذكره البغوي والطبراني وأخرج من طريق جرير بن حازم عن عبد الملك بن عمير عن مصعب الأسلمي قال انطلق غلام منا حتى أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال أسألك أن تجعلني ممن تشفع له فقال أعني بكثرة السجود وأخرجه البزار عن طالوت بن عباد عن جرير فقال عن عبد الملك كان بالمدينة غلام يكنى أبا مصعب فذكر الحديث مطولا وقال لا نعلمه إلا من هذا الوجه قال العسكري وهو مرسل قلت رواية البزار ظاهرة الإرسال لكن فيها أبو مصعب وأما رواية غيره فالوصل فيها ظاهر لكن عبد الملك كان يدلس
records.english: Al-Baghawī and al-Ṭabarānī mentioned him. And transmitted by way of Jarir ibn Hazim, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Musab al-Aslami, who said, ‘A young man from among us set out and came to the Prophet ﷺ. He said, “I ask you to make me one of those for whom you intercede.” He replied, “Help me on your behalf by prostrating frequently.”’ Al-Bazzar transmitted it from Talut ibn Abbad, from Jarir, who said, ‘From Abd al-Malik: there was a young man in Medina whose kunyah was Abu Musab,’ and he related the hadith at length. He said, ‘We know it only through this route.’ Al-Askari said that it was disconnected. I say: al-Bazzar's version is clearly disconnected, though it has Abu Musab. As for the version of the others, it appears connected, but Abd al-Malik practiced concealment in transmission.

records.arabic: البجلي له إدراك ذكره سيف وأنه كان من قواد المثنى بن حارثة وأمرائه على مقدمته لما سار إلى محاربة أهل العراق وذلك سنة ثلاث عشرة ثم شهد بعد ذلك القادسية
records.english: al-Bajalī. Lived to the period. Sayf mentioned him and stated that he was one of al-Muthanna ibn Harithah's commanders and was appointed over his vanguard when he marched to fight the people of Iraq in the year thirteen. He was later present at al-Qadisiyyah.

records.arabic: ويقال بن جدالة السلمي روى أبو موسى في الذيل من طريق زيد القمي عن محمد بن سيرين عن بن عباس أن رجلا من بني سليم من الأعراب اسمه مطرح بن جندلة سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال يا رسول الله ما فضل أمتك على أمة نوح قال كفضل الله على جميع الخلائق الحديث وأخرجه بن النقاش في الموضوعات وذكر في الحديث أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سماه مطرح بن الإسلام وأخرج إسماعيل بن أبي زياد السامي في تفسير ليث بن أبي سليم عن الضحاك عن بن عباس نحوه إلا أنه قال مطرح بن جدالة وبهذا ذكره بن منده
records.english: also said to be Ibn Jadālah al-Sulamī. Abu Musa transmitted in the Supplement by way of Zayd al-Qummi, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Ibn Abbas, that a Bedouin man of Banu Sulaym named Maṭraḥ ibn Jandalah asked the Prophet ﷺ, ‘O Messenger of God, what is the superiority of your community over the community of Noah?’ He replied, ‘Like God's superiority over all created beings,’ to the end of the hadith. Ibn al-Naqqash included it among the fabricated reports. The hadith states that the Prophet ﷺ named him Maṭraḥ ibn al-Islam. Ismail ibn Abi Ziyad al-Shami transmitted in a Tafsir from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, approximately the same, except that he said Maṭraḥ ibn Judalah. Ibn Mandah mentioned him in this form.

records.arabic: بن نضلة الباهلي ذكره أبو أحمد العسكري في الصحابة وقال أسلم وكتب له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كتابا وقال الرشاطي مطرف الكاهلي وفد على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد الفتح فكتب له كتابا فيه فرائض الصدقات كذا ذكره بالكاف وقال بن شاهين مطرف بن الكاهن الباهلي من بني فريص ثم ساق حديثه فقال حدثنا عمرو بن مالك أخبرني المنذر حدثنا الحسين بن محمد بن علي حدثنا علي بن محمد المدائني عن أبي معشر عن يزيد بن رومان عن محمد بن إسحاق عن شيوخه قالوا وفد مطرف بن الكاهن الباهلي أحد بني فريص على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد الفتح فقال يا رسول الله سلمنا للإسلام وشهدنا دين الله في سماواته وأنه لا إله غيره وصدقناك وآمنا بكل ما قلت فاكتب لنا كتابا فكتب له من محمد رسول الله لمطرف بن الكاهن ولمن سكن بيته من باهلة إن من أحيا أرضا مواتا فيها مراح الأنعام فهي له وعليه في كل ثلاثين من البقر فارض وفي كل أرعين من الغنم عتود وفي كل خمسين من الإبل مسنة الحديث وفيه فانصرف مطرف وهو يقول حلفت برب الراقصات عشية على كل حرف من سديس وبازل في أبيات يمدح بها النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهذا مما يقوي أنه من باهلة قال أبو عبيد البكري في معجم ما استعجم قال يعقوب بيشة واد يصب من جبل تهامة وفي بعضها لبني هلال وبعضها لسلول وهذا يقوي أنه باهلي
records.english:
ibn Naḍlah, al-Bāhilī. Abu Ahmad al-Askari included him among the Companions and said that he embraced Islam and that the Prophet ﷺ wrote a document for him. Al-Rushati said: ‘Mutarrif al-Kahili came to the Prophet ﷺ as a delegate after the Conquest, and he wrote him a document containing the prescribed alms dues.’ He gave the affiliation with a kaf. Ibn Shahin said: ‘Mutarrif ibn al-Kahin al-Bahili, of Banu Furays,’ and then cited his hadith, saying: Amr ibn Malik related to us; al-Mundhir informed me; al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Ali related to us; Ali ibn Muhammad al-Mada'ini related to us, from Abu Mashar, from Yazid ibn Ruman, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from his teachers, who said: ‘Mutarrif ibn al-Kahin al-Bahili, one of Banu Furays, came to the Messenger of God ﷺ in a delegation after the Conquest. He said, “O Messenger of God, we have submitted to Islam and borne witness to God's religion in His heavens, that there is no deity other than Him. We have affirmed you and believed all that you said, so write us a document.” He wrote for him: “From Muhammad, the Messenger of God, to Mutarrif ibn al-Kahin and those of Bahilah who live in his household: whoever brings dead land to life where livestock may rest owns it. On every thirty head of cattle he owes a mature cow (fāriḍ); at the next sheep threshold—whose damaged numeral remains uncertain—he owes a yearling buck; and on every fifty camels he owes a mature she-camel...”’ to the end of the hadith. It says that Mutarrif departed reciting:

‘I swore by the Lord of the she-camels journeying in the evening,
upon every lean and full-grown mount...’

in verses praising the Prophet ﷺ. This strengthens the view that he was of Bahilah. Abu Ubayd al-Bakri said in Mujam ma Istajam: ‘Yaqub said that Bishah is a valley flowing from the mountains of Tihamah. Part of it belongs to Banu Hilal and part to Sulul.’ This strengthens the view that he was Bahili.

records.arabic: بن الأعلم بن عمرو بن ربيعة العقيلي ذكره بن سعد والرشاطي في وفد بني عقيل قال بن سعد حدثنا هشام بن محمد بن السائب يعني الكلبي حدثنا رجل من بني عقيل عن أشياخ قومه قالوا وقدمنا على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من بني عقيل ربيع بن معاوية بن خفاجة بن عمرو بن عقيل ومطرف بن عبد الله بن الأعلم بن عمرو بن عقيل وأنس بن المنتفق بن عامر بن عقيل فبايعوا وأسلموا وبايعوه على من وراءهم من قومهم وأعطاهم العقيق وهي أرض في بلادهم فيها عيون ونخل وكتب لهم بذلك كتابا وفيه ما أقاموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة وسمعوا أطاعوا ولم يعلمه حقا مثله قالوا وكان الكتاب في يد مطرف
records.english: ibn al-Aʿlam ibn ʿAmr ibn Rabīʿah, al-ʿUqaylī. Ibn Sad and al-Rushati mentioned him among the delegation of Banu Uqayl. Ibn Sad said: Hisham ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib—meaning al-Kalbi—related to us: a man of Banu Uqayl related to us from elders of his people, who said, ‘Those of Banu Uqayl who came with us to the Messenger of God ﷺ were Rabi ibn Muawiyah ibn Khafajah ibn Amr ibn Uqayl, Mutarrif ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Alam ibn Amr ibn Uqayl, and Anas ibn al-Muntafiq ibn Amir ibn Uqayl. They pledged allegiance, embraced Islam, and pledged on behalf of those of their people who remained behind. He granted them al-Aqiq, land in their country containing springs and date palms, and wrote them a document to that effect. It included: “So long as they establish prayer, give alms, hear, and obey; and no one shall claim a right in it equal to theirs.”’ They said that the document was in Mutarrif's possession.

records.arabic: السلمي يعد في الكوفيين قال بن حبان له صحبة وقال الطبراني اختلف في صحبته وقال عثمان الدارمي سألت يحيى بن معين عن مطر ألقي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال لا أعلمه وما يروى عنه إلا هذا الحديث وقال بن أبي حاتم سئل بن معين أله صحبة فقال لا وقال عبد الله بن أحمد سألت أبي عنه هل له صحبة فقال لا يعرف قلت فله رواية قال لا أدري وقال البرديجي لم يرو عنه إلا أبو إسحاق ولا تصح له صحبة وقال أبو أحمد العسكري قال بعضهم ليست له صحبة وبعضهم يدخله في الصحابة روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حديث إذا قضى الله لعبد أن يموت بأرض جعل له إليها حاجة وأخرجه عبد الله بن أحمد في زيادات المسند والترمذي وقال حسن غريب ولا يعرف لمطر غير هذا الحديث وصححه الحاكم
records.english: al-Sulamī. Is counted among the Kufans. Ibn Hibban said that he had companionship, while al-Tabarani said that there was disagreement over his companionship. Uthman al-Darimi said, ‘I asked Yahya ibn Main about Matar: Did he meet the Messenger of God ﷺ? He replied, “I do not know that he did. Nothing is related from him except this hadith.”’ Ibn Abi Hatim said that Ibn Main was asked whether he had companionship, and he said no. Abd Allah ibn Ahmad said, ‘I asked my father about him: Did he have companionship? He replied, “It is not known.” I asked, “Does he have any transmission?” He replied, “I do not know.”’ Al-Bardhiji said, ‘No one but Abu Ishaq related from him, and companionship is not soundly established for him.’ Abu Ahmad al-Askari said, ‘Some said that he did not have companionship, while others included him among the Companions.’ He related from the Prophet ﷺ the hadith, ‘When God decrees that a servant shall die in a certain land, He creates a need for him to go there.’ Abd Allah ibn Ahmad transmitted it in the additions to the Musnad, and al-Tirmidhi transmitted it and called it sound but uncommon. No other hadith is known from Matar. Al-Hakim declared it authentic.

records.arabic: الغنوي ويقال مطر بن فيل وقال بن حبان مطر بن الزراع له صحبة وأخرج البغوي من طريق يحيى بن حماد عن مطر بن عبد الرحمن الأنق حدثتني امرأة من عبد القيس يقال لها أم أبان بنت الوازع بن الزراع أن جدها الزراع خرج وافدا إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من أشج عبد القيس قالت فخرج جدي بابن له مصاب وبأخ له من أمه من غيره ليس من عبد القيس اسمه مطر بن فيل العنزي فقال له الأشج خرجت معنا وافدا برجل مجنون وآخر ليس منا قال أما المجنون فيدعو له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عسى أن يعافيه الله وأما العنزي فأخي لأمي لا أصبر عنه فذكر الحديث بطوله وأخرجه بن منده من طريق موسى بن إسماعيل عن مطر لكن قال مطر بن هلال وأخرجه البزار من طريق أبي داود الطيالسي عن مطر بسنده إلى الزراع أنه خرج وافدا ومعه الأشج وخرج بان له مجنون يقال له مطر وابن أخ له الحديث وقد مضى له ذكر في ترجمة صحار بن العباس وفي ترجمة جهم بن قثم
records.english: al-Ghanawī. Also said to be Matar ibn Fil. Ibn Hibban said: ‘Matar ibn al-Zarra had companionship.’ Al-Baghawi transmitted by way of Yahya ibn Hammad, from Matar ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Anaq: a woman of Abd al-Qays named Umm Aban bint al-Wazi ibn al-Zarra related to me that her grandfather al-Zarra set out with the delegation of Ashajj Abd al-Qays to the Messenger of God ﷺ. She said: ‘My grandfather set out with an afflicted son of his and a maternal brother of his by another father who was not of Abd al-Qays, named Matar ibn Fil al-Anazi. Al-Ashajj said to him, “You have set out with us on delegation accompanied by a madman and another man who is not one of us.” He replied, “As for the madman, the Prophet ﷺ will pray for him, and perhaps God will restore him to health. As for the Anazi, he is my maternal brother, and I cannot bear to be apart from him.”’ Then she related the hadith at length. Ibn Mandah transmitted it by way of Musa ibn Ismail from Matar, but called him Matar ibn Hilal. Al-Bazzar transmitted it by way of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, from Matar, with his chain to al-Zarra, stating that al-Zarra set out with the delegation accompanied by al-Ashajj and took with him a mad son named Matar and a brother's son, to the end of the hadith. He was mentioned earlier in the entries for Suhar ibn al-Abbas and Jahm ibn Qutham.

records.arabic: البلوي ذكره بن يونس وقال صحابي روى عنه ربيعة بن لقيط وأخرج بن منده حديثه من طريق بن لهيعة عن إسحاق بن ربيعة بن لقيط عن أبيه قال خرجت إلى عبد الله بن عمرو في الفتنة فلقيت على بابه مطعم بن عبيدة البلوي فقال عهد إلي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن أسمع وأطيع وإن كان علي أسود مجدع الأطراف قال بن منده حديث غريب
records.english: al-Balawī. Ibn Yunus mentioned him and said that he was a Companion from whom Rabiah ibn Laqit related. Ibn Mandah transmitted his hadith by way of Ibn Lahiah, from Ishaq ibn Rabiah ibn Laqit, from his father, who said: ‘During the civil strife I went out to Abd Allah ibn Amr. At his door I met Mutim ibn Ubaydah al-Balawi, who said, “The Messenger of God ﷺ charged me to hear and obey even if the one placed over me were a black man with mutilated extremities.”’ Ibn Mandah said that the hadith was uncommon.

records.arabic: بن عبد عوف الزهري بن عم عبد الرحمن بن عوف بن عبد عوف ذكره بن إسحاق فيمن هاجر إلى الحبشة قال فمات بها فورثه ابنه عبد الله فيقال إنه أول وارث في الإسلام وقال الواقدي هاجر إلى الحبشة الهجرة الثانية فولد له بها عبد الله وقال بن الكلبي هاجر هو وولده عبد الله فماتا جميعا بأرض الحبشة وكانت مع المطلب امرأته رملة بنت أبي عوف بن صبيرة بن سعيد بن سعد بن سهم السهمي
records.english: ibn ʿAbd ʿAwf, al-Zuhrī. The paternal cousin of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf ibn Abd Awf. Ibn Ishaq included him among those who emigrated to Abyssinia. He died there, and his son Abd Allah inherited from him; it is said that this was the first inheritance in Islam. Al-Waqidi said that he emigrated to Abyssinia in the second emigration and that Abd Allah was born to him there. Ibn al-Kalbi said that he and his son Abd Allah emigrated and that both died in Abyssinia. Al-Muttalib was accompanied by his wife, Ramlah bint Abi Awf ibn Sabirah ibn Said ibn Sad ibn Sahm al-Sahmiyyah.

records.arabic: بن الحارث بن أسد بن عبد العزى القرشي الأسدي قتل أبوه كافرا يوم بدر وعاش هو بعد ذلك وهو أخو الأسود المتقدم في الألف ذكره الزبير بن بكار وقال كان عظيم الجثة وكذلك أخوه
records.english: ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Asad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā, al-Qurashī al-Asadī. His father was killed as an unbeliever on the day of Badr, while he lived beyond that time. He was the brother of al-Aswad, who appeared earlier under the letter alif. Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar mentioned him and said that he was large-bodied, as was his brother.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن الحارث بن عبيد الله بن مخزوم أبو عبد الله بن حنطب ذكره بن إسحاق فيمن أسر يوم بدر ثم أسلم وقد تقدم له حديث في ترجمة عبد الله بن حنطب اختلف في سنده
records.english: ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Makhzūm, Abū ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥanṭab. Ibn Ishaq included him among those captured on the day of Badr; he later embraced Islam. A hadith of his, over whose chain there is disagreement, appeared earlier in the entry for Abd Allah ibn Hantab.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن الحارث بن عبد المطلب بن هاشم تقدم في عبد المطلب قال البغوي المطلب بن ربيعة ويقال عبد المطلب بن ربيعة وأخرج له بن شاهين من طريق صباح بن يحيى عن يزيد بن أبي زياد عن عبد الله بن الحارث عنه رفعه من آذى العباس فقد آذاني
records.english: ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ibn Hāshim. He appeared earlier under Abd al-Muttalib. Al-Baghawi said: ‘Al-Muttalib ibn Rabiah, also said to be Abd al-Muttalib ibn Rabiah.’ Ibn Shahin transmitted for him by way of Sabah ibn Yahya, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from him, elevating the report: ‘Whoever harms al-Abbas has harmed me.’

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الحارث بن صبيرة بن سعيد بن سعد بن سهم القرشي السهمي ذكره بن سعد في مسلمة الفتح وقال الواقدي نزل المدينة وله بها دار وبقي دهرا وقال بن الكلبي كان لدة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال أبو عبيد له صحبة وروى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وحديثه في مسند أحمد بسند صحيح إلى عكرمة بن خالد عن المطلب بن أبي وداعة قال رأيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يسجد في النجم الحديث وفي آخره قال المطلب فلا أدع السجود فيها أبدا هذه رواية عبد الرزاق عن معمر وأدخل رباح بن زيد عن معمر بين عكرمة بن خالد والمطلب جعفر بن المطلب وأخرج البغوي من طريق عبد الله بن الحارث عن المطلب بن أبي وداعة قال جاء العباس إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وكأنه قد سمع شيئا فذكر الحديث وفيه إن الله خلق الخلق فجعلني في خيرهم قبيلة وفي المغازي لابن إسحاق إن أبا وداعة أسر يوم بدر فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إن له ابنا كيسا تاجرا ذا مال كأنكم به قد جاء في فداء أبيه فكان كذلك وروى أيضا عن حفصة أم المؤمنين وحديثه عنها في صحيح مسلم من رواية الزهري عن السائب بن يزيد عن المطلب عن حفصة في صلاة السبحة قاعدا روى عنه أولاده جعفر وكثير وعبد الرحمن وحفيده أبو سفيان بن عبد الرحمن وأخرج البغوي وابن شاهين من طريق عكرمة بن خالد عن جعفر بن المطلب بن أبي وداعة عن أبيه سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ بمكة والنجم يعني فسجد فيها وقال وأنا يومئذ كافر فلم أسجد فلا أسمعها من أحد إلا سجدت فيها
records.english: al-Ḥārith ibn Ṣubayrah ibn Saʿīd ibn Saʿd ibn Sahm, al-Qurashī al-Sahmī. Ibn Sad included him among those who embraced Islam at the Conquest. Al-Waqidi said that he settled in Medina, had a house there, and lived a long time. Ibn al-Kalbi said that he was the same age as the Prophet ﷺ. Abu Ubayd said that he had companionship and related from the Prophet ﷺ. His hadith appears in Ahmad's Musnad with a sound chain to Ikrimah ibn Khalid, from al-Muttalib ibn Abi Wadaah, who said, ‘I saw the Prophet ﷺ prostrate during Surat al-Najm,’ to the end of the hadith. At its end al-Muttalib said, ‘I shall therefore never omit prostration in it.’ This is Abd al-Razzaq's version from Mamar. Ribah ibn Zayd, from Mamar, inserted Jafar ibn al-Muttalib between Ikrimah ibn Khalid and al-Muttalib. Al-Baghawi transmitted by way of Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from al-Muttalib ibn Abi Wadaah, who said, ‘Al-Abbas came to the Prophet ﷺ as though he had heard something,’ and he related the hadith. It includes: ‘God created creation and placed me among the best of them as a tribe.’ In Ibn Ishaq's al-Maghazi it says that Abu Wadaah was captured on the day of Badr. The Prophet ﷺ said, ‘He has a clever son, a merchant possessed of wealth. It is as though you can see that he has already come to ransom his father.’ That is what happened. Al-Muttalib also related from Hafsah, Mother of the Believers. His hadith from her appears in Sahih Muslim through al-Zuhri, from al-Sa'ib ibn Yazid, from al-Muttalib, from Hafsah, concerning voluntary prayer while seated. His sons Jafar, Kathir, and Abd al-Rahman, and his grandson Abu Sufyan ibn Abd al-Rahman, related from him. Al-Baghawi and Ibn Shahin transmitted by way of Ikrimah ibn Khalid, from Jafar ibn al-Muttalib ibn Abi Wadaah, from his father: ‘I heard the Prophet ﷺ reciting Surat al-Najm in Mecca’—meaning that he prostrated during it. He said, ‘I was then an unbeliever and did not prostrate, so whenever I hear anyone recite it, I prostrate during it.’

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: له ذكر في غزوة بئر معونة فروى بن لهيعة عن أبي الأسود عن عروة ثم بعث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم المنذر بن عمرو الساعدي وبعث معه المطلب السلمي ليدلهم على الطريق فذكر القصة وأخرجه الطبراني من طريقه
records.english: He is mentioned in the expedition of Biʾr Maʿūnah. Ibn Lahiah related from Abu al-Aswad, from Urwah: ‘The Prophet ﷺ then sent al-Mundhir ibn Amr al-Saidi and sent al-Muttalib al-Sulami with him to guide them along the road,’ and he related the story. Al-Tabarani transmitted it through his route.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن أسد بن عبد العزى بن قصي القرشي الأسدي قال الزبير بن بكار أوصى إلى الزبير بن العوام ثم ساق من طريق هشام بن عروة أن مطيع بن الأسود قال سمعت عمر يقول من عهد إلى الزبير بن العوام فإن الزبير عمود من عمد الإسلام ووالده الأسود هو الذي عارض عثمان بن الحويرث عند قيصر لما طلب منه أن يملكه على أهل مكة وقصته مشهورة ذكرها الزبير وغيره
records.english: ibn Asad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Quṣayy, al-Qurashī al-Asadī. Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar said that he appointed al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam as his executor. He then cited by way of Hisham ibn Urwah that Muti ibn al-Aswad said, ‘I heard Umar say: Whoever entrusts his testament to al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam does well, for al-Zubayr is a pillar among the pillars of Islam.’ His father al-Aswad was the man who opposed Uthman ibn al-Huwayrith before Caesar when Uthman sought Caesar's appointment as ruler over the people of Mecca. His story is famous; al-Zubayr and others mentioned it.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن نضلة بن عوف بن عبيد بن عويج بن عدي بن كعب بن لؤي القرشي العدوي كان اسمه العاصي فسماه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مطيعا وهو والد عبد الله المتقدم ذكره في حرف العين قال بن سعد أسلم يوم الفتح وله رواية عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وحديثه في صحيح مسلم روى عنه ابنه عبد الله وعيسى بن طلحة التيمي قال مصعب الزبيري مات في خلافة عثمان بالمدينة وحكى بن البرقي عن بعضهم أنه قتل بالجمل
records.english: ibn Naḍlah ibn ʿAwf ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUwayj ibn ʿAdī ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy, al-Qurashī al-ʿAdawī. His name had been al-Asi, but the Prophet ﷺ renamed him Muti. He was the father of Abd Allah, who was mentioned earlier under the letter ayn. Ibn Sad said that he embraced Islam on the day of the Conquest. He related from the Prophet ﷺ, and his hadith appears in Sahih Muslim. His son Abd Allah and Isa ibn Talhah al-Taymi related from him. Musab al-Zubayri said that he died in Medina during Uthman's caliphate. Ibn al-Barqi related from some authorities that he was killed at the Battle of the Camel.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: من بني بكر بن كلاب الكلابي ذكره الفاكهي في كتاب مكة وروى عن ميمون بن الحكم عن محمد بن جعشم عن بن جريج قال سماه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مطيعا وكان اسمه العاصي والذي يظهر أنه الذي بعده وأن ذي تصحفت من ذي اللحية لكن النسخة من كتاب الفاكهي متقنة والتعدد محتمل
records.english: of Banū Bakr ibn Kilāb, al-Kilābī. Al-Fakihi mentioned him in Kitab Makkah and related from Maymun ibn al-Hakam, from Muhammad ibn Jasham, from Ibn Jurayj, who said that the Prophet ﷺ named him Muti; his name had been al-Asi. What appears is that he was the person in the following entry and that Dhi is a scribal corruption of Dhi al-Lihyah. Yet the manuscript of al-Fakihi's book is precise, and the possibility that there were two men remains.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن عوف بن كعب بن أبي بكر بن كلاب أخو ذي اللحية الكلابي ذكره بن الكلابي والطبراني والدارقطني فيمن له وفادة وله حديث في مسند بقي بن مخلد قال بن الكلبي وفد على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فسأله عن اسمه فقال العاصي فقال أنت مطيع
records.english: ibn ʿAwf ibn Kaʿb ibn Abī Bakr ibn Kilāb, the brother of Dhī al-Liḥyah, al-Kilābī. Ibn al-Kalbi, al-Tabarani, and al-Daraqutni included him among those who came as delegates. He has a hadith in Baqi ibn Makhlad's Musnad. Ibn al-Kalbi said that he came to the Prophet ﷺ as a delegate. The Prophet asked his name, and he replied, ‘Al-Asi.’ He said, ‘You are Muti.’

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكره الطبري في الصحابة واستدركه بن فتحون وأنا أخشى أن يكون هو قطبة المضاي في حرف القاف فتصحفت القاف إلى الميم وتصحفت الموحدة بالباء فالله أعلم
records.english: Al-Ṭabarī mentioned him among the Companions. And Ibn Fathun supplied this omitted entry. I fear that he may be Qutbah al-Mudai, under the letter qaf, with the qāf corrupted into a mīm and, according to an internally inconsistent wording, the single-dotted letter corrupted into bāʾ; the intended second letter description remains uncertain. فالله أعلم.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن عدي بن يزيد بن جشم بن حارثة الأنصاري الحارثي عم رافع بن خديج ضبطه بن ماكولا بضم الميم وفتح الظاء وتشديد الهاء المكسورة وقال له ولأخيه ظهير بالتصغير صحبة ورواية روى عنهما بن أخيهما رافع قلت ورواية رافع عن عميه في الصحيح بالإبهام وسمي ظهيرا في رواية ويقال اسم الآخر مهير بالميم مصغر أيضا ومظهر ذكره الواقدي فيمن شهد أحدا وعاش إلى خلافة عمر فقتله أعلاج من عبيدة بخيبر وكان أقامهم يعملون له في أرضه فحملهم اليهود على ذلك
records.english: ibn ʿAdī ibn Yazīd ibn Jusham ibn Ḥārithah, al-Anṣārī al-Ḥārithī. The paternal uncle of Rafi ibn Khadij. Ibn Makula vocalized his name with a dammah on the mim, a fathah on the za, and a doubled ha bearing a kasrah. He said that both Muzhir and his brother Zuhayr—in the diminutive—had companionship and transmitted reports. Their brother's son Rafi related from them. I say: Rafi's transmission from his two paternal uncles appears in the Sahih without their names. One version names Zuhayr, while it is also said that the other was named Muhayr—with a mim and likewise in the diminutive. Al-Waqidi included Muzhir among those present at Uhud. He lived until Umar's caliphate, when non-Arab laborers from Ubaydah killed him at Khaybar. He had settled them there to work on his land, and the Jews incited them to do it.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الجهني حليف الأنصار قال أبو سعيد بن يونس صحابي كان بمصر والشام قد ذكر فيهما روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أحاديث وله رواية عن أبي الدرداء وكعب الأحبار روى عنه ابنه سهل بن معاذ وحده وذكر أبو أحمد العسكري ما يدل على أنه بقي إلى خلافة عبد الملك بن مروان وكأنه أشار إلى ما أخرج البغوي من طريق فروة بن مجاهد عن سهل بن معاذ قال غزوت مع أبي الصائفة في زمن عبد الملك وعلينا عبد الله بن عبد الملك فقام أبي في الناس فذكر قصة فيها أنه غزا مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
records.english: al-Juhanī, an ally of the Anṣār. Abu Said ibn Yunus said: ‘A Companion who lived in Egypt and Syria and is mentioned in both places.’ He related hadiths from the Prophet ﷺ and also related from Abu al-Darda and Kab al-Ahbar. His son Sahl ibn Muadh alone related from him. Abu Ahmad al-Askari mentioned evidence that he remained alive until the caliphate of Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan. He seems to have alluded to what al-Baghawi transmitted by way of Farwah ibn Mujahid, from Sahl ibn Muadh, who said: ‘I went on the summer campaign with my father in the time of Abd al-Malik, when Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Malik commanded us. My father rose among the people,’ and he mentioned a story stating that his father had campaigned with the Prophet ﷺ.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن عمرو بن أوس بن عائذ بن عدي بن كعب بن عمرو بن أدى بن علي بن أسد بن ساردة بن يزيد بن جشم بن عدي بن نابي بن تميم بن كعب بن سلمة أبو عبد الرحمن الأنصاري الخزرجي الإمام المقدم في علم الحلال والحرام قال أبو إدريس الخولاني كان أبيض وضيء الوجه براق الثنايا أكحل العينين وقال كعب بن مالك كان شابا جميلا سمحا من خير شباب قومه وقال الواقدي كان من أجمل الرجال وشهد المشاهد كلها وروى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أحاديث روى عنه بن عباس وابن عمر وابن عدي وابن أبي أوفى الأشعري وعبد الرحمن بن سمرة وجابر بن أنس وآخرون من كبار التابعين وشهد بدرا وهو بن إحدى وعشرين سنة وأمره النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على اليمن والحديث بذلك في الصحيح من رواية بن عباس عنه وذكر سيف في الفتوح بسند له عن عبيد بن صخر قال قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لمعاذ حين بعثه إلى اليمن إني قد عرفت بلاءك في الدين والذي قد ركبك من الدين وقد طيبت لك الهدية فإن أهدي لك شيء فاقبل قال فرجع حين رجع بثلاثين رأسا أهديت له قال بهذا الأسناد إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال له لما ودعه حفظك الله من بين يديك ومن خلفك وعن يمينك وعن شمالك ومن فوقك ومن تحتك وأدرأ عنك شرور الإنس والجن وفي سنن أبي داود عن معاذ بن جبل قال قال لي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إني لأحبك الحديث في القول بعد كل صلاة وعده أنس بن مالك فيمن جمع القرآن على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو في الصحيح وفيه عن عبد الله بن عمرو رفعه اقرءوا القرآن من أربعة فذكره فيهم وقال الشعبي عن مسروق كنا عند بن مسعود فقرأ إن معاذا كان أمة قانتا لله فقال فروة بن نوفل نسيت فقال ما نسيت إنا كنا نشبهه بإبراهيم عليه السلام وقال أبو نعيم في الحلية إمام الفقهاء وكنز العلماء شهد العقبة وبدرا والمشاهد وكان من أفضل شباب الأنصار حلما وحياء وسخاء وكان جميلا وسيما روى عنه من الصحابة عمر وأبو قتادة وعبد الرحمن بن سمرة وغيرهم وقال عبد الرزاق أنبأنا معمر والزهري عن بن كعب بن مالك كان معاذ شابا جميلا سمحا لا يسأل الله شيئا إلا أعطاه وقال الأعمش عن أبي سفيان حدثني أشياخ منا فذكر قصة فيها فقال عمر عجزت النساء أن يلدن مثل معاذ ولولا معاذ لهلك عمر أخرجه محمد بن مخلد العطار في فوائده وفي حديث أبي قلابة عن أنس عند الترمذي وغيره في ذكر بعض الصحابة مرفوعا وأعلمهم بالحلال والحرام معاذ وفي مرسل أبي عون الثقفي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يأتي معاذ يوم القيامة أمام الناس برتوة أخرجه محمد بن عثمان بن أبي شيبة في تاريخه وأورده بن عساكر من طريق عن محمد بن الخطاب والرتوة بفتح الراء المهملة وسكون المثناة وفتح الواو وفي طبقات بن سعد من طريق منقطع أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كتب إلى أهل اليمن لما بعث معاذا إني بعثت لكم خير أهلي ومناقبه كثيرة جدا وقدم من اليمن في خلافة أبي بكر وكانت وفاته بالطاعون في الشام سنة سبع عشرة أو التي بعدها وهو قول الأكثر وعاش أربعا وثلاثين سنة وقيل غير ذلك
records.english: ibn ʿAmr ibn Aws ibn ʿĀʾidh ibn ʿAdī ibn Kaʿb ibn ʿAmr ibn Adā ibn ʿAlī ibn Asad ibn Sāridah ibn Yazīd ibn Jusham ibn ʿAdī ibn Nābī ibn Tamīm ibn Kaʿb ibn Salimah, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, al-Anṣārī al-Khazrajī. The foremost authority on what is lawful and unlawful. Abu Idris al-Khawlani said that he was fair-skinned, radiant of face, bright of front teeth, and dark-eyed. Kab ibn Malik said that he was a handsome and generous young man, among the finest young men of his people. Al-Waqidi said that he was one of the most handsome of men and was present at all the campaigns. He related hadiths from the Prophet ﷺ. Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, Ibn Adi, Ibn Abi Awfa, followed by al-Ashari in an uncertain syntactic relationship, Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah, Jabir ibn Anas, and others among the senior Followers related from him. He was present at Badr at the age of twenty-one. The Prophet ﷺ appointed him over Yemen; the hadith concerning this appears in the Sahih in Ibn Abbas's transmission from him. Sayf mentioned in al-Futuh, through a chain from Ubayd ibn Sakhr, that the Prophet ﷺ said to Muadh when he sent him to Yemen, ‘I know your service in the religion and the debt that has come upon you. I have made gifts lawful for you, so if anything is given to you, accept it.’ When he returned, he brought thirty head that had been given to him. Through the same chain he related that the Prophet ﷺ said to him when bidding him farewell: حفظك الله من بين يديك ومن خلفك وعن يمينك وعن شمالك ومن فوقك ومن تحتك وأدرأ عنك شرور الإنس والجن. In the Sunan of Abu Dawud, from Muadh ibn Jabal, he said: ‘The Prophet ﷺ said to me, “I truly love you,”’ in the hadith concerning what is said after every prayer. Anas ibn Malik counted him among those who collected the Quran in the time of the Messenger of God ﷺ; this appears in the Sahih. Also in the Sahih is a report from Abd Allah ibn Amr, elevated to the Prophet: ‘Learn the Quran from four,’ and Muadh was among those he named. Al-Shabi related from Masruq: ‘We were with Ibn Masud, and he recited, “Indeed, Muadh was a community, devoutly obedient to God.” Farwah ibn Nawfal said, “You have forgotten.” He replied, “I have not forgotten. We used to liken him to Abraham ﵇.”’ Abu Nuaym said in al-Hilyah: ‘The leader of the jurists and treasury of the scholars. He was present at al-Aqabah, Badr, and the campaigns. He was among the finest young men of the Ansar in forbearance, modesty, and generosity, and was handsome and fine-featured.’ Among the Companions who related from him were Umar, Abu Qatadah, Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah, and others. Abd al-Razzaq said: Mamar and al-Zuhri informed us, from Ibn Kab ibn Malik, that Muadh was a handsome and generous young man who never asked God for anything without God granting it to him. Al-Amash related from Abu Sufyan: elders from among us related to me—and he mentioned a story in which Umar said, ‘Women are incapable of giving birth to the like of Muadh. Were it not for Muadh, Umar would have perished.’ Muhammad ibn Makhlad al-Attar transmitted it in his Fawa'id. In the hadith of Abu Qilabah, from Anas, in al-Tirmidhi and elsewhere, mentioning certain Companions, it is attributed to the Prophet: ‘The most knowledgeable of them concerning what is lawful and unlawful is Muadh.’ In the disconnected report of Abu Awn al-Thaqafi from the Prophet ﷺ: ‘Muadh will come on the Day of Resurrection a rutwah ahead of the people.’ Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah transmitted it in his History, and Ibn Asakir cited it by way of Muhammad ibn al-Khattab. Rutwah has a fathah on the unpointed ra, a quiescent ta, and a fathah on the waw. In Ibn Sad's Tabaqat, through a disconnected route, the Prophet ﷺ wrote to the people of Yemen when he sent Muadh: ‘I have sent you the best of my household.’ His merits are extremely numerous. He returned from Yemen during Abu Bakr's caliphate. He died in the plague in Syria in the year seventeen or the year after it, which is the majority view, and lived thirty-four years. Other views are also reported.

records.arabic: بن عوف بن وهب بن عمرو بن عوف بن غنم بن مالك بن النجار الأنصاري الخزرجي يكنى أبا حليمة وهو بها أشهر وكان يقال له القاري ساق نسبه محمد بن سعد ويقال إن كنيته أبو الحارث وأبو حليمة لقب قال أبو عمر شهد الخندق وقيل لم يدرك من حياة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلا ست سنين وقد روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وروى أيضا عن أبي بكر وعمر وعثمان روى عنه نافع مولى بن عمر وعمران بن أبي أنس وسعيد المقبري وأبو الوليد البصري وقال بن عون كان أبو حليمة يقنت في رمضان وهذا أرسله بن عون عنه فإنه لم يدركه وقال البخاري يعد في أهل المدينة وشهد الجسر مع أبي عبيدة ولما فروا قال لهم عمر أنا فئتكم وأخرج البزار وابن منده من طريق ربيعة بن عثمان عن عمران بن أبي أنس سمعت معاذ بن الحارث سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول منبري على ترعة من ترع الجنة قال بن سعد وأبو أحمد الحاكم قتل يوم الحرة وقال أبو حاتم الرازي يقال إنه قتل بالحرة وقال بن حبان عاش تسعا وستين سنة قلت كانت الحرة سنة ثلاث وستين فعلى هذا يكون ما تقدم ذكره من عمره صحيحا وهو الذي أقامه عمر يصلي التراويح في شهر رمضان
records.english: ibn ʿAwf ibn Wahb ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf ibn Ghanm ibn Mālik ibn al-Najjār, al-Anṣārī al-Khazrajī. Had the kunyah Abu Halimah, by which he was better known. He was called al-Qari. Muhammad ibn Sad set out his lineage. It is also said that his kunyah was Abu al-Harith and that Abu Halimah was a nickname. Abu Umar said that he was present at the Trench. It is also said that he lived for only six years during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ. He related from the Prophet ﷺ and also from Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman. Nafi, the client of Ibn Umar, Imran ibn Abi Anas, Said al-Maqburi, and Abu al-Walid al-Basri related from him. Ibn Awn said that Abu Halimah would recite the qunut in Ramadan. Ibn Awn's report from him is disconnected, because he did not live to meet him. Al-Bukhari said that he was counted among the people of Medina. He was present at the Bridge with Abu Ubayd. When they fled, Umar said to them, ‘I am your rallying point.’ Al-Bazzar and Ibn Mandah transmitted by way of Rabiah ibn Uthman, from Imran ibn Abi Anas: ‘I heard Muadh ibn al-Harith say: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say, “My pulpit stands upon one of the canals of Paradise.”’ Ibn Sad and Abu Ahmad al-Hakim said that he was killed on the Day of al-Harrah. Abu Hatim al-Razi said that it is reported that he was killed at al-Harrah. Ibn Hibban said that he lived sixty-nine years. I say: al-Harrah occurred in the year sixty-three, so on that account the age stated above would be correct. He is the man whom Umar appointed to lead the tarawih prayer in Ramadan.

records.arabic: بن الحارث بن سواد بن مالك بن غنم بن مالك بن النجار الأنصاري الخزرجي المعروف بابن عفراء وقيل بحذف الحارث الثاني في نسبه وعفراء أمه عرف بها شهد العقبة الأولى مع الستة الذين هم أول من لقي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من الأوس والخزرج وشهد بدرا وشرك في قتل أبي جهل وعاش بعد ذلك وقيل بل جرح ببدر فمات من جراحته وله رواية عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في السنن للنسائي وغيره من طريق نصر بن عبد الرحمن القرشي واختلف في إسناده على علي بن نصر وهو عند البغوي بسند صحيح عن نصر عن معاذ عن رجل من قريش قال رأيت معاذ بن عفراء يطوف بالبيت فطاف ولم يصل بعد الصبح أو العصر فقلت سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ينهى عن الصلاة بعد الصبح الحديث وعند البغوي من طريق أبي نصر سليمان بن زياد عن معاذ بن عفراء عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال رأيت ربي الحديث
records.english: ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Sawād ibn Mālik ibn Ghanm ibn Mālik ibn al-Najjār, al-Anṣārī al-Khazrajī. Known as Ibn Afra. The second al-Harith is omitted in one version of his lineage. Afra was his mother, by whom he was known. He was present at the first al-Aqabah with the six men who were the first of al-Aws and al-Khazraj to meet the Prophet ﷺ. He was present at Badr and took part in killing Abu Jahl. He lived afterward, though it is also said that he was wounded at Badr and died of his wounds. He has a report from the Prophet ﷺ in the Sunan of al-Nasai and elsewhere, by way of Nasr ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Qurashi. There is disagreement over its chain from Ali ibn Nasr. Al-Baghawi has it through a sound chain from Nasr, from Muadh, from a man of Quraysh, who said, ‘I saw Muadh ibn Afra circumambulating the House. He circumambulated but did not pray after dawn or the afternoon prayer. I said, “Did you hear the Messenger of God ﷺ prohibit prayer after dawn...?”’ to the end of the hadith. Al-Baghawi also transmitted by way of Abu Nasr Sulayman ibn Ziyad, from Muadh ibn Afra, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said, ‘I saw my Lord...’ to the end of the hadith.

records.arabic: الأنصاري السلمي بفتح السين ذكره بن سعد في الصحابة وكانت عنده الرباب بنت البراء بن معرور فولدت له سعد بن معاذ قلت وليس سعد هذا الصحابي المشهور رئيس الأوس وإنما وافقه في اسمه واسم أبيه وصاحب الترجمة خزرجي فافترقا
records.english: al-Anṣārī al-Salamī, with an open sīn. Ibn Sad included him among the Companions. He was married to al-Rabab bint al-Bara ibn Marur, who bore him Sad ibn Muadh. I say: this Sad is not the famous Companion who was the leader of al-Aws. He merely shared his name and his father's name with him. The subject of this entry was a Khazraji, so the two are distinct.

records.arabic: بن عمرو بن عبد الله بن أنمار بن مالك بن يسار بن حطيط بن جشم الثقفي يكنى أبا زهير وهو بها أشهر واختلف في اسمه روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
records.english: ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Anmār ibn Mālik ibn Yasār ibn Ḥuṭayṭ ibn Jusham, al-Thaqafī. Had the kunyah Abu Zuhayr, by which he was better known. There is disagreement over his name. He related from the Prophet ﷺ.

records.arabic: الأنصاري الزرقي ذكره الواقدي وقال شهد غزوة بني قريظة مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على فرس قلت وفي التابعين معاذ بن رفاعة آخر يروي عن أبيه وجابر وخولة روى عنه عبد الله بن محمد بن عقيل
records.english: al-Anṣārī al-Zuraqī. Al-Waqidi mentioned him and said that he was present at the campaign against Banu Qurayzah with the Prophet ﷺ, mounted on a horse. I say: among the Followers there was another Muadh ibn Rifaah who related from his father, Jabir, and Khawlah. Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil related from him.

records.english: son of ʿAmr ibn ʿAdī ibn al-Ḥārith, of Banū Ẓafar. Abū ʿUmar said: He attended Uḥud, as did his two sons Abū Namlah and Abū Durrah.

records.arabic: الأنصاري وقع بالشك في صحيح البخاري والموطأ عن مالك عن نافع عن رجل من الأنصار عن معاذ بن سعد أو سعد بن معاذ أن جارية لكعب بن مالك كانت ترعى غنما بسلع الحديث أورده البخاري في كتاب الذبائح عقب رواية نافع عن بن كعب بن مالك عن أخيه أن جارية لهم وذكره بن منده وأبو نعيم وابن فتحون في الصحابة و
records.english: the Anṣārī. The name occurs with uncertainty in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī and the Muwaṭṭaʾ, from Mālik, from Nāfiʿ, from a man of the Anṣār, from Muʿādh ibn Saʿd—or Saʿd ibn Muʿādh—that a slave-girl belonging to Kaʿb ibn Mālik used to pasture sheep at Salʿ; the report follows. Al-Bukhārī included it in the Book of Slaughtered Animals, following Nāfiʿ's narration from Ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik, from his brother, that a slave-girl of theirs—and he related the report. Ibn Mandah, Abū Nuʿaym, and Ibn Fatḥūn included him among the Companions. The source then ends with an isolated ‘and’; no continuation survives before the next record, so the truncation remains unresolved.

title.english: Muʿādh ibn Saʿd, or Saʿd ibn Muʿādh

records.arabic: بن عمرو بن الجموح الأنصاري قال العدوي شهد أحدا وما بعدها وقتل يوم الحرة وذكر أبو عبيد القاسم بن سلام أن معاذ بن الصمة شهد بدرا هو وأخوه خراش فيحرر هل هو أو غيره
records.english: son of ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ, the Anṣārī. Al-ʿAdawī said that he attended Uḥud and the battles thereafter, and was killed on the Day of al-Ḥarrah. Abū ʿUbayd al-Qāsim ibn Sallām stated that Muʿādh ibn al-Ṣimmah attended Badr together with his brother Khirāsh. It therefore needs to be determined whether this was he or another man.

records.arabic: بن عثمان بن عبيد الله التيمي ذكره بن السكن في ترجمة والده وقال لهما صحبة وذكره بن فتحون في الصحابة وعزاه لخليفة وقال البخاري سمع أباه وروى عنه الزهري يعد في أهل الحجاز وقال بعضهم سمع معاذ عمر بن الخطاب ولا يصح وهو أخو عثمان وكذا قال أبو حاتم الرازي ولا يصح سماعه عن عمر انتهى وإذا لم يصح سماعه من عمر فكيف يدرك العصر النبوي وروايته قلت وحديثه في الصحيحين عن حمران مولى عثمان عن عثمان وكذا في النسائي ففي البخاري من طريق محمد بن إبراهيم التيمي وعند مسلم والنسائي من طريق نافع بن جبير وغيرهم كلهم عن معاذ بن عبد الرحمن عن حمران وذكره بن سعد في الطبقة الثانية من أهل المدينة وابن حبان في ثقات التابعين
records.english: son of ʿUthmān ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, the Taymī. Ibn al-Sakan mentioned him in his father's biography and said that both had companionship. Ibn Fatḥūn included him among the Companions, attributing this to Khalīfah. Al-Bukhārī said: He heard his father, and al-Zuhrī narrated from him; he is counted among the people of the Hijaz. Some said that Muʿādh heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, but that is unsound. He was ʿUthmān's brother. Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī likewise said that his hearing from ʿUmar is unsound. End quote. If his hearing from ʿUmar is unsound, how could he have reached the Prophetic period? The source then adds a syntactically unstable phrase about ‘his narration’; its relation to the question remains unresolved. I say: His report in the two Ṣaḥīḥs is from Ḥumrān, the client of ʿUthmān, from ʿUthmān; likewise in al-Nasāʾī. In al-Bukhārī it comes by way of Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, and in Muslim and al-Nasāʾī by way of Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr and others, all of them from Muʿādh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Ḥumrān. Ibn Saʿd placed him in the second generation of the people of Medina, and Ibn Ḥibbān among the trustworthy Successors.

names.arabic: معاذ بن عبد الرحمن بن عثمان بن عبيد الله التيمي

records.english: al-Ḥumaydī transmitted his hadith in his Musnad from Ibn ʿUyaynah. He expressed the name with this uncertainty and favored Muʿādh. Its wording has already appeared among those named ʿUthmān.

records.arabic: بن زيد بن حرام بن كعب بن غنم بن كعب بن سلمة الأنصاري الخزرجي السلمي قال البخاري له صحبة وقد تقدم ذكر أبيه أيضا وشهد معاذ هذا العقبة وبدرا وهو أحد من قتل أبا جهل وقال بن إسحاق في المغازي حدثني ثور عن عكرمة عن بن عباس قال قال معاذ بن عمرو بن الجموح سمعت القوم يقولون أبو الحكم لا يخلص إليه فجعلته من شأني فصمدت نحوه فحملت عليه فضربته ضربة فأطنت قدمه وذكر بن إسحاق أيضا فيما أخرجه بن أبي خيثمة عن يوسف بن بهلول عن عبد الله بن إدريس عنه عن عبد الملك بن أبي بكر ورجل آخر معه كلاهما عن عكرمة عن بن عباس عن معاذ بن عفراء أنه قال سمعت القوم وهم في مثل الحرجة وأبو جهل فيهم وهم يقولون أبو الحكم لا يخلص إليه فلما سمعتها جعلته من شأني فقصدت نحوه فلما أمكنني حملت عليه فذكر نحوه ويمكن الجمع بأن كلا منهما ضربه وأصح من ذلك ما في الصحيحين من حديث عبد الرحمن بن عوف في قصة أبي جهل فضربه ابنا عفراء حتى برد وهما معاذ ومعوذ وفي المغازي أيضا أن عكرمة بن أبي جهل ضرب معاذ بن عمرو فقطع يده فبقيت معلقة حتى تمطى عليها فألقاها وقاتل بقية يومه ثم بقي بعد ذلك دهرا حتى مات في زمن عثمان قاله البخاري وغيره
records.english: son of Zayd ibn Ḥarām ibn Kaʿb ibn Ghanm ibn Kaʿb ibn Salamah, the Anṣārī, Khazrajī, and Sulamī. Al-Bukhārī said: He had companionship. His father has also been mentioned above. This Muʿādh attended al-ʿAqabah and Badr, and he was one of those who killed Abū Jahl. Ibn Isḥāq said in al-Maghāzī: Thawr related to me, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said that Muʿādh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ said: I heard the people saying, ‘Abū al-Ḥakam cannot be reached.’ I made him my concern, headed straight for him, charged him, and struck him a blow that severed his foot. Ibn Isḥāq also related, in what Ibn Abī Khaythamah transmitted from Yūsuf ibn Buhlūl, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs, from him, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī Bakr and another man with him, both from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from Muʿādh ibn ʿAfrāʾ, that he said: I heard the people, while they were like a thicket around Abū Jahl, saying, ‘Abū al-Ḥakam cannot be reached.’ When I heard it I made him my concern, went straight for him, and when I had the opportunity I charged him; then he related something similar. The two accounts can be reconciled by holding that each man struck him. More sound than that is what occurs in the two Ṣaḥīḥs, in ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf's report concerning Abū Jahl: the two sons of ʿAfrāʾ struck him until he grew cold; they were Muʿādh and Muʿawwidh. Al-Maghāzī also states that ʿIkrimah ibn Abī Jahl struck Muʿādh ibn ʿAmr and cut off his hand. It remained hanging until he stepped upon it and cast it off. He fought for the rest of that day, then lived a long time afterward, dying in the time of ʿUthmān. Al-Bukhārī and others said this.

names.arabic: معاذ بن عمرو بن الجموح بن زيد بن حرام بن كعب بن غنم بن كعب بن سلمة

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن عبد العزى بن غزية بن عمرو بن عدي بن عوف بن مالك بن النجار الأنصاري الخزرجي ذكر البغوي عن بن القداح أنه شهد أحدا وما بعدها واستشهد باليمامة
records.english: son of ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Ghaziyyah ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAdī ibn ʿAwf ibn Mālik ibn al-Najjār, the Anṣārī and Khazrajī. Al-Baghawī related from Ibn al-Qaddāḥ that he attended Uḥud and the battles thereafter, and was martyred at al-Yamāmah.

names.arabic: معاذ بن عمرو بن قيس بن عبد العزى بن غزية بن عمرو بن عدي بن عوف بن مالك بن النجار

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ويقال بن معاص ويقال بن ناعص بالنون بن ميسرة بن خلدة بن عامر بن زريق أخو عباد الأنصاري الزرقي قال بن إسحاق وموسى بن عقبة شهد معاذ بدرا وروى الواقدي عن يونس بن محمد الظفري عن معاذ بن رفاعة أن معاذ بن ماعص جرح ببدر فمات من جرحه قال الواقدي والثبت أنه شهد بدرا وأحدا واستشهد يوم بئر معونة وذكر بن منده من طريق إبراهيم بن المنذر عن محمد بن طلحة التيمي أن معاذ بن ماعص كان من جملة الذين خرجوا في طلب الذين ساقوا لفاح رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مع عيينة بن حصن وكان أميرهم سعيد بن زيد وكذا أخرج الواقدي من طريق أبي بكر بن أبي الجهم نحو ذلك ووقع في مغازي موسى بن عقبة أنه استشهد يوم مؤتة وفي نسخة منها أن الذي استشهد فيها أخوه عباد
records.english: also said to be Ibn Maʿāṣ, and said to be Ibn Nāʿiṣ—with a nūn—son of Maysarah ibn Khaladah ibn ʿĀmir ibn Zurayq, the brother of ʿAbbād, the Anṣārī and Zurāqī. Ibn Isḥāq and Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah said that Muʿādh attended Badr. Al-Wāqidī narrated from Yūnus ibn Muḥammad al-Ẓafarī, from Muʿādh ibn Rifāʿah, that Muʿādh ibn Māʿiṣ was wounded at Badr and died of his wound. Al-Wāqidī said: The established account is that he attended Badr and Uḥud and was martyred on the Day of Biʾr Maʿūnah. Ibn Mandah mentioned, by way of Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir, from Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥah al-Taymī, that Muʿādh ibn Māʿiṣ was among those who set out in pursuit of the men who drove away the milk-camels of the Messenger of God ﷺ with ʿUyaynah ibn Ḥiṣn, and that Saʿīd ibn Zayd was their commander. Al-Wāqidī likewise transmitted something similar by way of Abū Bakr ibn Abī al-Jahm. In Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah's Maghāzī it occurs that he was martyred on the Day of Muʾtah; in one copy of it, the one martyred there was his brother ʿAbbād.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن عمرو بن محصن الأنصاري أبو الحارث إمام مسجد المدينة حكى بن أبي حاتم عن أبيه أنه أم بمسجد المدينة ثلاثين سنة ومات سنة أربع وخمسين قال الذهبي ومقتضى ذلك أن يكون صحابيا وهو كما قال
records.english: son of ʿAmr ibn Muḥṣin, the Anṣārī, Abū al-Ḥārith, imam of the mosque of Medina. Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from his father that he led prayer in the mosque of Medina for thirty years and died in the year 54. Al-Dhahabī said: The implication is that he was a Companion. It is as he said.

names.arabic: معاذ بن محمود بن عمرو بن محصن

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: حكى أبو عمر أنه أبو زيد الذي جمع القرآن وهو بكنيته أشهر واختلف في اسمه اختلافا كثيرا
records.english: Abū ʿUmar related that he was Abū Zayd, who collected the Qurʾān. He is better known by his kunyah, and there is extensive disagreement over his name.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: النهراني ذكره أبو الفتح الأزدي في الأسماء المفردة من الصحابة واستدركه أبو موسى وقال بن الأثير لا أدري هل آخره زاي أو نون
records.english: the Nahrānī. Abū al-Fatḥ al-Azdī mentioned him among the unique names of the Companions, and Abū Mūsā added him as an omitted entry. Ibn al-Athīr said: I do not know whether the final letter of his name is zāy or nūn.

records.arabic: الجرشي ذكره بن منده من طريق عبد العزيز بن قيس عن حميد عن أنس قال أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم برجل من تهامة يقال له معافى بن زيد الجرشي فقال ما تقول في النبيذ الحديث
records.english: the Jurashī. Ibn Mandah mentioned him by way of ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Qays, from Ḥumayd, from Anas, who said: A man from Tihāmah called Muʿāfā ibn Zayd al-Jurashī was brought to the Prophet ﷺ. He said, ‘What do you say about nabīdh?’ The report follows.

records.arabic: السلمي ذكره سيف في الفتوح عن سهل بن يوسف عن القاسم بن محمد وأنه كان ممن حارب الأسود العنسي في حياة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
records.english: the Sulamī. Sayf mentioned him in al-Futūḥ, from Sahl ibn Yūsuf, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, stating that he was among those who fought al-Aswad al-ʿAnsī during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ.
