records.arabic: بن أبي العاص بن أمية بن عبد شمس بن عبد مناف القرشي الأموي أبو عبد الملك وهو بن عم عثمان وكاتبه في خلافته يقال ولد بعد الهجرة بسنتين وقيل بأربع وقال بن شاهين مات النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو بن ثمان سنين فيكون مولده بعد الهجرة بسنتين قال وسمعت بن داود يقول ولد عام أحد يعني سنة ثلاث وقال بن أبي داود وقد كان في الفتح مميزا وفي حجة الوداع ولكن لا يدرى أسمع من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم شيئا أم لا وقال بن طاهر ولد هو والمسور بن مخرمة بعد الهجرة بسنتين لا خلاف في ذلك كذا قال وهو مردود والخلاف ثابت وقصة إسلام أبيه ثابتة في الفتح لو ثبت أن في ذلك السنة مولده لكان حينئذ مميزا فيكون من شرط القسم الأول لكن لم أر من جزم بصحبته فكأنه لم يكن حينئذ مميزا ومن بعد الفتح أخرج أبوه إلى الطائف وهو معه فلم يثبت له أزيد من الرؤية وأرسل عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وروى عن غير واحد من الصحابة منهم عمر وعثمان وعلي وزيد بن ثابت وعبد الرحمن بن الأسود بن عبد يغوث ويسرة بنت صفوان وقرنه البخاري بالمسور بن مخرمة في روايته عن الزهري عن عروة عنهما في قصة صلح الحديبية وفي بعض طرقه عنده أنهما رويا ذلك عن بعض الصحابة وفي أكثرها أرسلا الحديث روى عنه سهل بن سعد وهو أكبر منه سنا وقدرا لأنه من الصحابة وروى عنه من التابعين ابنه عبد الملك وعلي بن الحسين وعروة بن الزبير وسعيد بن المسيب وأبو بكر بن عبد الرحمن بن الحارث وعبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عتبة وغيرهم وكان يعد في الفقهاء وأنكر بعضهم أن يكون له رواية منهم البخاري وقيل إن أمه لما ولد أرسلت به إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليحنكه وهذا مشكل على ما ذكروه في سنة مولده لأنه إن كان قبل الهجرة فلم يتكن أمه أسلمت وإن كان بعدها فإنها لم تهاجر به والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما دخل مكة بعد الهجرة عام القضية وذلك سنة سبع ثم في الفتح سنة ثمان فإن كان ولد حينئذ بعد إسلام أبويه استقام لكن يعكر على من زعم أنه كان له عند الوفاة النبوية ست سنين أو ثمان أو أكثر وكان مع أبيه بالطائف إلى أن اذن عثمان للحكم في الرجوع إلى المدينة فرجع مع أبيه ثم كان من أسباب قتل عثمان ثم شهد الجمل مع عائشة ثم صفين مع معاوية ثم ولي إمرة المدينة لمعاوية ثم لم يزل بها إلى أن أخرجهم بن الزبير في أوائل إمرة يزيد بن معاوية فكان ذلك من أسباب وقعة الحرة وبقي بالشام إلى أن مات معاوية بن يزيد بن معاوية فبايعه بعض أهل الشام في قصة طويلة ثم كانت الوقعة بينه وبين الضحاك بن قيس وكان أميرا لابن الزبير فانتصر مروان وقتل الضحاك واستوثق له ملك الشام ثم توجه إلى مصر فاستولى عليها ثم بغته الموت فعهد إلى ولده عبد الملك فكانت مدته في الخلافة قدر نصف سنة ومات في شهر رمضان سنة خمس وستين قال بن طاهر هو أول من ضرب الدنانير الشامية التي يباع الدينار منها بخمسين وكتب عليها قل هو الله أحد
records.english: son of Abī al-ʿĀṣ ibn Umayyah ibn ʿAbd Shams ibn ʿAbd Manāf, the Qurashī and Umayyad, Abū ʿAbd al-Malik. He was ʿUthmān’s paternal cousin and his secretary during his caliphate. It is said that he was born two years after the Hijrah, and it is also said four. Ibn Shāhīn said that the Prophet ﷺ died when Marwān was eight, which would place his birth two years after the Hijrah. He said: I heard Ibn Dāwūd say, ‘He was born in the year of Uḥud,’ meaning the year three. Ibn Abī Dāwūd said: ‘At the Conquest and the Farewell Pilgrimage he had reached the age of discernment, but it is not known whether he heard anything from the Prophet ﷺ.’ Ibn Ṭāhir said, ‘He and al-Miswar ibn Makhramah were born two years after the Hijrah, without disagreement.’ That assertion is rejected, for disagreement is established. The account of his father’s conversion at the Conquest is established. If it were established that Marwān was born in the stated year, he would have been discerning at the Conquest and would meet the criterion for the first section. I have not, however, seen anyone state decisively that he had companionship, so it appears he was not yet discerning then. After the Conquest his father was sent out to al-Ṭāʾif, with Marwān accompanying him, so nothing beyond sight is established for him. He related from the Prophet ﷺ with a missing link and from more than one Companion, among them ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, Zayd ibn Thābit, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghūth, and Yasrah bint Ṣafwān. Al-Bukhārī paired him with al-Miswar ibn Makhramah in their narration through al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwah, from both men, concerning the Truce of al-Ḥudaybiyah. In some of al-Bukhārī’s routes, they related it from one of the Companions, but in most they related the hadith without naming a Companion. Sahl ibn Saʿd related from Marwān, although Sahl was older and of higher standing because he was a Companion. Among the Successors, Marwān’s son ʿAbd al-Malik, ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, and others related from him. He was counted among the jurists. Some, including al-Bukhārī, denied that he had any direct narration. It is said that when his mother bore him, she sent him to the Prophet ﷺ for taḥnīk. This is problematic in light of the dates given for his birth: if it was before the Hijrah, his mother had not yet embraced Islam; if after it, she did not emigrate with him. The Prophet ﷺ entered Mecca after the Hijrah only for the compensatory ʿumrah in the year seven and then for the Conquest in the year eight. If Marwān was born then, after his parents embraced Islam, the account would cohere, but it conflicts with those who claim that at the Prophetic death he was six, eight, or more. He remained with his father in al-Ṭāʾif until ʿUthmān allowed al-Ḥakam to return to Medina, and Marwān returned with him. He later became one of the causes of ʿUthmān’s killing, then witnessed the Camel with ʿĀʾishah and Ṣiffīn with Muʿāwiyah. He governed Medina for Muʿāwiyah and remained there until Ibn al-Zubayr expelled them at the beginning of Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiyah’s rule; that was one of the causes of the battle of al-Ḥarrah. He remained in Syria until Muʿāwiyah ibn Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiyah died. Some of the Syrians then pledged allegiance to Marwān in a long account. A battle followed between him and al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Qays, who was governor for Ibn al-Zubayr. Marwān prevailed, al-Ḍaḥḥāk was killed, and Marwān’s rule over Syria was consolidated. He then headed to Egypt and took control of it. Death overtook him, so he designated his son ʿAbd al-Malik as successor. His caliphate lasted about half a year, and he died in Ramaḍān of the year sixty-five. Ibn Ṭāhir said that he was the first to mint Syrian dinars, each of which sold for fifty, and that he inscribed on them, ‘Say: He is God, One.’

records.english: son of Suwayd, the Juhanī. He will be mentioned in the notice of his father under yāʾ, the last letter.

records.arabic: بن الربيع بن عامر بن خالد بن غانم بن زريق الأنصاري الزرقي أبو هارون ذكره بن سعد في الطبقة الأولى من تابعي أهل المدينة وحكى عن الواقدي أنه ولد على عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وتبعه بن حبان وأبو أحمد الحاكم وابن عبد البر وقال بن أبي خيثمة بلغني أنه ولد في أيام النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وحكاه عنه البغوي وذكره العسكري في فضل من ولد في العهد النبوي وأسند أبو أحمد عن خليفة أنه يكنى أبا هارون وله رواية في الصحيح وغيره عن أمه وعن عمر وعثمان وعلي وغيرهم وروى عنه أولاده إسماعيل وعيسى ويوسف وقيس ونافع بن جبير بن مطعم وسليمان بن يسار وابن المنكدر وغيرهم قال الواقدي كان سريا ثقة وقال أبو عمر يعد في جلة التابعين
records.english: son of al-Rabīʿ ibn ʿĀmir ibn Khālid ibn Ghānim ibn Zurayq, the Anṣārī and Zurāqī, Abū Hārūn. Ibn Saʿd included him in the first generation of the Successors of Medina and related from al-Wāqidī that he was born during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ. Ibn Ḥibbān, Abū Aḥmad al-Ḥākim, and Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr followed him. Ibn Abī Khaythamah said, ‘I have been informed that he was born during the days of the Prophet ﷺ,’ and al-Baghawī related this from him. Al-ʿAskarī included him among the distinguished people born in the Prophetic period. Abū Aḥmad reported from Khalīfah that his kunyah was Abū Hārūn. He has narrations in the Ṣaḥīḥ and elsewhere from his mother, from ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, and others. His sons Ismāʿīl, ʿĪsā, Yūsuf, and Qays, as well as Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, Sulaymān ibn Yasār, Ibn al-Munkadir, and others, related from him. Al-Wāqidī said that he was a man of standing and trustworthy. Abū ʿUmar said that he was counted among the eminent Successors.

records.arabic: بن خلف الجمحي ذكره بن الكلبي في قصة ركانة
records.english: son of Khalaf, the Jumaḥī. Ibn al-Kalbī included him in the story of Rukānah.

records.arabic: بن عبد عمرو بن نوفل بن عبد مناف القرشي النوفلي كان أبوه يكنى أبا عمرو وكان شديدا على المسلمين وتزوج بنت عتبة بن ربيعة فولدت له فاختة التي تزوجها معاوية ومات أبوها كافرا قبل الفتح وعاش ولده مسلم حتى قتل يوم الجمل ذكره الباوردي
records.english: son of ʿAbd ʿAmr ibn Nawfal ibn ʿAbd Manāf, the Qurashī and Nawfalī. His father’s kunyah was Abū ʿAmr, and he was harsh toward the Muslims. He married the daughter of ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah, who bore him Fākhitah, the woman Muʿāwiyah married. Her father died as an unbeliever before the Conquest. His son Muslim lived until he was killed on the day of the Camel. Al-Bāwardī included him.

records.arabic: بن عبد المطلب الهاشمي عده أبو بكر بن دريد في أولاد العباس واستدركه بن فتحون ولعله ولد بعد تمام
records.english: son of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, the Hāshimī. Abū Bakr ibn Durayd counted him among the sons of al-ʿAbbās, and Ibn Fatḥūn added his notice. Perhaps he was born after Tamām.

records.arabic: بن الشخير تقدم نسبه في ترجمة والده وهو التابعي المشهور قال بن حبان في ثقات التابعين ولد في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وكان من عباد أهل البصرة وزهادهم وقال الذهبي في التجريد تابعي أدرك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وذكر له بن سعد مناقب كثيرة وقال كان ثقة له فضل وورع وعقل وأدب وقال أحمد في الزهد حدثنا أبو النضر حدثنا سليمان بن المغيرة وكان مطرف إذا دخل منزله سبحت معه ابنة ابنته وقال غيره كان يركب الخيل ويلبس المطارف ويغشى السلطان ولكنه على جانب كبير من الصلابة في الدين وقال يزيد بن عبد الله بن الشخير أخوه أنا أكبر من الحسن بعشر سنين وأخي مطرف أكبر بعشر سنين كذا قال وهذا لو كان ثابتا وروينا في كتاب مجابي الدعوة لابن أبي الدنيا بسند جيد عن حميد بن هلال كان بين مطرف ورجل شيء فقال له مطرف إن كنت كاذبا فعجل الله حينك فسقط مكانه ميتا ومن شدة خوفه ما رواه يعقوب بن سفيان عنه بسند صحيح قال لو أتاني آت من ربي فخيرني بين أن يخبرني أنا من أهل الجنة أو من أهل النار أو أصير ترابا لاخترت أن أصير ترابا وروى مطرف عن أبيه وعثمان وعلي وعمار وعائشة وغيرهم روى عنه أخوه أبو العلاء يزيد وحميد بن هلال وغيلان بن جرير وثابت البناني وقتادة وآخرون ومناقبه كثيرة قال العجلي ثقة من كبار التابعين مات في إمارة الحجاج بعد الطاعون الذي كان سنة سبع وثمانين
records.english: son of al-Shikhkhīr. His lineage was given earlier in his father’s notice. He is the well-known Successor. Ibn Ḥibbān said among the trustworthy Successors that he was born during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ and was one of the devout worshipers and ascetics of Basra. Al-Dhahabī said in al-Tajrīd, ‘A Successor who lived to the time of the Prophet ﷺ.’ Ibn Saʿd mentioned many virtues of his and said, ‘He was trustworthy and possessed merit, scrupulousness, intelligence, and refinement.’ Aḥmad said in al-Zuhd: Abū al-Naḍr related to us, saying Sulaymān ibn al-Mughīrah related to us, that whenever Muṭarrif entered his home, his daughter’s daughter glorified God with him. Someone else said that he used to ride horses, wear ornamented cloaks, and frequent the ruler, yet remained extremely firm in religion. His brother Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr said, ‘I am ten years older than al-Ḥasan, and my brother Muṭarrif is ten years older than I.’ So he said, though the report would need to be established. In Ibn Abī al-Dunyā’s Kitāb Mujābī al-Daʿwah, we related with a good chain from Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl that something arose between Muṭarrif and a man. Muṭarrif said to him, ‘If you are lying, فعجل الله حينك.’ The man fell dead on the spot. An indication of Muṭarrif’s intense fear is what Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān related from him with a sound chain: ‘If a messenger from my Lord came to me and gave me the choice between being told that I am among the people of Paradise, being told that I am among the people of the Fire, or becoming dust, I would choose to become dust.’ Muṭarrif related from his father, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, ʿAmmār, ʿĀʾishah, and others. His brother Abū al-ʿAlāʾ Yazīd, Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl, Ghaylān ibn Jarīr, Thābit al-Bunānī, Qatādah, and others related from him. His virtues are many. Al-ʿIjlī said, ‘Trustworthy, one of the great Successors.’ He died during the governorship of al-Ḥajjāj, after the plague that occurred in the year eighty-seven.

records.arabic: ولد سيد البشر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكره بن ظفر الحموي في كتاب البشر بخير البشر لما عد أولاد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من خديجة وقال وبعض الناس يسميه الطاهر وهو سهو فإن الطاهر هو بن أبي هالة وهو من خديجة أيضا ولم يذكر مستنده فيما زعم وما المانع أن تكون خديجة سمت أحد أولادها من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولد لها من غيره وذلك موجود في العرب كثيرا وسبقه إلى ذلك غيره وفي تاريخ بن البرقي ولدت خديجة للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم القاسم وعبد الله والطيب والطاهر والمطهر ويقال إن الطيب هو الطاهر وهو عبد الله ويقال إن الطيب والمطيب ولدا في بطن وإن الطاهر والمطهر ولدا في بطن وقد تقدم ذكر الطاهر زيادة على هذا
records.english: the son of the master of humankind, Muḥammad ﷺ. Ibn Ẓafar al-Ḥamawī included him in Kitāb al-Bishr bi-Khayr al-Bashar when enumerating the children of the Prophet ﷺ by Khadījah. He said, ‘Some people call him al-Ṭāhir.’ That is an error, for al-Ṭāhir was Ibn Abī Hālah and was likewise a son of Khadījah. Ibn Ẓafar did not mention his basis for the claim. What, however, would prevent Khadījah from giving one of her children by the Prophet ﷺ the same name as a child she bore to another man? That occurs frequently among the Arabs. Someone else preceded Ibn Ẓafar in this. In Ibn al-Barqī’s Tārīkh it says: ‘Khadījah bore the Prophet ﷺ al-Qāsim, ʿAbd Allāh, al-Ṭayyib, al-Ṭāhir, and al-Muṭahhar.’ It is said that al-Ṭayyib was the same as al-Ṭāhir, namely ʿAbd Allāh. Another report says that al-Ṭayyib and al-Muṭayyab were born from one pregnancy, and that al-Ṭāhir and al-Muṭahhar were born from one pregnancy. Al-Ṭāhir appeared earlier with more than this.

records.arabic: بن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكر في الذي قبله
records.english: son of the Prophet ﷺ. He was mentioned in the preceding notice.

records.arabic: بن أبي أمية بن عبد الله بن عمرو بن مخزوم القرشي المخزومي بن أخي أم سلمة زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال أبو عمر له رؤية ولا صحبة له وقتل يوم الجمل وقال الزبير أمه زينب بنت أصرم بن الحارث بن السباق بن عبد الدار
records.english: son of Abī Umayyah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn Makhzūm, the Qurashī and Makhzūmī, the son of the brother of Umm Salamah, wife of the Prophet ﷺ. Abū ʿUmar said that he saw the Prophet but did not have companionship. He was killed on the day of the Camel. Al-Zubayr said that his mother was Zaynab bint Aṣram ibn al-Ḥārith ibn al-Sabbāq ibn ʿAbd al-Dār.

names.arabic: زينب بنت أصرم بن الحارث بن السباق
names.english: Zaynab bint Aṣram ibn al-Ḥārith ibn al-Sabbāq

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن عبد المطلب الهاشمي أحد الإخوة قال بن عبد البر ولد في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يسمع منه واستشهد بإفريقية في خلافة عثمان سنة خمس وثلاثين وقيل استشهد بها بعد ذلك في خلافة معاوية وذكر الدارقطني في كتاب الإخوة أن عليا ولاه مكة
records.english: son of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, the Hāshimī, one of the brothers. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said that he was born during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ but did not hear from him. He was martyred in Ifrīqiyah during the caliphate of ʿUthmān in the year thirty-five. Another report says that he was martyred there later, during the caliphate of Muʿāwiyah. Al-Dāraquṭnī mentioned in Kitāb al-Ikhwah that ʿAlī appointed him governor of Mecca.

records.arabic: بن النحام العدوي ذكره بن البرقي في ترجمة والده
records.english: son of al-Naḥḥām, the ʿAdawī. Ibn al-Barqī included him in his father’s notice.

records.arabic: بن الأسود الكندي تقدم نسبه في ترجمة والده وكان يكنى به وأخرج الدولابي في الكنى من طريق منصور عن هلال بن يساف قال بعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سرية وأمر عليها المقداد فلما رجع قال له كيف رأيت الإمارة يا أبا معبد قال خرجت يا رسول الله وأنا أراهم كالعبيد لي قال كذلك الإمارة يا أبا معبد إلا من وقاه الله شرها قال لا جرم والذي بعثك بالحق نبيا لا أتأمر على رجلين
records.english: ibn al-Aswad al-Kindī. His lineage was given earlier in the entry on his father, who used him as his kunya. Al-Dūlābī related in al-Kunā, by way of Manṣūr, from Hilāl ibn Yasāf, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ dispatched an expedition and placed al-Miqdād in command of it. When he returned, he asked him, ‘How did you find command, Abū Maʿbad?’ He replied, ‘I went out, Messenger of God, regarding them as though they were my slaves.’ He said, ‘That is what command is like, Abū Maʿbad, except for one whom God protects from its evil.’ He replied, ‘Certainly not! By the One who sent you as a prophet with the truth, I will never assume command over even two men.’

names.arabic: معبد بن المقداد بن الأسود الكندي
names.english: Maʿbad ibn al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad al-Kindī

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن أبي بن سلول الخزرجي تقدم نسبه في ترجمة أخيه عبد الله ومات أبوه في السنة التاسعة ولمعمر هذا ولد تزوج زينب بنت عمر بن الخطاب فيما ذكره الزيبر بن بكار فأقل أحوال معمر هذا أن تكون له رؤية
records.english: ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl al-Khazrajī. His lineage was given earlier in the entry on his brother ʿAbd Allāh. His father died in the ninth year. This Maʿmar had a son who married Zaynab bint ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, according to al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār; the transmitted text transposes his name as "al-Zaybir." Thus, the least that can be said of this Maʿmar is that he saw the Prophet.

names.arabic: معمر بن عبد الله بن أبي بن سلول الخزرجي
names.english: Muʿammar ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl al-Khazrajī

records.arabic: بن شعبة بن عبد الله بن أبي قيس بن عبد ود بن نصر بن مالك حسل بن عامر بن لؤي القرشي العامري وهشام يكنى أبا ذئب وهو جد الفقيه المشهور محمد بن عبد الرحمن ولد في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عام الفتح وله رواية عن عمر وغيره وذكره بن حبان في ثقات التابعين
records.english: ibn Shuʿbah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Qays ibn ʿAbd Wudd ibn Naṣr ibn Mālik Ḥisl ibn ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy al-Qurashī al-ʿĀmirī. Hishām had the kunya Abū Dhiʾb and was the grandfather of the well-known jurist Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. Al-Mughīrah was born during the Prophet’s ﷺ lifetime, in the year of the Conquest. He transmitted from ʿUmar and others. Ibn Ḥibbān included him among the trustworthy Successors.

names.arabic: المغيرة بن هشام بن شعبة بن عبد الله بن أبي قيس بن عبد ود بن نصر بن مالك حسل بن عامر بن لؤي القرشي العامري
names.english: al-Mughīrah ibn Hishām ibn Shuʿbah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Qays ibn ʿAbd Wudd ibn Naṣr ibn Mālik Ḥisl ibn ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy al-Qurashī al-ʿĀmirī

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الساعدي واسم أبي أسيد وهو بالتصغير مالك بن ربيعة تقدم نسبه في ترجمة والده قال بن حبان يقال ولد في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عام الفتح قلت وقع ذكره في الصحيحين من حديث سهل بن سعد قال أتى المنذر بن أبي أسيد إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حين ولد فوضعه على فخذه وأبو أسيد جالس فلها النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأمر أبو أسيد بابنه فحمل فأقلبوه فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أين الصبي فقال أبو أسيد قلبناه يا رسول الله قال ما اسمه قال فلان قال لا ولكن سمه المنذر وله رواية عن أبيه في الصحيح أيضا وعلق البخاري في الصلاة وقال أبو أسيد طولت بنا يا بني روى عنه الزبير بن المنذر وعبد الرحمن بن سليمان بن عبد الله بن حنظلة
records.english: al-Sāʿidī; the name of Abū Usayd, in diminutive form, was Mālik ibn Rabīʿah. His lineage was given earlier in the entry on his father. Ibn Ḥibbān said that he was reportedly born during the Prophet’s ﷺ lifetime, in the year of the Conquest. I say: he is mentioned in the two Ṣaḥīḥs in the hadith of Sahl ibn Saʿd, who said: Al-Mundhir ibn Abī Usayd was brought to the Messenger of God ﷺ when he was born, and he placed him on his thigh while Abū Usayd was sitting there. The Prophet ﷺ became occupied, so Abū Usayd ordered that his son be carried away, and they took him back. The Prophet ﷺ said, ‘Where is the boy?’ Abū Usayd replied, ‘We took him back, Messenger of God.’ He asked, ‘What is his name?’ He replied, ‘So-and-so.’ He said, ‘No; rather, name him al-Mundhir.’ Al-Mundhir also transmitted from his father in the Ṣaḥīḥ. Al-Bukhārī likewise cited, without a full chain, in the Book of Prayer: ‘Abū Usayd said, “You have made it long for us, my son.”’ Al-Zubayr ibn al-Mundhir and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥanẓalah transmitted from him.

names.arabic: عبد الرحمن بن سليمان بن عبد الله بن حنظلة
names.english: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥanẓalah

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: واسمه بشر بن عمرو بن حبيش بن المعلى بن يزيد بن حارثة بن معاوية العبدي وأمه أمامة بنت النعمان قال بن عساكر ولد في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولأبيه صحبة وقتل شهيدا في عهد عمر وأمر علي المنذر على أصطخر وقال يعقوب بن سفيان وكان شهد الجمل مع علي وولاه عبيد الله بن زياد في إمرة يزيد بن معاوية الهند فمات هناك في آخر سنة إحدى وستين أو في أول سنة اثنتين ذكر ذلك بن سعد وذكر أنه عاش ستين سنة وقال خليفة ولاه بن زياد السند سنة اثنتين وستين فمات بها والله أعلم
records.english: Al-Jārūd's name was Bishr ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥubaysh ibn al-Muʿallā ibn Yazīd ibn Ḥārithah ibn Muʿāwiyah al-ʿAbdī, and his mother was Umāmah bint al-Nuʿmān. Ibn ʿAsākir said that he was born during the Prophet’s ﷺ lifetime. His father was a Companion and was killed as a martyr during ʿUmar’s rule. ʿAlī appointed al-Mundhir over Iṣṭakhr. Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān said that he had been present at the Battle of the Camel with ʿAlī. ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Ziyād, during the rule of Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiyah, appointed him over India, and he died there at the end of the year sixty-one or the beginning of the year sixty-two. Ibn Saʿd related this and stated that he lived sixty years. Khalīfah said that Ibn Ziyād appointed him over Sind in the year sixty-two and that he died there. والله أعلم

names.arabic: بشر بن عمرو بن حبيش بن المعلى بن يزيد بن حارثة بن معاوية العبدي
names.english: Bishr ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥubaysh ibn al-Muʿallā ibn Yazīd ibn Ḥārithah ibn Muʿāwiyah al-ʿAbdī

records.arabic:
بن الوليد المخزومي تقدم نسبه في ترجمة والده قال خليفة وابن سعد والزبير بن بكار أمه أسماء بنت أنس بن مدرك الخثعمية وقال أبو عمر كان غلاما على عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وشهد صفين مع علي وشهد قبلها الجمل ففقئت فيها عينه وقال بن عساكر أدرك حياة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وكان مع علي وقال أبو حذيفة البخاري في الفتوح لم ينج من بني المغيرة في طاعون عمواس إلا المهاجر وعبد الله بن أبي عمرو بن حفص وعبد الرحمن بن الحارث بن هشام وفي ذلك يقول المهاجر بن خالد
أفنى بني ريطة فرسانهم
عشرون لم يعصب لهم شارب
ومن بني أعمامهم مثلهم
من مثل هذا يعجب العاجب
طعن وطاعون مناياهم
ذلك ما خط لنا الكاتب قال وريطة التي أشار إليها هي زوج المغيرة بن عبد الله بن عمر بن مخروم وهي بنت سعيد بالتصغير بن سهم ولدت من المغيرة عشرة رجال وقال سيف بن عمر في الفتوح عن مجالد عن الشعبي خرج الحارث بن هشام في سبعين من أهل بيته لم يرجع منهم إلا أربعة فذكر الأبيات وذكر الدولابي في الكنى من طريق الحسن بن عثمان قال وممن قتل بصفين مع أصحاب علي المهاجر بن خالد بن الوليد وكذا قال يعقوب بن شيبة في مسنده وأنشد له الزبير بن بكار من قوله
رب ليل ناعم أحييته
في عفاف عند فنا الحشى
ونهار قد لهونا بالتي
لا ترى شبها لها فيمن مشى
ذاك إذ نحن وسلمى جيرة
نصل الحبل ونعصي من وشى
records.english:
ibn al-Walīd al-Makhzūmī. His lineage was given earlier in the entry on his father. Khalīfah, Ibn Saʿd, and al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār said that his mother was Asmāʾ bint Anas ibn Mudrik al-Khathʿamiyyah. Abū ʿUmar said that he was a boy during the Prophet’s ﷺ lifetime. He attended Ṣiffīn with ʿAlī, and before it he attended the Battle of the Camel, where his eye was put out. Ibn ʿAsākir said that he lived into the Prophet’s ﷺ lifetime and was with ʿAlī. Abū Ḥudhayfah al-Bukhārī said in al-Futūḥ that no one of Banū al-Mughīrah survived the plague of ʿAmwās except al-Muhājir, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī ʿAmr ibn Ḥafṣ, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām. On that subject al-Muhājir ibn Khālid said:

Banū Rayṭah’s horsemen were annihilated—
twenty, none of them with a bound moustache;
and as many again from among their paternal cousins.
At the like of this, the one who marvels may marvel.
Stabbing and plague were their deaths;
that is what the Scribe had inscribed for us.

He said: the Rayṭah to whom he referred was the wife of al-Mughīrah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn Makhrūm. She was the daughter of Saʿīd—using the diminutive—ibn Sahm, and she bore al-Mughīrah ten sons. Sayf ibn ʿUmar said in al-Futūḥ, from Mujālid, from al-Shaʿbī: Al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām set out with seventy members of his household, of whom only four returned. He then cited the verses. Al-Dūlābī mentioned in al-Kunā, by way of al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUthmān, that among those killed at Ṣiffīn with ʿAlī’s companions was al-Muhājir ibn Khālid ibn al-Walīd. Yaʿqūb ibn Shaybah likewise said this in his Musnad. Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār recited among al-Muhājir’s own verses:

Many a pleasant night I kept alive,
chastely, beside Fanā al-Ḥashā;
and many a day we took our pleasure with one
whose like is not seen among those who walk.
That was when Salmā and we were neighbors,
maintaining the bond and defying the tale-bearer.

names.arabic: المهاجر بن خالد بن الوليد المخزومي
names.english: al-Muhājir ibn Khālid ibn al-Walīd al-Makhzūmī

names.arabic: أسماء بنت أنس بن مدرك الخثعمية
names.english: Asmāʾ bint Anas ibn Mudrik al-Khathʿamiyyah

names.arabic: عبد الله بن أبي عمرو بن حفص
names.english: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī ʿAmr ibn Ḥafṣ

names.arabic: عبد الرحمن بن الحارث بن هشام
names.english: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām

names.arabic: المغيرة بن عبد الله بن عمر بن مخروم
names.english: al-Mughīrah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn Makhrūm

records.english: al-Azdī. He will be mentioned in the final section.

records.arabic: بن غانم القرشي العدوي قال أبو عمر له رؤية ولا نعلم له رواية أورده في ترجمة والده ولم يفرده واستدركه بن فتحون
records.english: ibn Ghānim al-Qurashī al-ʿAdawī. Abū ʿUmar said that he saw the Prophet, but we know of no transmission by him. He included this in the entry on his father rather than giving him a separate entry. Ibn Fatḥūn added him as an omission.

names.arabic: موسى بن حذيفة بن غانم القرشي العدوي
names.english: Mūsā ibn Ḥudhayfah ibn Ghānim al-Qurashī al-ʿAdawī

records.arabic: بن عبيد الله التيمي تقدم نسبه في ترجمة والده يكنى أبا عيسى وقيل كنيته أبو محمد ونزل الكوفة وأمه خولة بنت القعقاع بن معبد بن زرارة قال بن عساكر ولد في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فسماه وأخرج البخاري في التاريخ الصغير من طريق العقدي عن إسحاق بن يحيى عن موسى بن طلحة قال صحبت عثمان اثنتي عشرة سنة ولموسى رواية في الصحيح والسنن عن أبيه وعثمان وعلى والزبير وأبي ذر وأبي أيوب وغيرهم روى عنه ابنه عمران وحفيده سليمان بن عيسى وابن أخيه إسحاق بن يحيى وابن أخيه الآخر موسى بن إسحاق وروى عنه أبو إسحاق السبيعي وعبد الملك بن عمير وسماك بن حرب وآخرون قال الزير كان من وجوه آل طلحة وقال العجلي تابعي ثقة وكان خيارا وقال أبو حاتم كان يقال له في زمنه المهدي وكان أفضل ولد طلحة بعد محمد ويقال إنه تحول من الكوفة إلى البصرة لما غلب المختار على الكوفة وقال عبد الملك بن عمير كان فصحاء الناس يعني في عصرهم أربعة فعد منهم موسى بن طلحة قال بن أبي شيبة وابن أبي عاصم مات سنة ست ومائة وقال الهيثم بن عدي وابن سعد مات سنة ثلاث وقال أبو نعيم وأحمد مات سنة أربع
records.english: ibn ʿUbayd Allāh al-Taymī. His lineage was given earlier in the entry on his father. He had the kunya Abū ʿĪsā, though it is also said that his kunya was Abū Muḥammad. He settled in Kufa. His mother was Khawlah bint al-Qaʿqāʿ ibn Maʿbad ibn Zurārah. Ibn ʿAsākir said that he was born during the Prophet’s ﷺ lifetime and that the Prophet named him. Al-Bukhārī related in al-Tārīkh al-Ṣaghīr, by way of al-ʿAqdī, from Isḥāq ibn Yaḥyā, from Mūsā ibn Ṭalḥah, who said: ‘I accompanied ʿUthmān for twelve years.’ Mūsā has transmissions in the Ṣaḥīḥ and the Sunan from his father, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, al-Zubayr, Abū Dharr, Abū Ayyūb, and others. His son ʿImrān, his grandson Sulaymān ibn ʿĪsā, his brother’s son Isḥāq ibn Yaḥyā, and his other brother’s son Mūsā ibn Isḥāq transmitted from him. Abū Isḥāq al-Sabīʿī, ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, Simāk ibn Ḥarb, and others also transmitted from him. Al-Zīr said that he was among the leading members of the house of Ṭalḥah. Al-ʿIjlī said: ‘A trustworthy Successor, and a virtuous man.’ Abū Ḥātim said that in his own time he was called ‘the Rightly Guided One,’ and that he was the best of Ṭalḥah’s children after Muḥammad. It is said that he moved from Kufa to Basra when al-Mukhtār took control of Kufa. ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr said: ‘The eloquent men of the people’—meaning in their era—‘were four,’ and he counted Mūsā ibn Ṭalḥah among them. Ibn Abī Shaybah and Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim said that he died in the year 106. Al-Haytham ibn ʿAdī and Ibn Saʿd said he died in the year 103, while Abū Nuʿaym and Aḥmad said he died in the year 104.

names.arabic: موسى بن طلحة بن عبيد الله التيمي
names.english: Mūsā ibn Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh al-Taymī

names.arabic: خولة بنت القعقاع بن معبد بن زرارة
names.english: Khawlah bint al-Qaʿqāʿ ibn Maʿbad ibn Zurārah

records.arabic: بن عمرو التجيبي من بني حلاوة قال بن يونس شهد فتح مصر ثم ولى الإمرة على غزو المغرب سنة سبع وخمسين قلت قدمت أنهم كانوا لا يؤمرون في زمن الفتوح إلا من كان صحابيا لكن إنما فعلوا ذلك في فتوح العراق فلذلك أذكر أمثال هذا في هذا القسم
records.english: ibn ʿAmr al-Tujībī, from Banū Ḥalāwah. Ibn Yūnus said that he attended the conquest of Egypt and was then placed in command of the expedition against the Maghrib in the year fifty-seven. I say: I stated earlier that, during the period of the conquests, they appointed only a Companion to command; however, they did that only in the conquests of Iraq. I therefore include cases such as this in this section.

names.arabic: مالك بن الأغر بن عمرو التجيبي
names.english: Mālik ibn al-Agharr ibn ʿAmr al-Tujībī

heading.arabic: القسم الثالث من كان في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ويمكنه أن يسمع منه ولم ينقل أنه سمع منه سواء كان رجلا أو مراهقا أو مميزا
heading.english: The third section: those who lived during the time of the Prophet ﷺ and could have heard from him, but from whom it is not transmitted that they did hear from him, whether an adult man, an adolescent, or a discerning child

records.arabic: له إدراك وذكر سيف في الفتوح أن عمر كتب إلى سعد بن أبي وقاص أن يجعل مالك بن حبيب على إحدى مجنبتي العسكر مع عمر بن مالك الزهري وعلى المجنبة الأخرى ربعي بن عامر واستدركه بن فتحون
records.english: He lived into the Islamic period. Sayf mentioned in al-Futūḥ that ʿUmar wrote to Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ instructing him to place Mālik ibn Ḥabīb over one of the army’s two wings together with ʿUmar ibn Mālik al-Zuhrī, and to place Ribʿī ibn ʿĀmir over the other wing. Ibn Fatḥūn added him as an omission.

records.arabic:
بن عبد يغوث بن مسلمة بن ربيعة بن الحارث بن جذيمة بن مالك بن النخع النخعي المعروف بالأشتر له إدراك قال وكان رئيس قومه وذكر البخاري أنه شهد خطبة عمر بالجابية وذكر بن حبان في ثقات التابعين أنه شهد اليرموك فذهبت عينه قال وكان رئيس قومه وقد روى عن عمر وخالد بن الويد وأبي ذر وعلي وصحبه وشهد معه الجمل وله فيها آثار وكذلك في صفين وولاه على مصر بعد صرف قيس بن سعد بن عبادة عنها فلما وصل إلى القلزم شرب شربة عسل فمات فقيل إنها كانت مسمومة وكان ذلك سنة ثمان وثلاثين بعد أن شهد مع علي الجمل ثم صفين وأبدى يومئذ عن شجاعة مفرطة روى عنه ابنه إبراهيم وأبو حسان الأعرج وكنانة مولى صفية وعبد الرحمن بن يزيد النخعي وعلقمة وغيرهم وذكر بن سعد في الطبقة الأولى من التابعين بالكوفة فقال وكان ممن ألب على عثمان وشهد حصره وله في ذلك أخبار وقال المرزباني في معجم الشعراء كان سبب تلقبه بالأشتر أنه ضربه رجل يوم اليرموك على رأسه فسالت الجراحة قيحا إلى عينه فشترتها وهو القائل
بقيت وفري وانحرفت عن العلا
ولقيت أضيافي بوجه عبوس
إن لم أشن على بن هند غارة
لم تخل يوما من ذهاب نفوس قال بعض المتأخرين من أهل الأدب لو قال إن لم أشن على بن حرب غارة كان أنسب قلت كلا بل بينهما فرق كبير نعم هو أنسب من جهة مراعاة النظير وبطرائق المتأخرين وأما فحول الشعراء فإنهم لا يعتنون بذلك بل نسبة خصمه إلى أمه أبلغ في نكايته وكان للأشتر مواقف في فتوح الشام مذكورة ذكرها سيف بن عمر وأبو حذيفة وغيرهما في مصنفاتهم في ذلك
records.english:
ibn ʿAbd Yaghūth ibn Maslamah ibn Rabīʿah ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Judhaymah ibn Mālik ibn al-Nakhaʿ, al-Nakhaʿī, known as al-Ashtar. He lived into the Islamic period. He was the leader of his people. Al-Bukhārī mentioned that he attended ʿUmar’s address at al-Jābiyah. Ibn Ḥibbān stated in al-Thiqāt among the Successors that he attended al-Yarmūk, where he lost an eye, and said that he was the leader of his people. He transmitted from ʿUmar, Khālid ibn al-Walīd, Abū Dharr, and ʿAlī; he accompanied ʿAlī and attended the Battle of the Camel with him, where he had notable exploits, as he also did at Ṣiffīn. ʿAlī appointed him over Egypt after removing Qays ibn Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah from it. When he reached al-Qulzum, he drank a draught of honey and died; it was said to have been poisoned. That was in the year thirty-eight, after he had attended the Battle of the Camel with ʿAlī and then Ṣiffīn, displaying extraordinary courage there. His son Ibrāhīm, Abū Ḥassān al-Aʿraj, Kinānah the client of Ṣafiyyah, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd al-Nakhaʿī, ʿAlqamah, and others transmitted from him. Ibn Saʿd included him in the first generation of the Successors in Kufa and said: ‘He was among those who incited opposition against ʿUthmān and attended his siege; reports about him in that matter are recorded.’ Al-Marzubānī said in Muʿjam al-Shuʿarāʾ that the reason he was nicknamed al-Ashtar was that a man struck his head on the day of al-Yarmūk, and pus from the wound flowed into his eye and turned its eyelid inside out. He is the one who said:

May my wealth remain and may I turn away from glory,
and may I meet my guests with a scowling face,
if I do not launch against Ibn Hind a raid
not free for a day from the loss of lives.

One of the later men of letters said: ‘If he had said, “against Ibn Ḥarb,” it would have been more fitting.’ I say: Not at all; rather, there is a great difference between the two. Yes, it would be more fitting in respect of matching parallel expressions and according to the methods of later poets. As for the master poets, they pay no attention to that; indeed, identifying his opponent through his mother is more effective in wounding him. Al-Ashtar had celebrated exploits in the conquests of Syria, mentioned by Sayf ibn ʿUmar, Abū Ḥudhayfah, and others in their works on that subject.

records.english: ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yaʿmur ibn al-Shaddākh al-Hudhalī. He lived into the Islamic period and was the grandfather of ʿUrwah ibn Udhaynah ibn Abī Saʿd Mālik, according to Ibn al-Kalbī. I say: it is possible that he is the preceding man.

records.english: ibn ʿAbd Shams ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Ghanm ibn Ḥabīb ibn Jubayr ibn ʿAdī ibn Salūl al-Khuzāʿī. He lived into the Islamic period. Ibn al-Kalbī mentioned that his son Mālik ibn ʿUmayr had the kunya Abū Rimāḥ, and said that he composed an elegy for al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī when he was killed [the transmitted connective is damaged, and "when" is supplied here].

names.english: Mālik ibn Ḥanṭab ibn ʿAbd Shams ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Ghanm ibn Ḥabīb ibn Jubayr ibn ʿAdī ibn Salūl al-Khuzāʿī

records.arabic: بن أيفع بن زبيب بن شارحيل بن ربيعة بن مرثد بن جشم بن حاشد بن جشم بن ضرار بن نوف بن همدان الهمداني له إدراك وكان لابنه عميرة ذكر بالشام والحارث بن عميرة مدحه الأعشى الهمداني وهو الذي قتل صالح بن مسروح الحروري وقيس بن عمر أخوه كان له بلاء عظيم في قتال قطري الخارجي ذكر كل ذلك بن الكبي وقد تقدم ذو المشعار حمرة بن أيفع في حرف الحاء
records.english: ibn Ayfaʿ ibn Zabīb ibn Shurāḥīl ibn Rabīʿah ibn Marthad ibn Jusham ibn Ḥāshid ibn Jusham ibn Ḍirār ibn Nawf ibn Hamdān al-Hamdānī. He lived into the Islamic period. His son ʿUmayrah was known in Syria. Al-Aʿshā al-Hamdānī praised al-Ḥārith ibn ʿUmayrah, who was the man who killed Ṣāliḥ ibn Masrūḥ al-Ḥarūrī. Qays ibn ʿUmar, his brother, rendered great service in the fighting against Qaṭarī the Kharijite. Ibn al-Kalbī mentioned all of that. Dhū al-Mishʿār, Ḥamrah ibn Ayfaʿ, was mentioned earlier under the letter ḥāʾ.

names.arabic: مالك بن ذي المشعار بن أيفع بن زبيب بن شارحيل بن ربيعة بن مرثد بن جشم بن حاشد بن جشم بن ضرار بن نوف بن همدان الهمداني

records.arabic: بن مالك بن سبيعة بن ربيعة بن سبيع الجرمي له إدراك وولده أوس بن مالك كان شريفا وهو الذي قضى دين بن الغريزة النهشلي في قصة ذكرها بن الكبي وابن الغريزة اسمه كثير بن عبد الله
records.english: ibn Mālik ibn Subayʿah ibn Rabīʿah ibn Subayʿ al-Jarmī. He lived into the Islamic period. His son Aws ibn Mālik was a nobleman, and it was he who paid the debt of Ibn al-Gharīzah al-Nahshalī in a story related by Ibn al-Kalbī. Ibn al-Gharīzah’s name was Kathīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh.

names.english: Mālik ibn Rubaynah ibn Mālik ibn Subayʿah ibn Rabīʿah ibn Subayʿ al-Jarmī

records.english: al-Azdī, one of the champions. He lived into the Islamic period and attended the conquest of Egypt with ʿAmr. He was the first person to climb the fortress.

records.arabic: بن عمرو بن عدي بن كريب بن أسلم بن قيس بن عداس بن نصر بن منصور بن عمرو بن ربيعة بن قيس بن بشير بن سعدي بن حاشد بن جشم بن همدان الهمداني حليف خولان ولذلك يعرف بالخولاني له إدراك وشهد فتح مصر واختط بها وكان من جلساء عمر بن الخطاب ثم عمر حتى جمع له عبد العزيز بن مروان بين القضاء والقصص بمصر لما كان أميرها وذلك في سنة ثلاث وثمانين وصرف عنها في صفر سنة أربع وثمانين فكانت ولايته سنة واحدة وشهرا وكان رئيس الجيش الذي أخرجه عبد العزيز لقتال عبد الله بن الزبير بمكة وذلك سنة ثلاث وسبعين وله مسجد بمصر يقال له مسجد مالك خولان يعرف به ومن ولده منتصر بن عبد الله بن عمرو بن مالك بن شراحيل الخولاني ويقال إن الحجاج بن يوسف بناه له بأمر عبد الملك وكان عبد العزيز يبعث إليه كل سنة يحلل وكذلك الحجاج كان يبعث إليه بحلل وثلاثة آلاف قال أبو عمر الكندي في كتاب قضاة مصر حدثني بن قديد قال دخل علي عبد العزيز بن مروان عبيد الله بن سعيد السعيدي وعنده مالك بن شراحيل فقال عبد العزيز لمالك أوسع لعمك ففعل ثم دخل آخر فقال له مثل ذلك فقال أيها الأمير أكثرت من قولك عمك لقد رعيت الإبل قبل أن يجتمع أبواه
records.english: ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAdī ibn Kurayb ibn Aslam ibn Qays ibn ʿAddās ibn Naṣr ibn Manṣūr ibn ʿAmr ibn Rabīʿah ibn Qays ibn Bashīr ibn Saʿdī ibn Ḥāshid ibn Jusham ibn Hamdān al-Hamdānī, an ally of Khawlān and therefore known as al-Khawlānī. He lived into the Islamic period, attended the conquest of Egypt, and took up a residence allotment there. He was among ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb’s companions. He then lived so long that ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Marwān combined for him the offices of judge and public preacher in Egypt when ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz was its governor, in the year eighty-three. He was removed from them in Ṣafar of the year eighty-four, so his term lasted one year and one month. He was commander of the army that ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz sent to fight ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr in Mecca in the year seventy-three. In Egypt he had a mosque called the Mosque of Mālik Khawlān, by which he was known. Among his descendants was Muntaṣir ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn Mālik ibn Sharāḥīl al-Khawlānī. It is said that al-Ḥajjāj ibn Yūsuf built it for him at ʿAbd al-Malik’s command. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz used to send him ceremonial robes every year, and al-Ḥajjāj likewise used to send him robes and three thousand. Abū ʿUmar al-Kindī said in his Book of the Judges of Egypt: Ibn Qudayd related to me that ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Saʿīd al-Saʿīdī entered upon ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Marwān while Mālik ibn Sharāḥīl was with him. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said to Mālik, ‘Make room for your uncle,’ and he did. Then another man entered and he said the same thing to him. Mālik said, ‘Commander, you have said “your uncle” many times! I had already herded camels before his two parents had even come together.’

names.arabic: مالك بن شراحيل بن عمرو بن عدي بن كريب بن أسلم بن قيس بن عداس بن نصر بن منصور بن عمرو بن ربيعة بن قيس بن بشير بن سعدي بن حاشد بن جشم بن همدان الهمداني
names.english: Mālik ibn Shurāḥīl ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAdī ibn Kurayb ibn Aslam ibn Qays ibn ʿAddās ibn Naṣr ibn Manṣūr ibn ʿAmr ibn Rabīʿah ibn Qays ibn Bashīr ibn Saʿdī ibn Ḥāshid ibn Jusham ibn Hamdān al-Hamdānī

names.arabic: منتصر بن عبد الله بن عمرو بن مالك بن شراحيل الخولاني
names.english: Muntaṣir ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn Mālik ibn Sharāḥīl al-Khawlānī

records.arabic: الضمري له إدراك وأخرج بن أبي شيبة من طريق حنبل بن المصبح قال أوصى مالك بن ضمرة بسلاحه للمجاهدين من بني ضمرة الا يقاتل به أهل نبوة فقال له أخوه يا أخي عند الموت تقول هو ذاك قال فلما كان أمر الحسين بن علي جاء رجل من البعث الذين سيرهم إليه عبيد الله بن زياد إلى موسى بن مالك فقال أعرني رمح أبيك فناوله فقالت له امرأة من أهله يا موسى أما تذكر وصية أبيك قال فطلبه حتى أخذ منه الرمح فكسره قلت وقد وصف مالك هذا بسعة العلم فروى المحاملي في أماليه من رواية البغداديين عنه عن أحمد بن محمد التبعي بسند له إلى أبي ذر قال ما ترك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شيئا مما صبه جبرائيل وميكائيل في صدره إلا قد صبه في صدري ولا تركت شيئا صبه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في صدري إلا قد صببته في صدر مالك بن ضمرة
records.english: al-Ḍamrī. He lived into the Islamic period. Ibn Abī Shaybah related by way of Ḥanbal ibn al-Muṣabbiḥ, who said: Mālik ibn Ḍamrah bequeathed his weapon to the fighters of Banū Ḍamrah on condition that the people of prophethood not be fought with it. His brother said to him, ‘Brother, at the time of death you say this?’ He replied, ‘That is so.’ When the affair of al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī occurred, a man from the force that ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Ziyād had sent against him came to Mūsā ibn Mālik and said, ‘Lend me your father’s spear.’ He handed it to him, but a woman of his household said to him, ‘Mūsā, do you not remember your father’s bequest?’ He pursued the man until he recovered the spear from him, and then broke it. I say: this Mālik was described as possessing wide knowledge. Al-Maḥāmilī related in his Amālī, among reports transmitted by Baghdadis, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Tabʿī with his chain to Abū Dharr, who said: ‘The Messenger of God ﷺ left nothing of what Gabriel and Michael poured into his breast without pouring it into my breast; and I left nothing of what the Messenger of God ﷺ poured into my breast without pouring it into the breast of Mālik ibn Ḍamrah.’

records.arabic: بن حنتف بن أوس بن حيي بن عمرو بن سلسلة بن غنم بن أيوب بن معن بن عتود الطائي له إدراك وكان ولده بهدل رئيس بني معن لما التقوا مع طليعة نجدة الحنفي بالآخر ذكره بن الكلبي
records.english: ibn Ḥantaf ibn Aws ibn Ḥayy ibn ʿAmr ibn Silsila ibn Ghanm ibn Ayyūb ibn Maʿn ibn ʿAtūd al-Ṭāʾī. He lived into the Islamic period. His son Bahdal was the leader of Banū Maʿn when they met the vanguard of Najdah al-Ḥanafī at al-Ākhir. Ibn al-Kalbī mentioned him.

names.arabic: مالك بن الطفيل بن حنتف بن أوس بن حيي بن عمرو بن سلسلة بن غنم بن أيوب بن معن بن عتود الطائي
names.english: Mālik ibn al-Ṭufayl ibn Ḥantaf ibn Aws ibn Ḥayy ibn ʿAmr ibn Silsila ibn Ghanm ibn Ayyūb ibn Maʿn ibn ʿAtūd al-Ṭāʾī

records.arabic: أبو عطية الوداعي تابعي من أهل الكوفة قيل إنه أدرك الجاهلية واستدركه أبو موسى قلت أبو عطية الوداعي تابعي كبير ثقة مشهور بكنيته اختلف في اسم أبيه فقيل هكذا وقيل عمرو بن جندب وقيل هما اثنان وسيأتي في الكنى
records.english: Abū ʿAṭiyyah al-Wādiʿī. He was a Successor from Kufa. It is said that he lived into the pre-Islamic period, and Abū Mūsā added him as an omission. I say: Abū ʿAṭiyyah al-Wadāʿī was a senior, trustworthy Successor famous by his kunya. There is disagreement over his father’s name: it is said to have been as given here, and it is also said to have been ʿAmr ibn Jundab; it is further said that they were two different men. He will be discussed under the kunyas.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الكندي كان أحد من ثبت على إسلامه حين ارتد قومه فخطبهم وخوفهم وأنشدهم أبياتا ذكرها وثيمة في كتاب الردة وكان عابدا لسنا فأطاعوه ثم غلب عليهم الشقاء فارتدوا وطردوه فلحق بزيادة بن لبيد والمسلمين
records.english: al-Kindī. He was one of those who remained firm in Islam when his people apostatized. He addressed them, warned them, and recited verses to them that Wathīmah mentioned in the Book of Apostasy. He was a devout and eloquent man, and they obeyed him. Then wretchedness overcame them: they apostatized and expelled him, so he joined Ziyādah ibn Labīd and the Muslims.

records.arabic: بن عمرون بن عمر بن ذيبان بن ثعلبة بن عمرو بن يشكر بن علي بن مالك بن سعد بن نذير بن قسر البجلي ثم القسري له إدراك وهو والد أبي أراكة صاحب الدار بالكوفة التي يقال لها دار أبي أراكة ولأبي أراكة فيها قصة مع علي ذكره بن الكلبي
records.english: ibn ʿAmrūn ibn ʿUmar ibn Dhibyān ibn Thaʿlabah ibn ʿAmr ibn Yashkur ibn ʿAlī ibn Mālik ibn Saʿd ibn Nadhīr ibn Qasr al-Bajalī, then al-Qasrī. He lived into the Islamic period. He was the father of Abū Arākah, owner of the house in Kufa known as the House of Abū Arākah. Abū Arākah had a story there involving ʿAlī, mentioned by Ibn al-Kalbī.

names.arabic: مالك بن عامر بن عمرون بن عمر بن ذيبان بن ثعلبة بن عمرو بن يشكر بن علي بن مالك بن سعد بن نذير بن قسر البجلي ثم القسري
names.english: Mālik ibn ʿĀmir ibn ʿAmrūn ibn ʿUmar ibn Dhibyān ibn Thaʿlabah ibn ʿAmr ibn Yashkur ibn ʿAlī ibn Mālik ibn Saʿd ibn Nadhīr ibn Qasr al-Bajalī, then al-Qasrī

records.arabic: مولى عمر هو الذي يقال له مالك الدار له إدراك وسمع من أبي بكر الصديق وروى عن الشيخين ومعاذ وأبي عبيدة روى عنه أبو صالح السمان وابناه عون وعبد الله ابنا مالك وأخرج البخاري في التاريخ من طريق أبي صالح ذكوان عن مالك الدار أن عمر قال في قحوط المطر يا رب لا آلو إلا ما عجزت عنه وأخرجه بن أبي خيثمة من هذا الوجه مطولا قال أصاب الناس قحط في زمن عمر فجاء رجل إلى قبر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال يا رسول الله استسق الله لأمتك فأتاه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في المنام فقال له ائت عمر فقل له إنكم مستسقون فعليك الكفين قال فبكى عمر وقال يا رب ما آلوا إلا ما عجزت عنه وروينا في فوائد داود بن عمرو الضبي جمع البغوي من طريق عبد الرحمن بن سعيد بن يربوع المخزومي عن مالك الدار قال دعاني عمر بن الخطاب يوما فإذا عنده صرة من ذهب فيها أربعمائة دينار فقال اذهب بهذه إلى أبي عبيدة فذكر قصته وذكر بن سعد في الطبقة الأولى من التابعين في أهل المدينة قال روى عن أبي بكر وعمر وكان معروفا وقال أبو عبيدة ولاه عمر كيلة عيال عمر فلما قدم عثمان ولاه القسم فسمى مالك الدار وقال إسماعيل القاضي عن علي بن المديني كان مالك الدار خازنا لعمر
records.english: ʿUmar's client; he is the one called Mālik al-Dār. He lived into the Islamic period, heard from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, and transmitted from the two shaykhs, Muʿādh, and Abū ʿUbaydah. Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Sammān and Mālik’s two sons, ʿAwn and ʿAbd Allāh, transmitted from him. Al-Bukhārī related in al-Tārīkh, by way of Abū Ṣāliḥ Dhakwān, from Mālik al-Dār, that during a drought ʿUmar said, يا رب لا آلو إلا ما عجزت عنه. Ibn Abī Khaythamah related it at greater length by this route: a drought afflicted the people in ʿUmar’s time, so a man came to the Prophet’s ﷺ grave and said, ‘Messenger of God, ask God for rain for your community.’ The Prophet ﷺ came to him in a dream and said, ‘Go to ʿUmar and tell him that you are seeking rain, and that he must use both palms.’ ʿUmar wept and said, يا رب ما آلوا إلا ما عجزت عنه. We also transmitted in the Benefits of Dāwūd ibn ʿAmr al-Ḍabbī, collected by al-Baghawī, by way of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Saʿīd ibn Yarbūʿ al-Makhzūmī, from Mālik al-Dār, who said: ‘One day ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb summoned me. With him was a purse of gold containing four hundred dinars. He said, “Take this to Abū ʿUbaydah,”’ and he related the story. Ibn Saʿd included him in the first generation of the Successors among the people of Medina and said that he transmitted from Abū Bakr and ʿUmar and was well known. Abū ʿUbaydah said that ʿUmar appointed him to measure provisions for ʿUmar’s dependents. When ʿUthmān became caliph, he appointed him over the distribution, and he was therefore called Mālik al-Dār. Ismāʿīl al-Qāḍī related from ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī that Mālik al-Dār was ʿUmar’s treasurer.

names.english: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Saʿīd ibn Yarbūʿ al-Makhzūmī

records.arabic: بن مالك بن خارجة بن عمرو بن مالك بن زيد بن مرة بن سلهم السلهمي له إدراك وشهد هو وأبوه فتح مصر وسكن أبوه دلاص من صعيد مصر ذكره سعيد بن عفير وحكاه بن يونس عن هانئ بن المنذر
records.english: ibn Mālik ibn Khārijah ibn ʿAmr ibn Mālik ibn Zayd ibn Murrah ibn Salham al-Salhamī. He lived into the Islamic period. He and his father attended the conquest of Egypt, and his father settled in Dalāṣ in Upper Egypt. Saʿīd ibn ʿUfayr mentioned this, and Ibn Yūnus transmitted it from Hāniʾ ibn al-Mundhir.

names.arabic: مالك بن قدامة بن مالك بن خارجة بن عمرو بن مالك بن زيد بن مرة بن سلهم السلهمي
names.english: Mālik ibn Qudāmah ibn Mālik ibn Khārijah ibn ʿAmr ibn Mālik ibn Zayd ibn Murrah ibn Salham al-Salhamī

records.arabic: بن جعشم المدلجي بن أخي سراقة أخرج البخاري من طريق الزهري عن عبد الرحمن بن مالك بن جعشم هذا عن أبيه عن سراقة قصة الهجرة ولم ارهم ذكروا مالك بن جعشم فكأنه مات في الجاهلية فيكون لولده مالك إدراك إن لم يكن له صحبة
records.english: ibn Juʿshum al-Mudlijī, the son of Surāqah's brother. Al-Bukhārī related, by way of al-Zuhrī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mālik ibn Juʿshum—this man—from his father, from Surāqah, the story of the Emigration. I have not seen them mention Mālik ibn Juʿshum, so it appears that he died in the pre-Islamic period. His son Mālik would therefore have lived into the Islamic period, unless he was himself a Companion.

names.arabic: مالك بن مالك بن جعشم المدلجي
names.english: Mālik ibn Mālik ibn Juʿshum al-Mudlijī

names.arabic: عبد الرحمن بن مالك بن جعشم
names.english: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mālik ibn Juʿshum

records.arabic: بن شيبان بن شهاب بن قلع واسمه علقمة بن عمرو أبو غسان الرافعي له إدراك قال بن عساكر ولد على عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وكان سيد ربيعة في زمانه مقدما رئيسا وفيه يقول حصين بن المنذر حياء أبي غسان خير لقومه لمن كان قد قاسى الأمور وجربا ومات سنة ثلاث أو أربع وسبعين
records.english: ibn Shaybān ibn Shihāb ibn Qalaʿ—whose name was ʿAlqamah ibn ʿAmr—Abū Ghassān al-Rāfiʿī. He lived into the Islamic period. Ibn ʿAsākir said that he was born during the Prophet’s ﷺ lifetime. He was the chief of Rabīʿah in his day, an eminent leader. Ḥuṣayn ibn al-Mundhir said of him: ‘Abū Ghassān’s modesty is better for his people than one who has suffered and tested affairs.’ He died in the year seventy-three or seventy-four.

names.arabic: مالك بن مسمع بن شيبان بن شهاب بن قلع
names.english: Mālik ibn Mismaʿ ibn Shaybān ibn Shihāb ibn Qalaʿ

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الصدفي يكنى أبا ناعمة ذكره بن يونس وقال كان من أصحاب عمر وهو صاحب الفرس المشهرو الذي يقال له أشقر صدق وشهد فتح مصر وذكر بن عفير عن أشياخ مصر أن مالك بن ناعمة كان من أمداد أهل المين وكان معه أم الأشقر وكان يعقر عليها الوحش في طريقه فخرج عليها من بعض الأودية فحل طريل أهلب لم ير مثله فنزا عليها فبادر مالك ليطرده عنها فلم يلحقه حتى نزل وقدم مالك الشام فأقام في محاربة الروم حتى وضعت فرسه فسماه الأشقر وذلك في يوم هزيمتهم وهو في الطلب فلم يزل يركض مع أمه يومه ما يلويه حتى منعه الليل من الطلب ثم دخل معه مصر لما فتحت فسبق به الناس
records.english: al-Ṣadafī, whose kunyah was Abū Nāʿimah. Ibn Yūnus mentioned him and said that he was among ʿUmar’s companions. He owned the famous horse called Ashqar Ṣidq and attended the conquest of Egypt. Ibn ʿUfayr related from the Egyptian shaykhs that Mālik ibn Nāʿimah was among the reinforcements of the people of al-Mayn. With him was the dam of al-Ashqar, and he used to hunt wild game from her on his journey. A tall, shaggy stallion, the like of which had never been seen, came out to her from one of the valleys and mounted her. Mālik hurried to drive it away from her but did not catch it before it dismounted. Mālik reached Syria and remained there fighting the Byzantines until his mare foaled; he named the foal al-Ashqar. That occurred on the day of their rout, while Mālik was in pursuit. The foal continued to run with his dam throughout that day, with nothing turning him aside, until night prevented further pursuit. He later entered Egypt with Mālik after it was conquered, and Mālik outstripped the people on him.
