records.arabic: ذكره عبدان في الصحابة وقال سمع من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم أخرج من وجهين عن يحيى بن سعيد الأنصاري عن محمد بن محمود قال رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أعمى يتوضأ فلما غسل يديه ووجهه جعل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول له اغسل باطن قدميك وهذا ليس فيه ما يدل على ما زعمه عبدان أنه سمع من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقد ذكره البخاري ومن تابعه في التابعين وقالوا إن حديثه مرسل واختلفوا في نسبه فقيل هو محمد بن محمود بن عبد الله بن مسلمة بن أخي محمد بن مسلمة وقيل حفيده وقد ذكر بن منده في تاريخه محمد بن محمود بن محمد بن مسلمة روى عن أبيه عدي روى عنه ابنه سليمان قال وروى يحيى بن سعيد عن سعيد عن محمد بن محمود وسيأتي في ترجمة أبي نصر الثقفي في الكنى مزيد كلام على هذا إن شاء الله تعالى
records.english: ʿAbdān mentioned him among the Companions and said that he heard from the Prophet ﷺ. He then transmitted by two routes from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Anṣārī, from Muḥammad ibn Maḥmūd, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ saw a blind man performing ablution. When the man had washed his hands and face, the Prophet ﷺ began saying to him, ‘Wash the soles of your feet.’ This contains nothing indicating what ʿAbdān claimed, that he heard from the Prophet ﷺ. Al-Bukhārī and those who followed him mentioned him among the Successors and said his report was disconnected. They differed over his lineage: it was said that he was Muḥammad ibn Maḥmūd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maslamah, the son of the brother of Muḥammad ibn Maslamah, and it was said that he was his grandson. Ibn Mandah mentioned in his Tārīkh Muḥammad ibn Maḥmūd ibn Muḥammad ibn Maslamah, after which the text has the ambiguous sequence ‘narrated from his father, ʿAdī; his son Sulaymān narrated from him.’ The clause boundary does not establish ʿAdī as the father's name, so the relationship remains unresolved. He said: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd also narrated from Saʿīd, from Muḥammad ibn Maḥmūd. Further discussion of this will appear under Abū Naṣr al-Thaqafī among the kunyahs, إن شاء الله تعالى.

records.arabic: المدني ذكره بن منده في الصحابة وقال ذكره جماعة في الصحابة وهو وهم منهم ثم أخرج من طريق أبي الفضل أحمد بن الحسين اللهبي عن عاصم بن سويد عن سليم بن محمد الكرماني عن أبيه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من توضأ فأحسن وضوءه ثم خرج إلى مسجد قباء لا يخرجه إلا الصلاة فقد انقلب بأجر عمرة قال بن منده الصواب عن محمد بن سليمان الكرماني عن أبي أمامة بن سهل بن حنيف عن أبيه انتهى والحديث المذكور عند بن ماجة وصححه الحاكم من طريق حاتم بن إسماعيل وعيسى بن يونس كلاهما عن محمد بن سليمان على الصواب وكذا أخرجه النسائي بنحوه من رواية مجمع بن يعقوب عن محمد بن سليمان فكأن اسم الراوي انقلب على أبي الفضل وسقط اسم شيخه فتركب منه صحابي لا وجود له
records.english: al-Madanī. Ibn Mandah mentioned him among the Companions and said: A group mentioned him among the Companions, but this was their error. He then transmitted by way of Abū al-Faḍl Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Lahabī, from ʿĀṣim ibn Suwayd, from Sulaym ibn Muḥammad al-Kirmānī, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said, ‘Whoever performs ablution and performs it well, then goes out to the mosque of Qubāʾ with nothing but prayer bringing him out, returns with the reward of an ʿumrah.’ Ibn Mandah said: The correct chain is from Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Kirmānī, from Abū Umāmah ibn Sahl ibn Ḥunayf, from his father. End quote. The cited report is found in Ibn Mājah and was authenticated by al-Ḥākim, by way of Ḥātim ibn Ismāʿīl and ʿĪsā ibn Yūnus, both from Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān, in the correct form. Al-Nasāʾī likewise transmitted similar wording from the narration of Mujammaʿ ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān. It appears that the narrator's name was reversed for Abū al-Faḍl and the name of his shaykh fell out, producing from the remnants a Companion who never existed.

records.arabic:
بن مسعود الثقفي يأتي نسبه في ترجمة والده في الكنى ذكره بن عبد البر فقال يكنى أبا إسحاق ولم يكن بالمختار كان أبوه من جلة الصحابة ويأتي في الكنى وولد المختار عام الهجرة وليست له صحبة ولا رؤية وأخباره غير مرضية حكاها عنه ثقات مثل الشعبي وغيره وكان قد طلب الإمارة وغلب على الكوفة حتى قلته مصعب بن الزبير بالكوفة سنة سبع وستين وكان قبل ذلك معدودا في أهل الفضل والخير إلى أن فارق بن الزبير وكان يتزين بطلب دم الحسين ويسر طلب الدنيا فيأتي بالكذب والجنون وكانت إمارته ستة عشر شهرا قال وروى موسى بن إسماعيل عن أبي عوانة عن مغيرة عن ثابت بن هرمز قال حمل المختار مالا من المدائن من عند عمه إلى علي فأخرج كيسا فيه خمسة عشر درهما فقال هذا من أجور المومسات فقال له علي ويلك مالي وللمومسات ثم قام وعليه مقطعة حمراء فلما سلم قال علي ما له قاتله الله لو شق عن قلبه الآن لوجد ملآن من حب اللات والعزى قال ويقال إنه كان في أول أمره خارجيا ثم صار زيديا ثم صار رافضيا وقتل المختار محمد بن عمار بن ياسر ظلما لأنه سأله أن يحدث عن أبيه بحديث كذب فلم يفعل فقتله وهذا ما ذكره أبو عمر في ترجمته وجزم بأن أباه كان صحابيا وأنه ولد سنة الهجرة وقد تقدم غير مرة أنه لم يبق بمكة ولا الطائف أحد من قريش وثقيف إلا شهد حجة الوداع فمن ثم يكون المختار من هذا القسم إا أن أخباره رديئة وقد زاد بن الأثير في ترجمته على ما ذكره بن عبد البر قليلا من ذلك قوله كان بين المختار والشعبي ما يوجب ألا يسمع كلام أحدهما في الآخر أدرج بن الأثير هذا القدر في كلام بن عبد البر وليس هو فيه ولا هو بصحيح فإن الشعبي لم ينفرد بما حكاه عن المختار والشعبي مجمع على ثقته والمختار بالعكس قد شهد عليه بدعوى النبوة والكذب الصريح جماعة من أهل البيت ومما ورد في ذلك ما أخرجه أحمد في مسند عمرو بن الحمق من طريق السدي عن رفاعة القتباني قال دخلت على المختار فألقلى إلي وسادة وقال لولا أن أخي جبرائيل قام عن هذه وأشار إلى أخرى عنده لألقيتها لك قال فأردت أن أضرب عنقه فذكر قصة وحديثا لعمرو بن الحمق وقال بن حبان في ترجمته صفية بنت أبي عبيد في الثقات هي أخت المختار المتنبي بالعراق وأقوى ما ورد في ذمه ما أخرجه مسلم في صحيحه عن أسماء بنت أبي بكر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال يكون في ثقيف كذاب ومبير فشهدت أسماء أن الكذاب هو المختار المذكور قال بن الأثير وكان المختار قد خرج يطلب بثأر الحسين فاجتمع عليه بشر كثير من الشيعة بالكوفة فغلب عليها وتطلب قتلة الحسين فقتلهم قتل شمر بن ذي الجوشن الذي باشر قتل الحسين وخولي بن يزيد الذي سار برأسه إلى الكوفة وعمر بن سعد بن أبي وقاص أمير الجيش الذي حاربوا الحسين حتى قتلوه وقتل معه ولده حفصا وأرسل إبراهيم بن الأشتر في عسكر كثيف فلقي عبيد الله بن زياد الذي كان جهز الجيش إلى الحسين فحاربوه فقتل عبيد الله بن زياد في تلك الواقعة قال بن الأثير فلذلك أحب المختار كثير من المسلمين فإنه أبلى في ذلك بلاء حسنا قال وكان يرسل المال إلى بن عمر وهو صهره زوج أخته صفية بنت أبي عبيد وإلى بن عباس وإلى بن الحنفية فيقبلونه ثم سار إيه مصعب من البصرة فقتل المختار انتهى وكان أول أمر المختار أن بن الزبير أرسله إلى الكوفة ليؤكد له أمر بيعته وولي عبد الله بن مطيع إمرة الكوفة فأظهر المختار أن بن الزبير دعا في السر للطلب بدم الحسين ثم أراد تأكيد أمره فادعى أن محمد بن الحنفية هو المهدي الذي سيخرج في آخر الزمان وأنه أمره أن يدعو الناس إلى بيعته وزور على لسانه كتابا فدخل في طاعته جمع جم فتقوى بهم وتتبع قتلة الحسين فقتلهم فقوي أمره بمن يحب أهل البيت ثم وقع بين بن الزبير وابن الحنفية وابن العباس ما وقع لكونهما امتنعا من المبايعة فحصرهما ومن كان من جهتهما في الشعب فبلغ المختار فأرسل عسكرا كثيفا وأمر عليهم أبا عبد الله الجدلي فهجموا مكة وأخرجوهما من الشعب فلحقا بالطائف فشكر الناس للمختار ذلك وفي ذلك يقول المختار أنشد له المرزباني
تسربلت من همدان درعا حصينة
ترد العوالي بالأنوف الرواغم
همو نصروا آل الرسول محمد
وقد أجحفت بالناس إحدى العظائم
وفوا حين أعطوا عهدهم لإمامهم
وكفوا عن الإسلام سيف المظالم وذكر بن سعد عن الواقدي بأسانيده أن أبا عبيد والد المختار قدم من الطائف في زمن عمر حين ندب الناس إلى العرق فخرج أبو عبيدة فاستشهد يوم الجسر وبقي ولده بالمدينة وتزوج بن عمر صفية بنت أبي عبيد واقام المختار بالمدينة منقطعا إلى بني هاشم ثم كان مع علي بالعراق وسكن البصرة بعد علي وله قصة مع الحسن بن علي لما ولي الخلافة ووشى إلى عبيد الله بن زياد عنه أنه ينكر قتل الحسين ونحو ذلك فأمر بجلده وحبسه حتى أرسل بن عمر يشفع فيه فنفاه إلى الطائف فأقام بها حتى مات يزيد بن معاوية وقام بن الزبير في طلب الخلافة فحضر إليه وعاضده وناصحه حتى استأذنه في التوجه للكوفة ليصعد عبد الله بن مطيع في الدعاء إلى طاعته فوثق به ووصى عليه وكان منه ما كان ثم قوى مصعب بن الزبير أمير البصرة عن أخيه عبد الله بن الزبير على المختار بكثير من أهل الكوفة ممن كان دخل في طاعة المختار ورجع عنه لما تبين له من تخليطه وأكاذيبه وقد ذكر محمد بن سعد في ترجمة محمد بن الحنفية من ذلك أشياء فلما التقى المختار ومصعب خذل المختار أولئك الذين كانوا معه فحوصر المختار في القصر إلى أن قتل هو ومن معه ثم لما انقضى أمر المختار سار عبد الملك بن مروان بعد قليل بجيوش الشام إلى مصعب بن الزبير فقتل واستولى عبد الملك على البصرة ثم على الكوفة وذكر عبد الملك بن عمر أنه رأى عبيد الله بن زياد وقد أتى برأس الحسين ثم رأى المختار وقد أتى برأس عبيد الله بن زياد ثم رأى مصعب بن الزبير وقد أتى برأس المختار ثم رأى عبد الملك وقد أتى برأس مصعب
records.english:
ibn Masʿūd al-Thaqafī. His lineage will appear in the notice on his father among the kunyahs. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr mentioned him and said: His kunyah was Abū Isḥāq, though he was by no means ‘the Chosen.’ His father was among the eminent Companions and will appear among the kunyahs. Al-Mukhtār was born in the year of the Hijrah and had neither companionship nor sight of the Prophet. The reports about him are discreditable, related by trustworthy men such as al-Shaʿbī and others. He sought political power and gained control of Kufa until Muṣʿab ibn al-Zubayr killed him there in the year 67. Before that he had been counted among people of merit and goodness, until he broke with Ibn al-Zubayr. He adorned himself with the claim of seeking vengeance for al-Ḥusayn's blood while secretly seeking worldly power, resorting to lies and madness. His rule lasted sixteen months. He said: Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl narrated from Abū ʿAwānah, from Mughīrah, from Thābit ibn Hurmuz, who said: Al-Mukhtār carried money from al-Madāʾin, from his paternal uncle, to ʿAlī. He took out a purse containing fifteen dirhams and said, ‘This is from the wages of prostitutes.’ ʿAlī said to him, ‘Woe to you! What have I to do with prostitutes?’ Then al-Mukhtār rose while wearing a red cloak. When he departed, ʿAlī said, ‘What is the matter with him? قاتله الله. If his heart were split open now, it would be found full of love for al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā.’ It is said that at the beginning of his career he was a Khārijite, then became a Zaydī, and then a Rāfiḍī. Al-Mukhtār unjustly killed Muḥammad ibn ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir because he asked him to relate a fabricated report from his father; when he refused, al-Mukhtār killed him. This is what Abū ʿUmar mentioned in his notice. He stated decisively that al-Mukhtār's father was a Companion and that al-Mukhtār was born in the year of the Hijrah. It has been explained more than once that no one of Quraysh or Thaqīf remained in Mecca or al-Ṭāʾif without attending the Farewell Pilgrimage. Al-Mukhtār therefore belongs in this section, although the reports about him are bad. Ibn al-Athīr added a little to Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr's notice, including the statement: ‘There was between al-Mukhtār and al-Shaʿbī something that required that neither one's words about the other be accepted.’ Ibn al-Athīr inserted this into Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr's words, but it is not found there and is not sound. Al-Shaʿbī was not alone in what he related about al-Mukhtār; al-Shaʿbī's trustworthiness is unanimously accepted, whereas the reverse is true of al-Mukhtār. A number of the Prophet's household bore witness against him for claiming prophethood and telling explicit lies. Among the reports concerning this is what Aḥmad transmitted in the Musnad of ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥamiq by way of al-Suddī, from Rifāʿah al-Qitbānī, who said: I entered upon al-Mukhtār. He tossed me a cushion and said, ‘Were it not that my brother Gabriel had risen from this one’—pointing to another cushion near him—‘I would have tossed it to you.’ He said: I wanted to strike off his head, but then he related an account and a report from ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥamiq. Ibn Ḥibbān said in the notice on Ṣafiyyah bint Abī ʿUbayd in al-Thiqāt: She was the sister of al-Mukhtār, the false prophet in Iraq. The strongest condemnation transmitted concerning him is what Muslim narrated in his Ṣaḥīḥ from Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr: the Messenger of God ﷺ said, ‘Among Thaqīf there will be a liar and a destroyer.’ Asmāʾ testified that the liar was this al-Mukhtār. Ibn al-Athīr said: Al-Mukhtār rose to seek vengeance for al-Ḥusayn. A great many of the Shiʿah in Kufa gathered around him, and he gained control of it. He pursued al-Ḥusayn's killers and killed them: he killed Shimr ibn Dhī al-Jawshan, who personally took part in killing al-Ḥusayn; Khawlī ibn Yazīd, who carried his head to Kufa; and ʿUmar ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, commander of the army that fought al-Ḥusayn until they killed him. He also killed ʿUmar's son Ḥafṣ with him. He sent Ibrāhīm ibn al-Ashtar with a large army, and they met ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Ziyād, who had dispatched the army against al-Ḥusayn. They fought, and ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Ziyād was killed in that battle. Ibn al-Athīr said: For that reason many Muslims loved al-Mukhtār, for he performed admirably in this matter. He used to send money to Ibn ʿUmar, his brother-in-law through marriage to al-Mukhtār's sister Ṣafiyyah bint Abī ʿUbayd, and to Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah, and they accepted it. Muṣʿab then marched against him from Basra and killed al-Mukhtār. End quote. Al-Mukhtār's affair began when Ibn al-Zubayr sent him to Kufa to strengthen allegiance to him, with ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muṭīʿ appointed governor of Kufa. Al-Mukhtār claimed that Ibn al-Zubayr had secretly called for vengeance for al-Ḥusayn's blood. Then, wishing to strengthen his own position, he claimed that Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah was the Mahdī who would emerge at the end of time, that he had ordered al-Mukhtār to call people to pledge allegiance to him, and he forged a letter in his name. A very large group entered his obedience, strengthening him, and he pursued al-Ḥusayn's killers and killed them. His support among those who loved the Prophet's household thereby increased. Then the conflict occurred between Ibn al-Zubayr, on one side, and Ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah and Ibn ʿAbbās, on the other, because the latter two refused to pledge allegiance. Ibn al-Zubayr confined them and their supporters in the mountain pass. News reached al-Mukhtār, so he sent a large army under Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Jadalī. They stormed Mecca, brought both men out of the pass, and the two went to al-Ṭāʾif. The people thanked al-Mukhtār for that. Concerning it al-Marzubānī recited verses by al-Mukhtār:

I clad myself in a strong coat of mail from Hamdān,
turning lofty spears back with noses ground in dust.
They aided the family of the Messenger Muḥammad
when a great calamity had overwhelmed the people.
They were faithful when they gave their pledge to their imam,
and they kept the sword of injustice away from Islam.

Ibn Saʿd reported from al-Wāqidī, through his chains, that Abū ʿUbayd, al-Mukhtār's father, came from al-Ṭāʾif during ʿUmar's time, when ʿUmar summoned the people to Iraq. Abū ʿUbayd set out and was martyred on the Day of the Bridge. His children remained in Medina, and Ibn ʿUmar married Ṣafiyyah bint Abī ʿUbayd. Al-Mukhtār stayed in Medina attached to Banū Hāshim, then was with ʿAlī in Iraq and lived in Basra after ʿAlī. He had an episode with al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī when al-Ḥasan assumed the caliphate. Someone informed ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Ziyād about al-Mukhtār, saying that he denounced al-Ḥusayn's killing and similar things, so Ibn Ziyād ordered him flogged and imprisoned. Ibn ʿUmar sent an intercession for him, so Ibn Ziyād banished him to al-Ṭāʾif. He remained there until Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiyah died and Ibn al-Zubayr rose to seek the caliphate. Al-Mukhtār came to him, supported him, and gave him sincere counsel, until he asked permission to go to Kufa to assist ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muṭīʿ in calling people to obey Ibn al-Zubayr. Ibn al-Zubayr trusted him and commended him to Ibn Muṭīʿ, after which what happened, happened. Later Muṣʿab ibn al-Zubayr, governor of Basra for his brother ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, was strengthened against al-Mukhtār by many Kufans who had entered al-Mukhtār's obedience but left him when his confusion and lies became clear to them. Muḥammad ibn Saʿd mentioned some of this in the notice on Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah. When al-Mukhtār and Muṣʿab met, those who had been with al-Mukhtār deserted him. Al-Mukhtār was besieged in the palace until he and those with him were killed. Not long after al-Mukhtār's affair ended, ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān marched with the armies of Syria against Muṣʿab ibn al-Zubayr, killed him, and took control first of Basra and then of Kufa. ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmar said that he saw ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Ziyād after al-Ḥusayn's head had been brought to him; then he saw al-Mukhtār after ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Ziyād's head had been brought to him; then he saw Muṣʿab ibn al-Zubayr after al-Mukhtār's head had been brought to him; and then he saw ʿAbd al-Malik after Muṣʿab's head had been brought to him.

names.arabic: المختار بن أبي عبيد بن مسعود الثقفي
names.english: al-Mukhtār ibn Abī ʿUbayd ibn Masʿūd al-Thaqafī

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: روى أنه أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليبايعه فقبض يده عنه لخلوق رآه فيها وذكره بن عبد البر فقال في حديثه اضطراب وفي صحبته نظر فإن كان جد عقبة بن أبي معيط فلا صحبة له ولا لقاء ولا رؤية وإن كان الحديث عن أبيه فلا يصح أيضا انتهى وذكر بن قانع في الصحابة فقال مدرك بن عمارة وأورده من طريق بن أبي زائدة عنه قال مررت في مسجد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في ناحية هكذا عنده
records.english: It is related that he came to the Prophet ﷺ to pledge allegiance to him. The Prophet withheld his hand because of the saffron perfume he saw on it. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr mentioned him and said: His report is inconsistent, and his companionship is questionable. If he was the grandfather of ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ, then he had neither companionship, meeting, nor sight; and if the report was from his father, it is not sound either. End quote. Ibn Qāniʿ mentioned him among the Companions as Mudrik ibn ʿUmārah and cited by way of Ibn Abī Zāʾidah, from him, that he said: I passed through the mosque of the Messenger of God ﷺ while the Prophet ﷺ was at one side. That is how he gave it.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكره المستغفري وأخرج من حديث جابر قال أعتق رجل من الأنصار غلاما له عن دبر يسمى مذكورا الحديث وهذا وهم من محاضر راويه عن الأعمش عن سلمة بن كهيل عن عطاء عنه والحديث معروف عن جابر لكن اسم العبد يعقوب والذي دبره هو أبو مذكور فانقلب وتحرف
records.english: Al-Mustaghfirī mentioned him and transmitted from the report of Jābir, who said: A man of the Anṣār arranged for a slave of his named Madhkūr to be freed after his death—the report. This was an error by Muḥāḍir, its narrator from al-Aʿmash, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Jābir. The report from Jābir is well known, but the slave's name was Yaʿqūb and the man who made the posthumous manumission arrangement was Abū Madhkūr. The names were reversed and corrupted.

heading.english: Mīm followed by dhāl and rāʾ

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: اليمامي الحنفي تقدم نسبه في ترجمة ولده مجاعة قال بن منده له ولولده مجاعة وفادة ثم أورد من طريق بن أبي عاصم قال حدثنا الجراح بن مخلد حدثنا يحيى بن راشد حدثنا الحارث بن مرة الحنفي عن سراج بن مجاعة بن مرارة عن مرارة عن أبيه عن جده قال أتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأقطعني وكتب لي كتابا الحديث وأخرجه أبو نعيم من طريق بن أبي عاصم وأشار إلى أنه خطأ ولم يبين وجه الوهم فيه وبيانه أنه سقط اسم شيخ الحارث بن مرة وهو هلال بن سراج بن مجاعة بن مرارة ومدار الحديث على سراج بن مجاعة وجده مرارة فخرج منه أن القصة لمرارة وليس كذلك وقد أخرج البغوي عن زياد بن أيوب عن عنبسة بن عبد الواحد عن الدخيل بن إياس عن عمه هلال بن سراج بن مجاعة عن أبيه سراج قال أعطى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مجاعة بن مرارة أرضا الحديث
records.english: al-Yamāmī al-Ḥanafī. His lineage appeared previously in the notice on his son Mujjāʿah. Ibn Mandah said: He and his son Mujjāʿah came as delegates. He then transmitted by way of Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim, who said: al-Jarrāḥ ibn Makhlad related to us; Yaḥyā ibn Rāshid related to us; al-Ḥārith ibn Murrah al-Ḥanafī related to us, from Sirāj ibn Mujjāʿah ibn Murārah, from Murārah, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: I came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he granted me a tract and wrote a document for me—the report. Abū Nuʿaym also transmitted it by way of Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim and indicated that it was erroneous, though he did not explain the error. Its explanation is that the name of al-Ḥārith ibn Murrah's shaykh fell out: he was Hilāl ibn Sirāj ibn Mujjāʿah ibn Murārah. The report revolves around Sirāj ibn Mujjāʿah and his grandfather Murārah, which made the event appear to concern Murārah, but that is not so. Al-Baghawī transmitted from Ziyād ibn Ayyūb, from ʿAnbasah ibn ʿAbd al-Wāḥid, from al-Dukhayl ibn Iyās, from his paternal uncle Hilāl ibn Sirāj ibn Mujjāʿah, from his father Sirāj, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ granted Mujjāʿah ibn Murārah some land—the report.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: أورده بن قانع وأخرج من طريق أبي الأشهب عبد الملك بن عمير عن أبي روح مر ذي الكلاع قال صلى بنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صلاة الصبح فقرأ بسورة الروم فتردد في آية الحديث قال بن قانع كذا قال ورواه زائدة عن عبد الملك عن شبيب أبي روح قلت وقع في الرواية الأولى تصحيف والصواب من بكسر الميم بعدها نون ساكنة وأما قوله مر بضم الميم وتشديد الراء فهو تصحيف وقد تقدم القول فيه في حرف الشين المعجمة
records.english: Ibn Qāniʿ included him. He transmitted by way of Abū al-Ashhab ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from Abū Rawḥ Murr Dhī al-Kalāʿ, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ led us in the dawn prayer and recited Sūrat al-Rūm, but hesitated over a verse—the report. Ibn Qāniʿ said: That is how he gave it. Zāʾidah narrated it from ʿAbd al-Malik, from Shabīb Abī Rawḥ. I say: The first transmission contains a scribal corruption. The correct word is ‘from,’ with kasrah on the mīm followed by a vowelless nūn. The reading ‘Murr,’ with ḍammah on the mīm and a doubled rāʾ, is a scribal corruption. Discussion of him appeared previously under the dotted letter shīn.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: العبدي ذكره بن قانع هكذا فيه تخليط فإنه أورد من طريق طالب بن حجير عن هود بن عبد الله سمعت مرثدا العبدي يقول كنت عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فجاء أشج عبد القيس الحديث وهو غلط نشأ عن تصحيف وإنما هو مزيدة وهو جد هود بن عبد الله لأمه وقد تقدم على الصواب في القسم الأول وفي الصحابة مرثد بن ظبيان أيضا وهو السدوسي تقدم قريبا
records.english: al-ʿAbdī. Ibn Qāniʿ mentioned him in this form, but it is confused. He transmitted by way of Ṭālib ibn Ḥujayr, from Hūd ibn ʿAbd Allāh: I heard Marthad al-ʿAbdī say, ‘I was with the Prophet ﷺ when al-Ashajj of ʿAbd al-Qays came...’—the report. This is an error caused by a scribal corruption. He is actually Mazīdah, the maternal grandfather of Hūd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, and he appeared correctly in the first section. Among the Companions there was also Marthad ibn Ẓabyān, al-Sadūsī, who appeared recently.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: هو بن عقفان الذي تقدم جعله الذهبي اثنين وهو واحد والله أعلم
records.english: He is ibn ʿAqfān, who appeared earlier. Al-Dhahabī made them two men, but they are one. والله أعلم.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الفهري روت عنه بنته أم سعد حديثا ذكره الذهبي أيضا فغاير بينه وبين مرة بن عمرو حبيب الذي تقدم في الأول وهو واحد وإنما نسب إلى جده
records.english: al-Fihrī. His daughter Umm Saʿd narrated a report from him. Al-Dhahabī also mentioned him but distinguished him from Murrah ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥabīb, who appeared previously in the first section. They are one person; he was merely ascribed to his grandfather.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الداري كذا وقع في رواية الواقدي وسماه غيره مران وقد تقدم وهو الصواب
records.english: al-Dārī. This is how the name appears in al-Wāqidī's transmission. Others called him Murrān, which appeared previously and is correct.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكره أبو عمر كذا في التجريد والذي في الاستيعاب مرارة كما تقدم وهو الصواب
records.english: Abū ʿUmar mentioned him in this form, according to al-Tajrīd. The form in al-Istīʿāb is Murārah, as appeared previously, and it is correct.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: أخرج البغوي من طرق محمد بن جحادة عن محمد بن عجلان عن بنت مرة الهمداني عن أبيها أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال كافل اليتيم له أو لغيره إذا اتقى معي في الجنة كهاتين يعني المسبحة والوسطى وقد تقدم في مرة بن عمرو بن حبيب الفهري من بني محارب بن فهر من طريق صفوان بن سليم وغيره عن أم سعد بنت مرة الفهري عن أبيها وهو المحفوظ والله أعلم
records.english: Al-Baghawī transmitted by routes from Muḥammad ibn Juḥādah. The routes continue from Muḥammad ibn Juḥādah, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAjlān, from the daughter of Murrah al-Hamdānī, from her father, that the Prophet ﷺ said, ‘The guardian of an orphan, whether related to him or unrelated, if he is mindful of God, will be with me in Paradise like these two’—meaning the index and middle fingers. A preserved version appeared previously under Murrah ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥabīb al-Fihrī, of Banū Muḥārib ibn Fihr, by way of Ṣafwān ibn Sulaym and others, from Umm Saʿd bint Murrah al-Fihrī, from her father. والله أعلم.

names.arabic: مرة بن عمرو بن حبيب الفهري
names.english: Murrah ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥabīb al-Fihrī

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الجهني كذا ذكره بن منده والصواب مسروح بن ياسر كما تقدم في الأول
records.english: al-Juhanī. Ibn Mandah mentioned him in this form. The correct name is Masrūḥ ibn Yāsir, as appeared previously in the first section.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن عمرو الفهري صحابي شهد فتح مصر واختط بها قاله بن يونس قال وتوفي بالإسكندرية سنة خمس وأربعين روى عنه علي بن رباح وورقاء بن شريح هكذا أورده الذهبي في التجريد وعلم له علامات بقي بن مخلد بحديث واحد ثم قال بعده المستورد بن شداد بن عمرو الفهري صحابي نزل الكوفة ثم مصر روى عنه جماعة وهذان واحد وقع في اسم أبيه تغيير والصواب كما في الثاني شداد وكذا هو في كتاب بن يونس
records.english: ibn ʿAmr al-Fihrī, a Companion who witnessed the conquest of Egypt and took up a plot there, according to Ibn Yūnus. He said that al-Mustawrid died in Alexandria in the year 45. ʿAlī ibn Rabāḥ and Warqāʾ ibn Shurayḥ narrated from him. Al-Dhahabī cited him in this form in al-Tajrīd, marked him with Baqī ibn Makhlad's symbols for one report, and then immediately listed al-Mustawrid ibn Shaddād ibn ʿAmr al-Fihrī, a Companion who settled first in Kufa and then in Egypt, from whom a group narrated. These two are one person; his father's name was altered. The correct form is the second, Shaddād, and that is also how it appears in Ibn Yūnus's book.

names.arabic: المستورد بن سلامة بن عمرو الفهري
names.english: al-Mustawrid ibn Salāmah ibn ʿAmr al-Fihrī

names.arabic: المستورد بن شداد بن عمرو الفهري
names.english: al-Mustawrid ibn Shaddād ibn ʿAmr al-Fihrī

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: صاحب الجيوش كذا نسبه الذهبي في التجريد لمسند بقي بن مخلد والصواب بن مسعدة وقد ذكروا أن اسمه عبد الله وقد تقدم في الأول
records.english: the commander of the armies. Al-Dhahabī attributed him in this form in al-Tajrīd to the Musnad of Baqī ibn Makhlad. The correct form is Ibn Masʿadah. They stated that his name was ʿAbd Allāh, and he appeared previously in the first section.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: فرق أبو نعيم بينه وبين مسعود بن أوس بن أصرم واستدركه يحيى بن عبد الوهاب بن منده على جده وتعقبه أبو موسى في الذيل فأجاد فإنه واحد وقد ذكره بن منده كما تقدم
records.english: Abū Nuʿaym distinguished him from Masʿūd ibn Aws ibn Aṣram, and Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn Mandah added him in correction of his grandfather. Abū Mūsā rebutted that in the Supplement and did well, for they are one person, whom Ibn Mandah had already mentioned as stated previously.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن عامر بن مخلد بن زريق الأنصاري الزرقي ذكره جعفر المستغفري وحرف اسم والده وإنما هو مسعود بن خالد كما تقدم على الصواب
records.english: ibn ʿĀmir ibn Makhlad ibn Zurayq al-Anṣārī al-Zuraqī. Jaʿfar al-Mustaghfirī mentioned him but corrupted his father's name. He is actually Masʿūd ibn Khālid, as appeared previously in the correct form.

names.arabic: مسعود بن خلدة بن عامر بن مخلد بن زريق الأنصاري الزرقي
names.english: Masʿūd ibn Khaladah ibn ʿĀmir ibn Makhlad ibn Zurayq al-Anṣārī al-Zuraqī

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن قيس بن خلدة هو الذي قبله وإنما وقع في نسبه تحريف كرره أبو عمر بلا فائدة
records.english: ibn Qays ibn Khaladah. He is the preceding person; a corruption occurred in his lineage, and Abū ʿUmar repeated him without benefit.

names.arabic: مسعود بن سعد بن قيس بن خلدة
names.english: Masʿūd ibn Saʿd ibn Qays ibn Khaladah

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: السلمي فرق بن الأثير بينه وبين مسعود بن سنان الأسلمي وهو واحد كما بينته في الأول
records.english: al-Sulamī. Ibn al-Athīr distinguished him from Masʿūd ibn Sinān al-Aslamī, but they are one person, as I explained in the first section.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن عامر هو مسعود بن سعد بن عامر جعله أبو عمر اثنين وهو واحد واختلف في تسمية أبيه
records.english: ibn ʿĀmir. He is Masʿūd ibn Saʿd ibn ʿĀmir. Abū ʿUmar made them two men, but they are one; there was disagreement over his father's name.

names.arabic: مسعود بن عبد سعد بن عامر
names.english: Masʿūd ibn ʿAbd Saʿd ibn ʿĀmir

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: اللخمي غاير بن منده بينه وبين مسعود بن الضحاك بن عدي نسبه بن منده إلى جده فاستدركه أبو موسى وهو واحد
records.english: al-Lakhmī. Ibn Mandah treated him as different from Masʿūd ibn al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn ʿAdī, having ascribed the latter to his grandfather. Abū Mūsā therefore added him, but they are one person.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن ربيعة القاري غاير الذهبي بينه وبين مسعود بن ربيعة بن عمرو وهو واحد اختلف في اسم أبيه والثاني هو الأصح وقد نسبه أبو عمر إلى جده فقال هو مسعود بن عمرو القاري ويحتمل أن يكون الثاني عم الأول وقد تقدم في الأول
records.english: ibn Rabīʿah al-Qārī. Al-Dhahabī treated him as different from Masʿūd ibn Rabīʿah ibn ʿAmr, but they are one person. There was disagreement over his father's name, and the second form is more correct. Abū ʿUmar ascribed him to his grandfather and called him Masʿūd ibn ʿAmr al-Qārī. It is also possible that the second man was the paternal uncle of the first. This appeared previously in the first section.

names.arabic: مسعود بن عمار بن ربيعة القاري
names.english: Masʿūd ibn ʿAmmār ibn Rabīʿah al-Qārī

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن خلدة بن مخلد الزرقي ذكره أبو عمر فقال شهد بدرا كذا قال بن الكلبي وفيه نظر قلت مسعود بن سعد بن قيس إلى آخر النسب سقط ذكر أبيه فنسب إلى جده فأشكل أمره
records.english: ibn Khaladah ibn Makhlad al-Zuraqī. Abū ʿUmar mentioned him and said, ‘He witnessed Badr; that is what Ibn al-Kalbī said.’ This is questionable. I say: He is Masʿūd ibn Saʿd ibn Qays, followed by the rest of the lineage. His father's name fell out and he was ascribed to his grandfather, making his identity obscure.

names.arabic: مسعود بن قيس بن خلدة بن مخلد الزرقي
names.english: Masʿūd ibn Qays ibn Khaladah ibn Makhlad al-Zuraqī

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن خباب مختلف في صحبة أبيه وأما هو فأرسل شيئا وذكره البغوي في الصحابة وقال لا أحسب له صحبة قال وقد قيل إنه روى عن أبيه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم انتهى وله رواية أيضا عن أمه وعن أم رافع وحديثه المذكور أخرجه النسائي والبغوي وغيرهما من رواية سليمان بن يسار عنه قال قالوا يا رسول الله كيف نستغفر فذكر الحديث ووقع في رواية النسائي عن سليمان عن مسلم بن السائب عن خباب بن الأرت وقوله بن الأرت خطأ والصواب حذفه ويكون الحديث لخباب جد مسلم وإليه أشار البغوي وقال أبو حاتم الرازي روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مرسلا وهو من التابعين وأدخله بعضهم في الحصابة ظنا منهم أن له صحبة وليس كذلك وقال أبو أحمد العسكري حديثه مرسل وذكره بن حبان في ثقات التابعين وقال يروي المراسيل وكذا ذكره البخاري وغير واحد في التابعين
records.english: ibn Khabbāb. There is disagreement over his father's companionship. As for Muslim, he transmitted something in disconnected form. Al-Baghawī mentioned him among the Companions and said, ‘I do not think he had companionship.’ He said: It has also been stated that he narrated from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ. End quote. He also narrated from his mother and from Umm Rāfiʿ. His cited report was transmitted by al-Nasāʾī, al-Baghawī, and others from the narration of Sulaymān ibn Yasār, from him. He said: They asked, ‘O Messenger of God, how should we seek forgiveness?’ and he related the report. In al-Nasāʾī's narration it reads: from Sulaymān, from Muslim ibn al-Sāʾib, from Khabbāb ibn al-Aratt. The words ‘ibn al-Aratt’ are an error and should be omitted, making the report belong to Khabbāb, Muslim's grandfather. Al-Baghawī alluded to this. Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī said: He narrated in disconnected form from the Prophet ﷺ and was one of the Successors. Some included him among the Companions because they supposed that he had companionship, but that is not so. Abū Aḥmad al-ʿAskarī said that his report was disconnected. Ibn Ḥibbān mentioned him among the trustworthy Successors and said that he narrated disconnected reports. Al-Bukhārī and more than one other authority likewise listed him among the Successors.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكره بعضهم في الصحابة لحديث أرسله قال بن أبي حاتم عن أبيه روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مرسلا وكذا قال العسكري
records.english: Some mentioned him among the Companions because of a report he transmitted as mursal. Ibn Abī Ḥātim reported from his father that he narrated from the Prophet ﷺ in disconnected form. Al-ʿAskarī said the same.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن عبد الله بن مسلم بن شهاب الزهري والد الإمام بن شهاب الزهري روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وفي قصة أبي رغال فذكره بعضهم في الصحابة وجزم غير واحد بأنه لا صحبة له ولا رؤية وقال البخاري وأبو حاتم حديثه مرسل وكذا قال أبو أحمد العسكري
records.english: ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muslim ibn Shihāb al-Zuhrī, father of the imam Ibn Shihāb al-Zuhrī. He narrated from the Prophet ﷺ in the account of Abū Righāl, so some mentioned him among the Companions. More than one authority stated decisively that he had neither companionship nor sight of the Prophet. Al-Bukhārī and Abū Ḥātim said that his report was disconnected, as did Abū Aḥmad al-ʿAskarī.

names.arabic: مسلم بن عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن مسلم بن شهاب الزهري
names.english: Muslim ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muslim ibn Shihāb al-Zuhrī

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن محارب بن فهر استدركه أبو موسى وقال هو والد حبيب بن مسلمة وعزاه للمستغفري والصواب أنه مسلمة بن مالك كما تقدم في القسم الأول سقط بينه وبين شيبان ستة آباء وهو مسلمة بن مالك بن وهب بن ثعلبة بن وائلة بن عمرو بن شيبان بن محارب
records.english: ibn Muḥārib ibn Fihr. Abū Mūsā added him, said he was the father of Ḥabīb ibn Maslamah, and attributed the notice to al-Mustaghfirī. The correct identity is Maslamah ibn Mālik, as appeared previously in the first section. Six forefathers between him and Shaybān were omitted. He is Maslamah ibn Mālik ibn Wahb ibn Thaʿlabah ibn Wāʾilah ibn ʿAmr ibn Shaybān ibn Muḥārib.

names.arabic: مسلمة بن مالك بن وهب بن ثعلبة بن وائلة بن عمرو بن شيبان بن محارب
names.english: Maslamah ibn Mālik ibn Wahb ibn Thaʿlabah ibn Wāʾilah ibn ʿAmr ibn Shaybān ibn Muḥārib

names.arabic: مسلمة بن شيبان بن محارب بن فهر
names.english: Maslamah ibn Shaybān ibn Muḥārib ibn Fihr

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: العدوي تابعي أرسل حديثا فذكره بعضهم في الصحابة أورده العسكري وقال حديثه مرسل
records.english: al-ʿAdawī, a Successor. He transmitted a report in disconnected form, so some mentioned him among the Companions. Al-ʿAskarī cited him and said that his report was disconnected.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: أحد من شهد في عهد العلاء بن الحضرمي استدركه بن فتحون والذهبي وهو خطأ نشأ عن تصحيف وتغيير وإنما هو المستنير بن أبي صعصعة وقد تقدم علي الصواب في الأول
records.english: one of those present in the time of al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Ḥaḍramī. Ibn Fatḥūn and al-Dhahabī added him, but this is an error caused by scribal corruption and alteration. He is actually al-Mustanīr ibn Abī Ṣaʿṣaʿah, who appeared correctly in the first section.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن عمرو اليامي ذكره بن أبي حاتم وقال له صحبة كذا نقله عنه بن فتحون وهو وهم ولفظة بن أبي حاتم مصرف بن كعب بن عمرو روى عن أبيه قال بعضهم له صحبة فالضمير في قوله له يعود على أبيه وهو كعب وقد تقدم بيان الاختلاف فيه في كعب بن عمرو وفي عمرو بن كعب والرواية جاءت من طريق ليث بن أبي سليم عن طلحة بن مصرف عن أبيه عن جده عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فالجد هو الذي قيل إن له صحبة ورواية عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم واختلف في اسمه وأما مصرف فليس بصحابي جزما
records.english: ibn ʿAmr al-Yāmī. Ibn Abī Ḥātim mentioned him and said that he had companionship; Ibn Fatḥūn quoted him in this form, but it is an error. Ibn Abī Ḥātim's wording is: ‘Miṣraf ibn Kaʿb ibn ʿAmr narrated from his father; some said that he had companionship.’ The pronoun in ‘he had’ refers to his father, Kaʿb. The disagreement concerning him was explained previously under Kaʿb ibn ʿAmr and ʿAmr ibn Kaʿb. The narration came by way of Layth ibn Abī Sulaym, from Ṭalḥah ibn Miṣraf, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet ﷺ. Thus it was the grandfather who was said to have companionship and narration from the Prophet ﷺ, although there was disagreement over his name. As for Miṣraf, he was certainly not a Companion.

names.arabic: مصرف بن كعب بن عمرو اليامي
names.english: Muṣarrif ibn Kaʿb ibn ʿAmr al-Yāmī

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكره البغوي في حرف الميم من الصحابة وأورد من طريق سويد بن عفلة قال أتانا مصدق النبي فقال فذكر الحديث وكأنه توهم أنه علم وأما النبي فكأنه لم يضبطه فيجوز أن يكون صفة أو نسبا وليس كذلك وإنما هو اسم فاعل من الصدقة والنبي بالنون والموحدة مضاف وهذا محله في المبهمات
records.english: Al-Baghawī mentioned him under the letter mīm among the Companions and cited by way of Suwayd ibn Ghafalah, who said: ‘The Prophet's alms collector came to us...’ and related the report. Al-Baghawī appears to have supposed that Muṣaddiq was a proper name and not to have understood al-Nabī, perhaps treating it as a description or a lineage. That is not so. Muṣaddiq is an active participle derived from alms, and al-Nabī—with nūn and bāʾ—is annexed to it. Its proper place is among the anonymous persons.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكره يحيى بن يونس الشيرازي في الصحابة وتعقبه جعفر بأنه تابعي وحديثه مرسل ورواه قرة عن قتادة في قصة مرثد بن ظبيان فروى عنه عن مرثد وروى عنه مرسلا وقد روى مضارب وهو بن حرب العجلي رواية عن علي وغيره
records.english: Yaḥyā ibn Yūnus al-Shīrāzī mentioned him among the Companions, but Jaʿfar objected that he was a Successor and his report was disconnected. Qurrah narrated it from Qatādah in the account of Marthad ibn Ẓabyān, both narrating through Muḍārib from Marthad and narrating it from Muḍārib in disconnected form. Muḍārib—who was Ibn Ḥarb al-ʿIjlī—also narrated from ʿAlī and others.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: والد بشر تقدم في ترجمة أبيه وهو مختلق
records.english: the father of Bishr. He appeared previously in the notice on his father and is fabricated.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن سواد بن مالك بن غنم ذكره البغوي عن يحيى بن سعيد الأموي عن أبيه عن بن إسحاق أنه ذكره فيمن شهد بدرا واستدركه بن فتحون وهو وهم نشأ عن سقط وهو معاذ بن رفاعة بن الحارث بن سواد فسقط من النسب رجلان وقد تقدم على الصواب في الأول وهو المعروف بابن عفراء
records.english: ibn Sawād ibn Mālik ibn Ghanm. Al-Baghawī mentioned him from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Umawī, from his father, from Ibn Isḥāq, who listed him among those who witnessed Badr. Ibn Fatḥūn added him, but this is an error caused by an omission. He is Muʿādh ibn Rifāʿah ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Sawād: two men fell out of the lineage. He appeared correctly in the first section and is known as Ibn ʿAfrāʾ.

names.arabic: معاذ بن الحارث بن سواد بن مالك بن غنم
names.english: Muʿādh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Sawād ibn Mālik ibn Ghanm

names.arabic: معاذ بن رفاعة بن الحارث بن سواد
names.english: Muʿādh ibn Rifāʿah ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Sawād

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكره بعضهم في الصحابة والصحبة إنما هي لولده أبي زهير بن معاذ وسيأتي في الكنى
records.english: Some mentioned him among the Companions, but companionship belonged only to his son, Abū Zuhayr ibn Muʿādh, who will appear among the kunyahs.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكره يحيى بن يونس الشيرازي في الصحابة وهو تابعي أرسل حديثا أخرجه أبو داود في المراسيل وقال جعفر المستغفري وهم من زعم أن له صحبة وقال البخاري عن يحيى بن معين حديثه مرسل وقد ذكره البغوي في الصحابة ولكنه قال لا أدري له صحبة أم لا
records.english: Yaḥyā ibn Yūnus al-Shīrāzī mentioned him among the Companions, but he was a Successor who transmitted a report in disconnected form. Abū Dāwūd transmitted it in al-Marāsīl. Jaʿfar al-Mustaghfirī said: Whoever claimed that he had companionship erred. Al-Bukhārī reported from Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn that his report was disconnected. Al-Baghawī mentioned him among the Companions but said, ‘I do not know whether he had companionship or not.’

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: استدركه الذهبي في التجريد وقال له حديث في المنتقى من حديث المخلص قلت هو من رواية عبد الحكيم بن أبي المخارق عن سنان بن سلمة عنه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من عطب له هدي فلينحره الحديث واختلف فيه على عبد الكريم مع ضعفه فقيل عنه عن سنان بن سلمة عن سلمة بن المحبق عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقيل عن عبد الكريم عن معاذ بن سعوة عن سنان بن سلمة عن سلمة بن المحبق وقد ذكره البخاري في التابعين وقال حديثه مرسل
records.english: Al-Dhahabī added him in al-Tajrīd and said that he had a report in al-Muntaqā from the reports of al-Mukhalliṣ. I say: It is narrated by ʿAbd al-Ḥakīm ibn Abī al-Makhāriq, from Sinān ibn Salamah, from him, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said, ‘Whoever has a sacrificial animal become disabled should slaughter it...’—the report. There was disagreement over it from ʿAbd al-Karīm, in addition to his weakness. One version is from him, from Sinān ibn Salamah, from Salamah ibn al-Muḥabbiq, from the Prophet ﷺ. Another is from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from Muʿādh ibn Saʿwah, from Sinān ibn Salamah, from Salamah ibn al-Muḥabbiq. Al-Bukhārī mentioned Muʿādh among the Successors and said that his report was disconnected.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: روى عمران بن حدير عنه أن قطبة بن جرير أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فبايعه قال أبو عمر قيل إن حديثه مرسل قلت أخذ تسميته من بن أبي حاتم وإنما هو مقاتل بن معدان وقد سماه على الصواب في ترجمة قطبة في موضعين ومقاتل تابعي باتفاق وقطبة هو أبو الحويصلة تقدم في القاف في الأول
records.english: ʿImrān ibn Ḥudayr narrated from him that Quṭbah ibn Jarīr came to the Prophet ﷺ and pledged allegiance to him. Abū ʿUmar said: It is said that his report was disconnected. I say: He took this name from Ibn Abī Ḥātim, but the correct name is Muqātil ibn Maʿdān. He named him correctly in two places in the notice on Quṭbah. Muqātil was a Successor by agreement, and Quṭbah is Abū al-Ḥuwayṣilah, who appeared previously under qāf in the first section.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الحماني تابعي أرسل حديثا فذكره الإسماعيلي في الصحابة وقال لا أدري له صحبة أو لا وأخرج من طريق عامر بن السمط عن أبي الجحاف عنه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يا علي من أحبك فقد أحبنى الحديث أورده أبو موسى وقد ذكر البخاري هذا الحديث من هذا الوجه من رواية معاوية بن ثعلبة عن أبي ذر وكذا ذكره أبو حاتم وغيرهما
records.english: al-Ḥimmānī. He was a Successor. He transmitted a report in disconnected form, so al-Ismāʿīlī mentioned him among the Companions and said, ‘I do not know whether he had companionship or not.’ He transmitted by way of ʿĀmir ibn al-Simṭ, from Abū al-Jaḥḥāf, from him, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said, ‘O ʿAlī, whoever loves you has loved me...’—the report. Abū Mūsā cited it. Al-Bukhārī mentioned this report through the same route as the narration of Muʿāwiyah ibn Thaʿlabah from Abū Dharr. Abū Ḥātim and others likewise gave it that way.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: كذا رأيته بخط الخطيب في المؤتلف وعلي حزن ضبة وأظنه تصحف حزن من حيدة وتقدم في القسم الأول
records.english: Thus I saw it in al-Khaṭīb's handwriting in al-Muʾtalif. The following words, ‘ʿAlī Ḥazn Ḍabbah,’ have no securely recoverable clause boundary. I think Ḥazn is a scribal corruption of Ḥaydah. He appeared previously in the first section.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: تقدمت الإشارة إليه في القسم الأول
records.english: Reference to him appeared earlier in the first section.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الجشمي تقدم ذكره في عبد الله بن أبي بكر بن ربيعة
records.english: al-Jushamī. He was mentioned previously under ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr ibn Rabīʿah.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكره بعضهم وحديثه مرسل قاله العسكري كذا قرأت بخط مغلطاي وأخشى أن يكون معاذ بن زهرة الماضي قريبا
records.english: Some mentioned him, and his report is mursal. This is according to al-ʿAskarī. That is how I read it in Mughlaṭāy's handwriting, though I fear it may actually be Muʿādh ibn Zuhrah, who appeared shortly before.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن عقيل والد كعب الأخيل بن الرجال له وفادة كذا في التجريد وهو غلط نشأ عن سقط وإنما الوفادة لولده هبيرة بن معاوية كما سيأتي في ترجمته في حرف الهاء وأما معاوية فكان يقال له فارس الهزار والهزار فرسه وكان مشهورا في الجاهلية وقد ذكر بن الكلبي أنه هو الذي طعن زهير بن جذيمة رئيس بني عبس في الجاهلية وابنه عامر كان له ذكر في الجاهلية ويقال له بن المفاضة وله ذكر يأتي في ترجمة أخيه هبيرة قلت وكعب المعروف بالأخيل جد قبيلة مشهورة منها ليلى الأخيلية الشاعرة في زمن عبد الملك بن مروان وهي ليلى بنت عبد الله بن معاذ بن شداد بن كعب
records.english: ibn ʿUqayl, father of Kaʿb al-Akhyil ibn al-Rijāl. He came as a delegate, according to al-Tajrīd, but this is an error caused by an omission. The delegation actually belonged to his son Hubayrah ibn Muʿāwiyah, as will appear in his notice under the letter hāʾ. As for Muʿāwiyah, he was called the Horseman of al-Hazzār, al-Hazzār being his horse, and he was famous in the pre-Islamic period. Ibn al-Kalbī stated that he was the one who speared Zuhayr ibn Jadhīmah, chief of Banū ʿAbs, in the pre-Islamic period. His son ʿĀmir was also prominent then and was called Ibn al-Mufāḍah; mention of him will appear in the notice on his brother Hubayrah. I say: Kaʿb, known as al-Akhyal, was the ancestor of a famous tribe that included Laylā al-Akhyaliyyah, the poetess in the time of ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān. She was Laylā bint ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muʿādh ibn Shaddād ibn Kaʿb.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن أبي أحمد أورده بن أبي علي في الصحابة وهو وهم نشأ عن حذف فإنه أورد من طريق عبد الرحمن بن الحارث عن عاصم بن عبيد الله عنه قال رأيت حمنة هي بنت جحش تسقي العطشى وتداوي الجرحى يوم أحد وهذا الحديث إنما رواه معاوية بهذا عن أنس كذا ذكره البخاري وأبو حاتم وغيرهما وذكر أن أبا ضمرة روى عنه وأبو ضمرة لقي بعض التابعين وجده أبو أحمد صحابي مشهور وأبو عبد الله بن أبي أحمد له رؤية وظن الذهبي أنه آخر فقال معاوية بن عبد الله بن أحمد شهد أحدا وما أدري مؤمنا أم كافرا كذا قال وحمنة هي عمة أبيه
records.english: ibn Abī Aḥmad. Ibn Abī ʿAlī cited him among the Companions, but this is an error caused by an omission. He transmitted by way of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith, from ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from him, who said: I saw Ḥamnah—she was bint Jaḥsh—giving water to the thirsty and treating the wounded on the Day of Uḥud. This report was actually narrated by Muʿāwiyah through this chain from Anas, as al-Bukhārī, Abū Ḥātim, and others stated. They mentioned that Abū Ḍamrah narrated from him, and Abū Ḍamrah met some Successors. His grandfather Abū Aḥmad was a famous Companion, and Abū ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Aḥmad had sight of the Prophet. Al-Dhahabī thought he was another person and said, ‘Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad witnessed Uḥud; I do not know whether as a believer or unbeliever.’ That is what he said. Ḥamnah was the paternal aunt of Muʿāwiyah's father.

names.arabic: معاوية بن عبد الله بن أبي أحمد
names.english: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Aḥmad

names.arabic: معاوية بن عبد الله بن أحمد
names.english: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic:
أورده بن قانع في الصحابة وهو وهم فأورد من طريق عاصم بن سويد عن عبد الرحمن عن جده معاوية بن معبد قال كعب بن مالك
زعمت سخينة أن ستغلب ربها
وليغلبن مغالب الغلاب فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم شكر الله قولك
records.english:
Ibn Qāniʿ included him among the Companions. This inclusion is an error. He transmitted by way of ʿĀṣim ibn Suwayd, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from his grandfather Muʿāwiyah ibn Maʿbad, who said that Kaʿb ibn Mālik recited:

Sukhaynah claims that she will overcome her Lord,
but the One who overcomes all contenders will surely overcome her.

The Prophet ﷺ said, شكر الله قولك.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الجهني تابعي أرسل حديثا فذكره بعضهم في الصحابة وقيل هو معبد الجهني الذي كان أول من تكلم في القدر بالبصرة وكان في عصر الصحابة ولا صحبة له فاختلف في اسم أبيه كما تقدم في القسم الأول والله أعلم
records.english: al-Juhanī, a Successor. He transmitted a report in disconnected form, so some mentioned him among the Companions. It is said that he was Maʿbad al-Juhanī, the first to speak about predestination in Basra. He lived in the time of the Companions but had no companionship. There was disagreement over his father's name, as appeared previously in the first section. والله أعلم.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكره أبو نعيم وأورده من طريق إسحاق بن إبراهيم عن سعد بن الصلت عن أبي حنيفة عن منصور بن زادان عن الحسن عن معبد أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بينا هو في صلاته إذ أقبل أعمى فوقع في زبية الحديث وفيه من كان منكم قهقه فليعد الوضوء والصلاة قال أبو نعيم رواه أسد بن عمرو عن أبي حنيفة فقال معبد بن صبيح ورواه مكي بن إبراهيم عن أبي حنيفة فقال معبد بن أبي معبد وساقه أبو موسى هكذا من غير زيادة وأنكر بن الأثير على أبي موسى استدراكه وقال قد أخرج بن منده معبد بن أم معبد وذكر له حديث الضحك في الصلاة فليس لاستدراك أبي موسى له وجه قلت راوي حديث القهقهة قيل هو معبدالجهني الذي كان يتكلم في القدر وقد ذكر في الذي قبله وقيل هو معبد بن أم معبد التي مر بها النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في الهجرة وهذا لا يصح لأن راوي حديث القهقهة جهني وولد أم معبد خزاعي وقد ذكرت ترجمته في القسم الأول وإنما أتى من الاشتراك في الاسم وكنية الأب
records.english: Abū Nuʿaym mentioned him and transmitted by way of Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm, from Saʿd ibn al-Ṣalt, from Abū Ḥanīfah, from Manṣūr ibn Zādhān, from al-Ḥasan, from Maʿbad, that while the Prophet ﷺ was praying, a blind man approached and fell into a pit—the report. It includes: ‘Whoever among you laughed aloud must repeat ablution and the prayer.’ Abū Nuʿaym said: Asad ibn ʿAmr narrated it from Abū Ḥanīfah and called him Maʿbad ibn Ṣabīḥ, while Makkī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated it from Abū Ḥanīfah and called him Maʿbad ibn Abī Maʿbad. Abū Mūsā presented it in this form without addition. Ibn al-Athīr objected to Abū Mūsā's addition and said: Ibn Mandah had already cited Maʿbad ibn Umm Maʿbad and mentioned for him the report about laughter during prayer, so there was no basis for Abū Mūsā to add him. I say: The narrator of the report about loud laughter was said to be Maʿbad al-Juhanī, who spoke about predestination and was mentioned in the preceding notice. It was also said to be Maʿbad ibn Umm Maʿbad, past whom the Prophet ﷺ passed during the Hijrah. This is not sound, because the narrator of the laughter report was Juhanī while Umm Maʿbad's son was Khuzāʿī. I gave his notice in the first section. The error arose only from the shared personal name and the father's kunyah.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: النمري هكذا ذكره بن عبد البر وخالف ذلك في الكنى فسماه يحيى وهو الصواب الذي جزم به غيره كما سيأتي
records.english: al-Namarī. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr mentioned him in this form but contradicted it among the kunyahs, where he called him Yaḥyā. That is the correct form stated decisively by others, as will appear.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: روى عنه خالد بن معدان حديثا أورده أبو موسى في الذيل ففرق بن الأثير بينه وبين معد يكرب الهمداني الذي ذكره أبو أحمد العسكري فقال لا أدري أهما واحد أو اثنان قلت الراوي من الطريقين خالد بن معدان فهو دليل الاتحاد
records.english: Khālid ibn Maʿdān narrated a report from him that Abū Mūsā cited in the Supplement. Ibn al-Athīr distinguished him from Maʿdīkarib al-Hamdānī, whom Abū Aḥmad al-ʿAskarī mentioned, and said, ‘I do not know whether they are one or two.’ I say: The narrator in both routes is Khālid ibn Maʿdān, which is evidence that they are one.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ترجم له بن قانع فوهم لأنه صفة لا اسم قال حدثنا عبد الله بن أحمد حدثنا أبي حدثنا عبد الرحمن بن مهدي حدثنا همام عن قتادة عن الحسن عن عبد الله بن عثمان الثقفي عن رجل من ثقيف يقال له معروف وأثنى عليه خيرا قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الوليمة حق الحديث ثم رواه من طريق حجاج عن همام فقال فيه عن زهير بن عثمان الأعور قال بن قانع شك فيه قتادة كذا قال وقد أخرج الحديث عن بهز بن أحمد عن همام عن قتادة عن الحسن عن عبد الله بن عثمان عن رجل أعور من ثقيف قال قتادة وكان يقال له معروفا أي يثني عليه خيرا فقد فسر بهز مراد قتادة بقوله يقال له معروفا ويؤيده تسميته في رواية حجاج بن المنهال زهير بن عثمان وكذا سماه عبد الصمد بن عبد الوارث عن همام أخرجه أحمد أيضا وقال الدارمي في مسنده أنبأنا عفان حدثنا همام فذكره بلفظ أزال الإشكال من أصله فقال عن رجل من ثقيف أعور يقال له معروفا أي يثني عليه خيرا إن لم يكن اسمه زهير بن عثمان فلا أدري ما اسمه وكذا هو عند أبي داود والنسائي عن محمد بن المثنى عن عفان وتقدم في حرف الزاي في القسم الأول والله أعلم
records.english: Ibn Qāniʿ gave him an entry, but erred, for it is a description, not a name. He said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad related to us; my father related to us; ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī related to us; Hammām related to us, from Qatādah, from al-Ḥasan, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān al-Thaqafī, from a man of Thaqīf called Maʿrūf, of whom he spoke well, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said, ‘A wedding feast is a right...’—the report. He then narrated it by way of Ḥajjāj, from Hammām, where it reads ‘from Zuhayr ibn ʿUthmān al-Aʿwar.’ Ibn Qāniʿ said: Qatādah was uncertain about him. That is what he said. The report was also transmitted from Bahz ibn Aḥmad, from Hammām, from Qatādah, from al-Ḥasan, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān, from a one-eyed man of Thaqīf. Qatādah said, ‘He was called maʿrūf,’ meaning that he was spoken of favorably. Thus Bahz explained what Qatādah meant by ‘he was called maʿrūf.’ This is supported by his being named Zuhayr ibn ʿUthmān in the narration of Ḥajjāj ibn al-Minhāl. ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn ʿAbd al-Wārith likewise named him in his narration from Hammām, which Aḥmad also transmitted. Al-Dārimī said in his Musnad: ʿAffān informed us; Hammām related to us—and he cited it with wording that removed the confusion at its root: ‘from a one-eyed man of Thaqīf who was called maʿrūf,’ meaning that he was spoken of favorably; ‘if his name was not Zuhayr ibn ʿUthmān, I do not know his name.’ It appears the same way with Abū Dāwūd and al-Nasāʾī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā, from ʿAffān. He appeared previously under the letter zāy in the first section. والله أعلم.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكره بعضهم من أجل حديث أرسله رواه عمارة بن غزية وغيره عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال البخاري هو مرسل
records.english: Some mentioned him because of a report he transmitted as mursal. ʿUmārah ibn Ghaziyyah and others narrated it from him, from the Prophet ﷺ. Al-Bukhārī said: It is disconnected.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: والد أبي خزيمة ذكره بعضهم من أجل حديث أرسله أورده أبو موسى في الذيل ونقله عن تاريخ يعقوب بن سفيان وإنما هو يعمر أوله مثناة تحتانية وسيأتي في موضعه وتقدم ذكر الاختلاف فيه في الحارث بن سعد وفي سعد بن هذيم من هذا القسم
records.english: the father of Abū Khuzaymah. Some mentioned him because of a report he transmitted in disconnected form. Abū Mūsā cited him in the Supplement, quoting Yaʿqūb ibn Sufyān's Tārīkh. He is actually Yaʿmar, beginning with a yāʾ below, and will appear in his proper place. The disagreement concerning him was mentioned previously under al-Ḥārith ibn Saʿd and Saʿd ibn Hudhaym in this section.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: مر به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو كاشف فخذه وفرق أبو موسى تبعا لابن شاهين بينه وبين معمر بن عبد الله بن نضلة وهو واحد كما أوضحته في القسم الأول
records.english: The Prophet ﷺ passed by him while his thigh was uncovered. Abū Mūsā, following Ibn Shāhīn, distinguished him from Maʿmar ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Naḍlah, but they are one person, as I explained in the first section.

names.arabic: معمر بن عبد الله بن نضلة
names.english: Maʿmar ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Naḍlah

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكره بن شاهين في الصحابة وهو وهم فاخرج من طريق روح عن عبد العزيز بن أبي سلمة عن عبد الله بن عبد الرحمن عن معمر الأنصاري عن أنس قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من تعلم علما مما ينفع الله به في الآخرة لا يتعلمه إلا للدنيا حرم الله عليه أن يجد عرف الجنة قال أبو موسى أظنه عبد الله بن عبد الرحمن بن معمر فلعله تصحف قلت وهو كما ظن لأن هذا المتن معروف من رواية أبي طوالة واسمه عبد الله بن عبد الرحمن بن معمر رواه عن سعيد بن يسار عن أبي هريرة أخرجه أبو داود والنسائي من طريق فليح بن سليمان عنه وأخرجه الخطيب في كتاب اقتضاء العلم العمل من هذا فلعل عبد العزيز أرسله وتصحف بن معمر فصار عن معمر فنشأ اسم صحابي لا وجود له والله المستعان
records.english: Ibn Shāhīn mentioned him among the Companions, but this is an error. He transmitted by way of Rawḥ, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Abī Salamah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Maʿmar al-Anṣārī, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said, ‘Whoever learns knowledge of a kind through which God grants benefit in the Hereafter, learning it only for worldly gain, God will forbid him from finding the scent of Paradise.’ Abū Mūsā said: I think he is ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Maʿmar, and perhaps the text was corrupted. I say: It is as he thought. This wording is known from the narration of Abū Ṭuwālah, whose name was ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Maʿmar. He narrated it from Saʿīd ibn Yasār, from Abū Hurayrah. Abū Dāwūd and al-Nasāʾī transmitted it by way of Fulayḥ ibn Sulaymān, from him, and al-Khaṭīb transmitted it in Iqtiḍāʾ al-ʿIlm al-ʿAmal from this route. Perhaps ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz transmitted it in disconnected form and ‘ibn Maʿmar’ was corrupted into ‘from Maʿmar,’ thereby creating a Companion who never existed. والله المستعان.

names.arabic: عبد الله بن عبد الرحمن بن معمر
names.english: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Maʿmar

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بموحدة ومهملة وكان مصغر ذكره الذهبي في الميزان وتردد في ضبطه ولم يذكره في تجريد الصحابة وهو على شرطه فإنه ذكر من أنظاره جماعة ولفظه في الميزان معمر أو معمر بن بريك رأيت ورقة فيها أحاديث سئلت عن صحتها فأجبت ببطلانها وأنها كذب واضح وفيها أنبأنا أحمد بن إبراهيم السامي أنبأنا عبد الله بن إسحاق السنجاري أنبأنا عبد الله بن موسى السنجاري سمعت علي بن إسماعيل السنجاري يقول بسنجار في سنة سبع وعشرين وستمائة سمعت معمر بن بريك يقول سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول يشيب المرء ويشب منه خصلتان الحرص والأمل وبه أربعة يصلبون على شفير جهنم الجائر في حكمه وباغض آل محمد الحديث قال الشيباني وأنبأنا عبد المحمود المؤدب بسنجار أنبأنا الصدر عن عبد الوهاب سمعت علي بن إسماعيل السنجاري يقول سمعت معمر بن بريك يقول سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول من شم الورد ولم يصل علي فقد جفاني قال الذهبي فهذا من نمط رتن الهندي فقبح الله من يكذب
records.english: with a bāʾ and an undotted rāʾ, in the diminutive form. Al-Dhahabī mentioned him in al-Mīzān and hesitated over how to vocalize his name, but did not mention him in Tajrīd al-Ṣaḥābah, even though he met its criteria, for he mentioned a group of similar cases. His wording in al-Mīzān is: ‘Muʿammar—or Maʿmar—ibn Burayk. I saw a sheet containing reports about whose soundness I was asked. I answered that they were invalid and obvious lies. Among them was: Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Sāmī informed us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Isḥāq al-Sinjārī informed us; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mūsā al-Sinjārī informed us: I heard ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl al-Sinjārī say in Sinjār in the year 627: I heard Muʿammar ibn Burayk say: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say, “A person grows gray while two traits in him grow young: greed and hope.” Through the same chain: “Four will be crucified at the brink of Hell: one unjust in his judgment and one who hates the family of Muḥammad...”’—the report. Al-Shaybānī said: ‘ʿAbd al-Maḥmūd the tutor informed us in Sinjār; al-Ṣadr informed us, from ʿAbd al-Wahhāb: I heard ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl al-Sinjārī say: I heard Muʿammar ibn Burayk say: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say, “Whoever smells a rose and does not invoke blessings upon me has treated me coldly.”’ Al-Dhahabī said: ‘This is of the same kind as Ratan the Indian. فقبح الله من يكذب.’

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بضم أوله والتشديد شخص اختلق اسمه بعض الكذابين من المغاربة أخبرنا الكمال أبو البركات بن أبي يزيد المكناسي إجازة مكاتبة قال صافحني والدي وقد عاش مائة قال صافحني الشيخ أبو الحسن على الحطاب بالحاء المهملة بمدينة تونس وعاش مائة وثلاثين سنة قال صافحني الشيخ أبو عبد الله محمد الصقلي وعاش مائة وستين سنة قال صافحني أبو عبد الله معمر وكان عمره أربعمائة سنة قال صافحني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ودعا لي فقال عمرك الله يا معمر ثلاث مرات قلت وهذا من جنس رتن وقيس بن تميم وأبي الخطاب ومكلبة ونسطور وقد بسطت ترجمة المعمر بالتشديد في لسان الميزان فلم أر الإطالة بذكر هنا وقد وجدت للمعمر بالتشديد في لسان الميزان فلم أر الإطالة يذكر هنا وقد وجدت للمعمر خبرا آخر ذكرته في حرف العين في عمار وقصته تشبه قصة رتن الهندي وكان في زمانه ذكر أبو الحسن بن أبي نصر البجاني أنه رآه في بلدة تسمى قطنة من آخر بلاد الترك ووجدت له خبرا آخر ذكرته في حرف الجيم في جبير بن الحارث وأنه كان بعد الستمائة أيضا ورواه الناصر لدين الله العباسي وأنه كان في الصيد فاستجرهم الصيد في طلب الصيد حتى وقفوا على قرية زعم أهلها أنهم كلهم من ذرية المعمر أيضا وقد استوعبت تراجم هؤلاء في كتاب المعمرين وبالله التوفيق
records.english: with its first letter vocalized u and doubled. He was a person whose name was fabricated by one of the liars of the Maghreb. Al-Kamāl Abū al-Barakāt ibn Abī Yazīd al-Miknāsī informed us by written authorization, saying: My father, who lived one hundred years, shook my hand and said: Shaykh Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī al-Ḥaṭṭāb—with an unpointed ḥāʾ—in Tunis, who lived one hundred and thirty years, shook my hand and said: Shaykh Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad al-Ṣiqillī, who lived one hundred and sixty years, shook my hand and said: Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muʿammar, who was four hundred years old, shook my hand and said: The Messenger of God ﷺ shook my hand and invoked for me, saying عمرك الله يا معمر three times. I say: This is of the same kind as Ratan, Qays ibn Tamīm, Abū al-Khaṭṭāb, Maklabah, and Nasṭūr. I treated the notice on Muʿammar—with the doubled mīm—at length in Lisān al-Mīzān and therefore saw no need to lengthen the discussion here. The transition at this point is repeated in overlapping, tangled wording, and its exact duplicated syntax remains unresolved. I also found another report about Muʿammar, which I mentioned under the letter ʿayn in the notice on ʿAmmār. His story resembles that of Ratan the Indian, who lived in his time. Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Abī Naṣr al-Bajjānī mentioned that he saw him in a town called Qaṭnah, at the farthest reaches of the Turkic lands. I found yet another report about him, which I mentioned under the letter jīm in the notice on Jubayr ibn al-Ḥārith: he was also alive after the year 600. Al-Nāṣir li-Dīn Allāh the Abbasid narrated it: while hunting, they were drawn onward in pursuit of the game until they stopped at a village whose people claimed that all of them were also descendants of Muʿammar. I collected the notices on all these supposed long-lived men in Kitāb al-Muʿammarīn. وبالله التوفيق.

records.arabic: الخفاجي وخفاجة من عقيل له صحبة ذكره أبو نعيم وقد ذكرت ما قيل فيه في القسم الأول
records.english: al-Khafājī; Khafājah is of ʿUqayl. He had companionship. Abū Nuʿaym mentioned him, and I discussed what has been said concerning him in the first section.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكر أبو الحسن بن القصار المالكي أن عمر رفع إليه كتاب زوره عليه معن بن زائدة ونقش مثل خاتمه فجلده مائة ثم سجنه فشفع له قوم فقال ذكرتني الطعن وكنت ناسيا ثم جلده مائة أخرى ثم جلده مائة ثالثة وذلك بمحضر من العلماء ولم ينكر عليه أحد فكان ذلك إجماعا قلت الشأن في ثبوت ذلك فإن ثبت فيحتمل أن يكون فعل ذلك بطريق الاجتهاد فلم ينكره لأن مجتهدا لا يكون حجة على مجتهد فلا يلزم أن يكونوا قائلين بجواز ذلك فأين الإجماع هذا من حيث الحكم وأما إدراك معن العصر النبوي فواضح فلو ثبت لذكرته في القسم الثالث لكن معن بن زائدة لم يدرك ذلك الزمان وإنما كان في آخر دولة بني أمية وأول دولة بني العباس وولي إمرة اليمن وله أخبار شهيرة في الشجاعة والكرم ويحتمل أن يكون محفوظا ويكون ممن وافق اسم هذا واسم أبيه على بعد في ذلك
records.english: Abū al-Ḥasan ibn al-Qaṣṣār al-Mālikī mentioned that a letter forged against ʿUmar by Maʿn ibn Zāʾidah was brought before him. The forgery included an engraved copy of ʿUmar's seal. ʿUmar gave him one hundred lashes and then imprisoned him. Some people interceded for him, and ʿUmar said, ‘You have reminded me of stabbing when I had forgotten it.’ He then gave him another hundred lashes, and then a third hundred, in the presence of the scholars, none of whom objected; this therefore constituted consensus. I say: The issue is whether this account is established. If it is, the act may have been based on ʿUmar's independent legal judgment, and others did not object because one independent jurist is not an authority binding another. It does not follow that they held such punishment permissible. Where, then, is the consensus? That concerns the legal ruling. As for Maʿn's having lived in the prophetic era, it would be evident if the report were established, and I would have mentioned him in the third section. Maʿn ibn Zāʾidah, however, did not live in that period. He lived at the end of the Umayyad state and beginning of the Abbasid state, governed Yemen, and has famous accounts concerning courage and generosity. It is possible, though remote, that the report was preserved correctly and concerned another man whose name and father's name happened to agree with his.

records.arabic: اليمامي روى حديثه شاصويه بن عبيد عن معرض بن عبد الله بن معيقيب عن أبيه عن جده قال حججت حجة الوداع الحديث ذكره بن منده قال أبو نعيم هذا وهم وإنما هو معرض بن معيقيب يعني انقلب وقد مضى على الصواب
records.english: al-Yamāmī. Shāṣawayh ibn ʿUbayd narrated his report from Muʿarriḍ ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muʿayqīb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: I performed the Farewell Pilgrimage—the report. Ibn Mandah mentioned him. Abū Nuʿaym said: This is an error; he is actually Muʿarriḍ ibn Muʿayqīb, meaning that the names were reversed. He appeared previously in the correct form.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن هشام المخزومي ذكره أبو نعيم وقال مختلف في صحبته ذكره الحضرمي يعني محمد بن عبد الله المعروف بمطين في الوحدان وأخرج عن هارون بن إسحاق عن قدامة بن محمد عن مغيرة بن المغيرة بن الحارث بن هشام عن أبيه عن جده قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يكفي المؤمن المواقعة في الشهر قلت سقط بين المغيرة والحارث عبد الرحمن كذلك ذكره البخاري في تاريخه في ترجمة حفيده فقال مغيرة بن يحيى بن مغيرة بن عبد الرحمن بن الحارث روى قدامة بن محمد المدني عنه عن أبيه عن جده مرسلا قلت وعبد الرحمن بن الحارث له رؤية وهو والد أبي بكر أحد فقهاء المدينة والمغيرة هذا هو اخوه وكان مولده في خلافة معاوية ولم يدرك العصر النبوي قطعا
records.english: ibn Hishām al-Makhzūmī. Abū Nuʿaym mentioned him and said that there was disagreement over his companionship. Al-Ḥaḍramī—meaning Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh, known as Muṭayyan—mentioned him among the solitary narrators and transmitted from Hārūn ibn Isḥāq, from Qudāmah ibn Muḥammad, from Mughīrah ibn al-Mughīrah ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said, ‘Intercourse once a month is sufficient for the believer.’ I say: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān fell out between al-Mughīrah and al-Ḥārith. Al-Bukhārī gave it that way in his Tārīkh in the notice on his grandson, saying: Mughīrah ibn Yaḥyā ibn Mughīrah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith; Qudāmah ibn Muḥammad al-Madanī narrated from him, from his father, from his grandfather, in disconnected form. I say: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith saw the Prophet and was the father of Abū Bakr, one of the jurists of Medina. This Mughīrah was Abū Bakr's brother. He was born during Muʿāwiyah's caliphate and certainly did not live in the prophetic era.

names.arabic: المغيرة بن الحارث بن هشام المخزومي
names.english: al-Mughīrah ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām al-Makhzūmī

names.arabic: مغيرة بن المغيرة بن الحارث بن هشام
names.english: Mughīrah ibn al-Mughīrah ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الخزاعي تابعي أرسل حديثا فذكره بن شاهين في الصحابة وأخرج من طريق حميد الطويل عنه أن رجلين اختصما في شيء إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال هل لكما في الشطر وأومأ بيده رواه البغوي بسند صحيح إلى حميد وقد ذكر بن أبي حاتم المغيرة المذكور في التابعين وقال روى عن بن عمر وكذا ذكره بن حبان في الثقات وروايته عن بن عمر عند النسائي
records.english: al-Khuzāʿī, a Successor. He transmitted a report in disconnected form, so Ibn Shāhīn mentioned him among the Companions and transmitted by way of Ḥumayd al-Ṭawīl, from him, that two men disputed over something before the Messenger of God ﷺ, who said, ‘Will you accept half?’ and gestured with his hand. Al-Baghawī narrated it with a sound chain as far as Ḥumayd. Ibn Abī Ḥātim mentioned this Mughīrah among the Successors and said that he narrated from Ibn ʿUmar. Ibn Ḥibbān likewise mentioned him in al-Thiqāt, and his narration from Ibn ʿUmar is found in al-Nasāʾī.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: أو فلان بن المغيرة المخزومي من بني مخزوم أخرج بن سعد في الطبقات عن أبي نعيم عن سعيد بن يزيد الأحمسي عن الشعبي حدثتني فاطمة بنت قيس أنها كانت تحت المغيرة بن فلان أو فلان بن المغيرة من بني مخزوم فذكر الحديث قلت وكأن راويه لم يحفظ اسمه فنسبه إلى جده الأعلى وتردد مع ذلك فقلبه فقال المغيرة بن فلان وكلاهما خطأ وإنما هو أبو عمرو بن حفص بن المغيرة بن عبد الله بن عمر بن مخزوم وقيل هو أبو حفص بن عمرو بن عمرو بن المغيرة وسيأتي في الكنى
records.english: or So-and-so ibn al-Mughīrah al-Makhzūmī, of Banū Makhzūm. Ibn Saʿd transmitted in al-Ṭabaqāt from Abū Nuʿaym, from Saʿīd ibn Yazīd al-Aḥmasī, from al-Shaʿbī: Fāṭimah bint Qays related to me that she had been married to al-Mughīrah ibn So-and-so—or So-and-so ibn al-Mughīrah—of Banū Makhzūm, and he related the report. I say: It appears that the narrator did not remember his name, so he ascribed him to his more remote ancestor and, while uncertain, reversed it as al-Mughīrah ibn So-and-so. Both forms are wrong. He is actually Abū ʿAmr ibn Ḥafṣ ibn al-Mughīrah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn Makhzūm. It is also said that he was Abū Ḥafṣ ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Mughīrah. He will appear among the kunyahs.

names.arabic: أبو عمرو بن حفص بن المغيرة بن عبد الله بن عمر بن مخزوم
names.english: Abū ʿAmr ibn Ḥafṣ ibn al-Mughīrah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn Makhzūm

names.arabic: أبو حفص بن عمرو بن عمرو بن المغيرة
names.english: Abū Ḥafṣ ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Mughīrah

records.arabic: بمثناة ثم موحدة بن النحاس بنون ومهملة تابعي أرسل حديثا فذكره بن فتحون في ذيل الاستيعاب ونقل عن محمد بن عثمان بن أبي شيبة عن يعلى بن يحيى المحاربي عن أبيه عن المغيرة بن عتبة قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على حمار وعلي رديفه فقال قل اللهم اغفر لي وارحمني اللهم تب علي لعلك تصيبك إحداهن قال بن فتحون وذكر سيف في الفتوح أن خالد بن الوليد استعمل عتبة والد المغيرة هذا فيمن استعمل من كماة الصحابة على اللهازم من بكر بن وائل يعني فإذا كان أبو من الصحابة جاز أن يكون هو كذلك وهو كما قال لكن الواقع خلاف ذلك فإنه مذكور في طبقة صغار التابعين ممن روى عن كبار التابعين كموسى بن طلحة وكناه بذلك بن أبي حاتم وغيره
records.english: with tāʾ and then bāʾ; ibn al-Naḥḥās, with nūn and an undotted letter. He was a Successor. He transmitted a report in disconnected form, so Ibn Fatḥūn mentioned him in the Supplement to al-Istīʿāb and quoted Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shaybah, from Yaʿlā ibn Yaḥyā al-Muḥāribī, from his father, from al-Mughīrah ibn ʿUtbah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ was on a donkey with ʿAlī riding behind him. He said, ‘Say: اللهم اغفر لي وارحمني; اللهم تب علي.’ The clause that follows these supplications is damaged, so its force remains unresolved. Ibn Fatḥūn said: Sayf mentioned in al-Futūḥ that Khālid ibn al-Walīd appointed ʿUtbah, the father of this Mughīrah, as one of the brave Companions whom he appointed over al-Lahāzim of Bakr ibn Wāʾil. The ensuing clause is damaged at the word abū; it appears to reason from a father's companionship to the possibility of the son's, but the missing relation remains unresolved. The reality, however, is otherwise: al-Mughīrah is listed in the generation of the younger Successors who narrated from senior Successors such as Mūsā ibn Ṭalḥah. The closing statement says that Ibn Abī Ḥātim and others gave him ‘that kunyah,’ but no antecedent kunyah is visible, so the claim remains unresolved.

records.arabic: تقدم في القسم الثالث
records.english: He appeared earlier in the third section.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: التغلبي أورده بن قانع وقال حدثنا بشر بن موسى حدثنا سعيد بن منصور حدثنا عبد العزيز بن محمد عن عمرو بن يحيى عن أبي زائدة مولى التغلبيين عن مفضل بن أبي الهيثم حليف لهم قد أدرك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال نهى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يستقبل القبلة بغائط وبول قال بن قانع كذا قال بشر وهو عندي خطأ والصواب معقل وهو كما قال
records.english: al-Taghlibī. Ibn Qāniʿ cited him and said: Bishr ibn Mūsā related to us; Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr related to us; ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muḥammad related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Yaḥyā, from Abū Zāʾidah, client of the Taghlibīs, from Mufaḍḍal ibn Abī al-Haytham, an ally of theirs who had lived into the time of the Prophet ﷺ. He said: The Prophet ﷺ prohibited facing the prayer direction while defecating or urinating. Ibn Qāniʿ said: That is how Bishr gave it, but in my view it is an error; the correct name is Maʿqil. It is as he said.
